meta.name: Starfall
meta.subtitle: Second city of the Noctari, seat of the Academy of Astral Harmony
meta.era: Part One — The Architect, c. 1450 AO (Age of Order, the city alive)
meta.culture: Noctari (night elf); Umbrion-aligned; scholars of the heavens
meta.coordinate_system: polar around the caldera centre (0,0). r = metres from centre; a_deg = degrees where 0 = +Z (front / the Grand Processional & causeway), increasing toward +X. world x = r*sin(a), z = r*cos(a). y = terrace top height (metres). Screen/plate angle = 180 - a_deg.
meta.status: FOUNDATION + two wedges fully specified (House Vael'Suran H0, House Serenthil H8 — the pair flanking the Grand Processional). Seven Houses + the Academy island still stubbed. Geometry LOCKED to godot/threed/StarfallCity3D.gd & docs/Scale_Reference.md.
meta.theme: Two maps of one city. The Plate (this visible survey) and the Ledger-map beneath it (the Under-Terraces) do not contain each other. That omission is the story of Part One.

grid.kind: metric survey grid overlaid on the radial city
grid.note: The city is radial (concentric caldera). The grid is a coordinate reference for placement, not a street grid — Starfall has no Cartesian blocks.

geometry_locked.note: Under-Terraces occupy negative Y beneath the shore/canal rings — the service city the Plate omits (barge locks, conduit galleries, bunk-halls). Depths -8 to -30.

districts.name: The Rim & the Nine Towers
districts.desc: The rim walk crowned by the nine House observatory towers (one dead). Each House seats itself here, highest and coldest, above its own wedge.

districts.name: The Upper Terraces
districts.desc: Sparse villas of senior astronomers, each with a surveyed, legally-protected sightline down to the Mirror (the 'ray-lines' of the Plate). To lose your sightline is to lose your rank.

districts.name: The Middle Terraces
districts.desc: Lecture annexes, scribe-halls, chart-makers and lens-guilds, and the dwellings of lesser scholars who serve the Houses without a sightline of their own.

districts.name: The Canal Quarter
districts.desc: The dense, warm, lowest visible ring: three star-water canals, footbridges, instrument-workshops, market rows, inns, a shrine. Where the city actually lives.

districts.name: The Shore & Processionals
districts.desc: Black basalt strand where the four processionals meet the star-lake; the armillary monument; customs posts where goods arrive from below.

districts.name: The Mirror & Causeway
districts.desc: The star-lake — a hole showing sky — crossed by the single railless causeway to the Academy island.

districts.name: The Academy of Astral Harmony (island)
districts.desc: Dead centre: the great observatory, theory wings, moon-bridge, the warded containment structure. Elorin, Corel, Coil, Sera and the Nullstone team work here.

districts.name: The Under-Terraces
districts.desc: THE OMITTED CITY. Beneath the canal quarter and shore: barge locks that raise cargo from the world below, conduit galleries carrying the Song to the star-lamps, bunk-halls of Terran deep-wrights and orc labour, the canteens and foremen. Not on the Plate. Not by conspiracy — the cartographers simply never considered it part of the city.

houses.name: House Vael'Suran
houses.domain: The unmoving stars; the master survey from which every sightline in Starfall is measured. The eldest and proudest House; its charts are the city's ground truth.
houses.sigil: a silver gnomon crossed by a single fixed star, on indigo
houses.colours: silver-white on deep indigo; a thread of antique gold

houses.name: House Nyx'Talar
houses.domain: Eclipses, transits, and every moment one light passes behind another. Readers of what hides what.
houses.sigil: a black disc crossing a silver ring

houses.name: House Oravelle
houses.domain: The wandering lights (planets); ephemerides and prediction. The House the Conclave trusts with dates.
houses.sigil: five linked circlets in a curve

houses.name: House Sabreth
houses.domain: Comets and omens; the House everyone consults and no one admits to consulting. Faintly disreputable, quietly wealthy.
houses.sigil: a silver star trailing a fine comet-tail of gold

houses.name: House Ilmyra
houses.epithet: Keepers of the Tides of the Song
houses.domain: The moons and the slow tides the Song makes in all things; the House that tends the city's water-clocks and the canal locks' timing.
houses.note: Its wedge holds the Grand Processional's far (-Z/back) counterpart is NOT here; the front processional falls in the Vael'Suran/Serenthil gap.

houses.name: House Corvane
houses.domain: The dark between the stars — the void itself. The most Umbrion-aligned House; feared a little, and the one whose theory feeds the Academy's void-work. Elorin's intellectual kin, though not her blood.
houses.sigil: an empty silver ring around unmarked indigo

houses.name: House ————
houses.domain: Unknown / struck from the record. Its dome is dark, its sigil scraped from the ring, its name unsaid. No one has ever proposed relighting it; some absences are load-bearing.
houses.sigil: none — a dome struck through with one black shard
houses.note: The dead House of the greybox (DEAD_TOWER index). Its wedge is the city's quiet scar — under-tended terraces, cheaper rents, the district people move to when they wish not to be measured.

houses.name: House Duskmere
houses.domain: The twilight band, risings and settings, the last and first light. The House of thresholds and departures; keeps the outer switchback stair and the rim gates.
houses.sigil: a silver line of horizon under a half-sunk star

houses.name: House Serenthil
houses.domain: The meridian and the hour; timekeepers of Starfall. They ring the bells, including the ninth-bell count of every Luminarae — and the same bells that toll the festival toll the labour-shifts in the dark below. The House the whole city depends on and none reveres: a utility, not a glory. Flanks the Grand Processional opposite Vael'Suran.
houses.sigil: a vertical silver meridian line through a single gold point
houses.colours: silver on indigo; one gold point at the meridian; verdigris on the bells

structures.name: The Great Observatory

position.note: dead centre of the island — the greybox's ~110 m hero dome (green verdigris, lit spire)

structures.purpose: The single silhouette that rules the whole caldera: a verdigris-domed drum rising 110 m from the island, its lit spire visible from every terrace and every wedge. Under the dome the Academy reads a sky no single House owns — the shared instrument the nine Houses grudgingly answer to. It is the reason Starfall exists where it does, over the hole in the world that shows the stars.

rooms.name: The Great Hall
rooms.purpose: the floor beneath the dome; the aperture opens the ceiling to the true sky; the balcony ring girdles the drum outside (the Cold Open balcony is one such ledge, at scale)

rooms.name: The Meridian Circle
rooms.purpose: the Academy's master transit instrument — the line the Houses' clocks and charts are all quietly corrected against

rooms.name: The Orrery Room
rooms.purpose: a great brass model of the wandering lights, kept running; Oravelle envies it

rooms.name: The Archmagister's Study
rooms.purpose: the head of the Academy's rooms, highest habitable floor, the finest sightline in Starfall

rooms.name: Observers' cells
rooms.purpose: spare rooms for the astronomers who keep the night watches

structures.notes: Archmagister + First Astronomer + 12 live-in observers/watch-keepers. The lit apex is the greybox spire finial.

structures.name: The Theory Wings & Moon-Bridge

position.note: the ±X wings of the greybox island, joined by the arched moon-bridge

footprint.form: two 3-storey wings joined by a bridge

structures.purpose: Two galleried library-halls of receding star-crystal stacks, joined at second-storey height by the arched moon-bridge that gives the island its silhouette. Where the Academy THINKS: lectures, glyph-boards, the reading of everything the nine Houses have ever measured. The Nullstone team first assembles here — the arguments that end in a void artifact begin as chalk on these boards.

rooms.name: The West Gallery
rooms.purpose: two storeys of stacks; a mezzanine walk at 3.6 m; ~6 lecterns/glyph-boards on the floor

rooms.name: The East Gallery
rooms.purpose: the reading hall; long tables under high comb-crystal windows

rooms.name: Study alcoves (x3)
rooms.purpose: where Coil argues thresholds and Vara out-thinks the room she is not credited in

rooms.name: The Moon-Bridge
rooms.purpose: the arched span between the wing-tops; the Academy's favourite place to be seen thinking

structures.notes: Senior lector Vessine + 5 resident theorists. Coil (CH-009), Vara (CH-010), Sera (CH-008) and Durak (CH-011) WORK here daily but lodge elsewhere (city). SQ-P1-03 seed.

structures.name: The Containment Halls

position.note: the back (-Z) warded structure of the greybox island; gold ward-glyph floor

structures.purpose: The heaviest, coldest building on the island: an industrial-arcane hall around a recessed containment rig-pit, glyph-warded floor to ceiling. THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT ROOM IN PART ONE is the drafting dais at its end — the SAFEGUARD DESIGN happens at that table, and the buried flaw is authored there, at this drafting table, by Elorin's own hand. What is meant here as 'containment' drifts, across the act, into 'control.'

rooms.name: The Rig-Pit Hall
rooms.purpose: central containment rig-pit (8 m ⌀, recessed 1.5 m) where prototype tests run; cold arcane-blue glow

rooms.name: The Schematic Dais
rooms.purpose: raised drafting dais; the 3×1.5 m table where the safeguard — and its buried flaw — is drawn (PR-010)

rooms.name: The Ward-Store
rooms.purpose: warded materials, glyph-stock, the prototype's cradle

rooms.name: Corel's office
rooms.purpose: the exhausted archmagister's room — decency worn thin by duty

structures.notes: Corel (CH-013) keeps an office and often sleeps here (4 counted incl. 3 night-wards). Act II core; SQ-P1-06 (The Buried Flaw). The prototype (PR-001) sits above the rig-pit in Act II.

structures.name: The Scholars' Residence
structures.purpose: The quiet ring of cells and studies where the Academy's resident fellows live — including Elorin Voidweaver, through the years she builds the thing that ends the world. Her rooms are spare, Noctari-dark, over-open in the Umbraveil way (a door she will not shut), and stacked with the void-theory House Corvane first taught her. The most consequential bedroom in the history of the Song, and nobody on the island knows it yet.

rooms.name: Elorin's rooms
rooms.purpose: study + cell; the void kept as 'presence, not absence'; a low window on the Mirror

rooms.name: Fellows' cells (x8)
rooms.purpose: resident theorists and senior scholars

rooms.name: The Common Study
rooms.purpose: shared fire, shared silence

structures.notes: Elorin (CH-001/002) + 11 resident fellows. Her home for the Academy years (Narrative Outline Ch2-5). Coil may lodge here too when not at the Wings.

structures.name: The Refectory & Commons
structures.purpose: The one warm, loud room on a cold island — where archmagisters, students, and the Solari and human and Terran scholars the Houses keep at arm's length all eat at the same long tables. The Academy's small daily proof that the city's careful separations are a choice, not a law.

rooms.name: The Long Hall
rooms.purpose: trestle tables, a great hearth, a board of the night's observing assignments

rooms.name: Kitchens & stores
rooms.purpose: run by the refectory staff

structures.notes: Refectory-master Ondle + 8 kitchen/commons staff (boarded).

structures.name: The Students' Dormitory
structures.purpose: Where the Academy's students board — the sharpest young minds the nine Houses (and, rarely, the city below, and, once in a generation, somewhere outside it entirely) can send. Crowded, cold, ferociously competitive, and the only place a House heir and a canal-quarter prodigy share a wall. The NA-02 crowd of the exterior scenes lives here.

rooms.name: Sleeping ranges (x3 floors)
rooms.purpose: shared student cells, 2-4 to a room

rooms.name: The Study Hall
rooms.purpose: a night-lit common study; the competition never sleeps

rooms.name: Proctors' rooms
rooms.purpose: the resident proctors who keep order

structures.notes: ~84 students + 4 proctors. The island's largest population; the Academy's future, most of whom will never own a sightline.

structures.name: The Gate Plaza & Fountain

position.note: the +Z gate plaza where the causeway meets the island; the greybox Gate Fountain

structures.purpose: Where the one causeway lands: a 12×12 m marble gate-plaza with the star-water Gate Fountain students trail a hand in for luck on the way to their examinations. The island's only door to the rest of the city, and — like the customs posts on the shore — it faces the water, not the dark below.

rooms.name: The Gatehouse
rooms.purpose: the porter's lodge and the notice board (PR-016); the island's register of who is on it

rooms.name: The Plaza & Fountain
rooms.purpose: open marble; the Gate Fountain that gives nothing back but a doubled sky

structures.notes: Gate-porter Sull + 2 (night-porters). The moon-bridge, notice board, fountain and students are the §10 island interactables.

structures.name: The Warders' Post
structures.purpose: A small hard post beside the Containment Halls: the ward-keepers who guard the prototype and the drafting dais, the nearest thing the scholarly island has to soldiers. In Part One they are almost bored. Three hundred years later, guarding the finished Stone in a different vault, their successors (the Void Wardens, CH-017) will not be.

rooms.name: The Guard-Room
rooms.purpose: the ward-keepers' watch; a rack of ward-staves

rooms.name: Bunk
rooms.purpose: the on-island wards sleep at their post

structures.notes: 6 ward-keepers. A quiet foreshadow of the Void Wardens who guard the Nullstone Vault in both parts.

structures.name: The Gnomon Tower

position.note: the Vael'Suran rim observatory — greybox tower i=0

structures.purpose: The master survey of the fixed stars is kept and corrected here; every protected sightline in Starfall is a copy of a line first drawn in this tower. The House's authority is literally the instrument on its top floor.

rooms.name: The Meridian Hall
rooms.purpose: ground instrument hall; the great mural quadrant fixed to the north wall

rooms.name: The Chart Vault
rooms.purpose: fireproof silver-lined vault of the master plates; only the House head and First Surveyor hold keys

rooms.name: Head's Study
rooms.purpose: Magister Ysolde's study, sightline due to the Mirror

rooms.name: Computers' Room
rooms.purpose: where junior scholars reduce the night's readings by hand; ink, tables, and quiet

rooms.name: The Gnomon Chamber
rooms.purpose: top floor; the great gnomon and the roof aperture; the reading is taken standing in the cold

rooms.name: Servants' stair & lamp-room
rooms.purpose: the spiral stair; the star-lamp that crowns the dome is tended from here

structures.notes: 3 named + 4 live-in junior computers (dormitory on the 4th floor). The dome's lit finial is one of the nine on the greybox rim.

structures.name: The Vael'Suran Seat
structures.purpose: The living seat of the House on the rim beside its tower — cold, immaculate, and arranged so that every principal room holds the same framed view of the star-lake. Status here is measured in windows.

rooms.name: The Hall of Sightlines
rooms.purpose: reception; nine framed sightline-drawings, one per generation of heads

rooms.name: Ysolde's chambers
rooms.purpose: the matriarch's rooms, the best sightline in the House

rooms.name: Family wing
rooms.purpose: four chambers for the near family

rooms.name: Cold-court
rooms.purpose: an open inner court left deliberately unroofed to the sky — the House takes readings without leaving home

rooms.name: Kitchen & stores
rooms.purpose: below the hall

rooms.name: Staff quarters
rooms.purpose: attic rooms for the household staff

structures.notes: Ysolde + near family (5) + 13 household staff (cook, chart-porters, lamp-tender, a gate-lodge keeper, maids). Ysolde also keeps a study in the tower.

structures.name: The Corrected Chart (the Open House)

position.note: the enterable interior already built in godot/threed/StarfallCity3D.gd (_build_open_house)

structures.purpose: Home and working room of Sub-Magister Aeliston Vael'Suran, a cousin of the House who keeps the running correction of the caldera's own sky from this terrace. A lifetime's chart is pinned to the lectern, corrected in a fine hand.

rooms.name: The Reading Room
rooms.purpose: one open room; the star-chart lectern against the back wall, a cot, a stove, a cold-shelf of instruments

structures.notes: Ties the built Open House interior into canon. Aeliston lives alone by choice; the whole House thinks him eccentric for keeping his own hours and his own door.

structures.name: Sightline Villa — Halvenor
structures.purpose: The household of First Surveyor Halvenor Daskei, the House's most important commoner-born scholar — the man who actually runs the survey Ysolde signs.

rooms.name: Ground hall & study
rooms.purpose: study with the protected sightline; a second-best mural quadrant

rooms.name: Family rooms (x3)
rooms.purpose: Halvenor, his wife, three children

rooms.name: Roof platform
rooms.purpose: a private observing platform — the perquisite of his post

structures.notes: Halvenor (First Surveyor), spouse Renne, 3 children, 1 live-in aunt.

structures.name: Sightline Villa — Corvane-in-marriage
structures.purpose: A Vael'Suran daughter married into House Corvane (the Deep Field) and kept her sightline; the villa quietly does void-adjacent work the fixed-star House disowns in public and funds in private.

rooms.name: Study of the Dark
rooms.purpose: shuttered by day; the sightline used at new-moon only

rooms.name: Living rooms
rooms.purpose: the couple + 2 children

rooms.name: Servant's room
rooms.purpose: one maid

structures.notes: Magistra Ivrenne (née Vael'Suran) + husband + 2 children + 1 maid. A thread that connects wedge 0 to House Corvane (H5).

structures.name: Sightline Villa — the Widow Sarrent
structures.purpose: A villa whose sightline is being slowly, legally encroached by a neighbour's new roofline — the great terror of the upper terrace. The widowed astronomer Sarrent is fighting it in the House court and losing.

rooms.name: Contested study
rooms.purpose: the sightline here is 4 degrees narrower than it was a decade ago

rooms.name: Rooms
rooms.purpose: Sarrent + a companion

structures.notes: Sarrent + companion Ol + one servant. A ready side-quest seed (the sightline suit).

structures.name: The Scribes' Hall of the Fixed Stars
structures.purpose: Where the House's charts are fair-copied and bound, and where the apprentice scribes lodge. A young Noctari apprentice named Talindir keeps a cot and a candle here — he is eighty, which for an elf is a boy, and he copies faster and more beautifully than anyone will admit.

rooms.name: The Copying Floor
rooms.purpose: ranked sloped desks under high comb-crystal windows

rooms.name: The Binding Room
rooms.purpose: presses, thread, silver leaf

rooms.name: Apprentices' dormitory
rooms.purpose: 12 cots; Talindir's is by the window

rooms.name: Master-scribe's room
rooms.purpose: the hall's warden

structures.notes: Master-scribe Ovinn + 13 apprentices incl. Talindir (CH-006, here as an apprentice ~1450 AO — 550 years before the Cold Open). Canonical anchor.

structures.name: The Lens-Grinders' Court
structures.purpose: Optical glass for the whole wedge is ground and figured here — the slow, wet, patient trade that makes the Houses' instruments possible and gets none of the credit. A family firm, three generations deep.

rooms.name: The Grinding Shed
rooms.purpose: pitch laps, abrasive tubs, the great figuring wheel

rooms.name: The Testing Room
rooms.purpose: a dark room with a slit; lenses proved against a star-lamp

rooms.name: Family dwelling
rooms.purpose: the Marn family above the shed

rooms.name: The Court
rooms.purpose: open drying/working court

structures.notes: Master optician Delu Marn + spouse + 4 children + 3 journeymen (lodged).

structures.name: Lesser Scholars' Row
structures.purpose: Six joined narrow houses of the wedge's lesser scholars — the reducers, correctors, and lecture-assistants who serve the Houses without a sightline of their own. Respectable, cramped, sightless.

rooms.name: Per-house: ground room + 2 up
rooms.purpose: each of the 6 houses: a work-room and two small chambers

structures.notes: 6 households, ~22 souls total (the reducer Kessa Von and family named; the rest counted). No protected sightline — a social border made of geometry.

structures.name: The Sounding-Glass
structures.purpose: The wedge's inn, on the canal — warm, low-ceilinged, loud, and the one place a sightless scholar, an off-shift deep-wright, and a slumming House son drink in the same room. In game terms, the Strain-relief haven for this quarter (Zone_Atlas Z-06).

rooms.name: The Common Room
rooms.purpose: hearth, long tables, the cracked sounding-glass over the bar that gives the place its name

rooms.name: Letting rooms (x5)
rooms.purpose: five rooms above for travellers and the newly-evicted

rooms.name: Cellar
rooms.purpose: canal-cooled store; a hatch to the Under-Terraces the innkeeper pretends not to know about

structures.notes: Innkeeper Bruin Hale + 2 family + 2 staff. The cellar hatch is a real connection to VS-X05 (a thing the Plate does not know).

structures.name: The Instrument Market
structures.purpose: Ten stalls and shopfronts: brass-founders, tube-makers, engravers of scales, a dealer in second-hand quadrants, a paper-and-ink merchant. Live-over-the-shop trade.

rooms.name: Per unit: shopfront + workshop + room above
rooms.purpose: 10 units, most with a family living above

structures.notes: 10 shops, ~34 souls. Named: brass-founder Ossa Kellen (whose foundry vents to an Under-Terrace flue), engraver the elder Pim.

structures.name: The Deepening
structures.purpose: A small windowless shrine to Umbrion, Weaver of Shadow — dark on purpose, entered to sit in the friendly void the Noctari call presence, not absence. A keeper tends one silver lamp that is never lit.

rooms.name: The Dark Cell
rooms.purpose: no light; a bowl of still star-water; you find the seat by touch

rooms.name: Keeper's cell
rooms.purpose: the shrine-keeper's room

structures.notes: The keeper, blind Serae — chosen for the post because the dark costs her nothing. A quiet counterpoint to the Solari sun-worship of the Cold Open.

structures.name: Vara's Garret
structures.purpose: A single rented attic room where Vara — the human prodigy the Academy uses and under-credits — lives. Books to the ceiling, a borrowed quadrant she is not supposed to have, and the longest walk to the island of anyone on the team, because a human is not given rooms on the rim.

rooms.name: The Garret
rooms.purpose: bed, desk, and more paper than floor; a skylight she uses as a poor man's aperture

structures.notes: Vara (CH-010, PO-008) — canonical Nullstone-team anchor placed in wedge 0. 'Twice as good, half as credited' is literally spatial here: she has the worst room and the best mind in the wedge.

structures.name: Canal Dwellings — Lockside
structures.purpose: The densest housing on the visible city: eight dwellings stacked three storeys over the canal, home to the artisans, boatwrights, lamplighters and canal-workers who keep the quarter running.

rooms.name: Per dwelling: 2-3 rooms
rooms.purpose: 8 dwellings, families of 3-6

structures.notes: ~38 souls. Named: lamplighter Corrun, who climbs the whole wedge every dusk, and knows a stair down that isn't drawn.

structures.name: The Vael'Suran Canal & its two bridges

position.note: one of the greybox's three canals, threading the wedge's canal quarter

footprint.form: curved channel, base_a ~0.35 rad in greybox

structures.purpose: Star-water — black, still, faintly starred — runs the canal that both drains the quarter and, through the lock below, connects to the barges of the Under-Terraces. Two arched stone footbridges cross it.
structures.notes: The canal is the visible top of an invisible system: what looks like a decorative channel is the throat of the cargo route the Plate omits (see VS-X01, the lock).

structures.name: The Processional Foot & Customs Post
structures.purpose: Where the Grand Processional meets the shore on the wedge's side: a customs post that weighs and tallies everything coming up from below before it is allowed onto the terraces. The one official door between the two cities — and it faces up, never down.

rooms.name: The Weighing Hall
rooms.purpose: scales, tally-desks, a wardsealed strongroom

rooms.name: Officers' room
rooms.purpose: the customs officer and two clerks

structures.notes: Customs officer Trell + 2 clerks (day post, not resident overnight — counted at their canal homes; listed here as workplace).

structures.name: Cael's Lock

position.depth_note: beneath the canal quarter

structures.purpose: A stone chamber-lock that raises cargo barges from the world below the caldera up into the wedge's canal. The whole visible quarter's stone, glass, food and fuel arrives through here, lifted by chain-gangs. The Plate draws the pretty canal above it and stops.

rooms.name: The Lock Chamber
rooms.purpose: the flooding/emptying basin; the great counter-weighted gates

rooms.name: The Capstan Floor
rooms.purpose: where the lift-gangs walk the capstans; named for a worker who died at them

rooms.name: Tally hole
rooms.purpose: the under-clerk's niche

structures.notes: Worked, not lived-in. Named: lock-master Dregg. The under-clerk here keeps the OTHER tally — the real one, on ledger-paper, in charcoal.

structures.name: The Conduit Gallery

position.depth_note: runs radially under the terraces

structures.purpose: The Song does not fill the wedge's star-lamps by magic that tends itself. It is carried up this gallery in tuned crystal conduits that must be kept clean, aligned, and singing — hand-work, done in the dark, by people the light above never sees. When a lamp on the terrace 'simply burns,' someone down here made it.

rooms.name: The Long Gallery
rooms.purpose: the conduit run; access ladders up to each terrace's lamp-stems

rooms.name: Tuning niches (x4)
rooms.purpose: where conduit-wrights kneel to true the crystal

structures.notes: Worked by conduit-wrights (mostly Terran). Thematically the literal machinery behind the Cold Open's 'the star-lamps burn without flame because the Song fills them.'

structures.name: The Deep-Wrights' Hall

position.depth_note: cut into the shore-mass

structures.purpose: Home and hall of the Terran stone-wrights who cut and maintain the Under-Terraces — the deep folk who literally hold the beautiful city up. Carved, warm with glow-stone, and prouder than anything on the rim. Durak Ironthought, the geomancer the Academy consults and the Houses condescend to, lodges here among his own kind when he is in Starfall.

rooms.name: The Carved Hall
rooms.purpose: a communal hall; a long stone table; the deep-folk do not build separate boxes to eat in

rooms.name: Sleeping galleries
rooms.purpose: bunk-niches for ~40 wrights

rooms.name: Durak's cell
rooms.purpose: a plain stone room; a geomancer's tuning-forks and a basin of still water

rooms.name: The Shrine of Petrocore
rooms.purpose: a Stone-Voice shrine — the wrong god for this city, kept anyway

structures.notes: Durak Ironthought (CH-011, PO-009) + ~43 Terran deep-wrights. Canonical anchor; explains why Durak argues 'we would build a basin' — he lives with the people who build.

structures.name: The Lift-Gang Bunks

position.depth_note: beside the lock

structures.purpose: The bunk-hall of the orc lift-gangs who walk the lock capstans and carry what the barges bring. This is where the young Elorin, come down on some errand of theory, first SEES the labour the Academy is built on — the beat the Narrative Outline gives Ch2. Cruelty here is not spectacle; it is routine, and the routine is the point.

rooms.name: Bunk rows
rooms.purpose: riveted double-bunks for ~30; no window, because there is no outside to have one onto

rooms.name: The Collar-room
rooms.purpose: where shift-tallies are logged; a quiet, bureaucratic horror

structures.notes: ~30 orc labourers. Named: the elder Ghesh, who counts. Foreshadows Part Two's Ashpile without stating it. Part of the unnamed 778 the whole game is about.

structures.name: The Underspill Canteen

position.depth_note: at the junction of the galleries

structures.purpose: The one warm shared room of the Under-Terraces: a canteen at the crossing of the galleries where deep-wrights, lift-gangs, conduit-crews and the occasional lost scholar eat the same grey, good stew. The real social heart of the wedge — the thing the Plate has no symbol for.

rooms.name: The Long Room
rooms.purpose: trestle tables, a great range, a wall where the dead are chalked

rooms.name: Kitchen & store
rooms.purpose: run by the canteen-keeper

structures.notes: Canteen-keeper Mother Vesh + 3 helpers (resident in a back nook). The cellar hatch of the Sounding-Glass (VS-K01) comes out near here — the only informal seam between the two cities.

structures.name: The Foreman's Post

position.depth_note: at the foot of the customs stair

structures.purpose: A small hard office at the foot of the stair up to the customs post — the point where the under-city answers to the over-city. The foreman is the only person who routinely crosses between the two maps, and is trusted by neither.

rooms.name: The Office
rooms.purpose: a ledger-desk, a lamp, a locked shift-book

rooms.name: Bunk
rooms.purpose: the foreman sleeps at the seam

structures.notes: Foreman Adric — over-city clothes, under-city hands. A natural quest-broker character.

structures.name: The Umbral Tower

position.note: the Nyx'Talar rim observatory — greybox tower i=1; the House that times what hides what

structures.purpose: Where the House measures the exact instant one light passes behind another — an eclipse, a transit, an occultation — and, from that, the exact instant of everything else. The instruments here can time a shadow to the breath; the House long ago learned that whoever owns the timing of a concealment owns the concealment. Its readings are never published entire.

rooms.name: The Occultation Hall
rooms.purpose: the ground instrument floor; a wall of shuttered apertures opened one at a time

rooms.name: The Timed Vault
rooms.purpose: a lead-lined room of dated observations; each is a record of who or what was hidden, and precisely when

rooms.name: Head's shuttered study
rooms.purpose: Magister Suvane's study; the only window in the House that is never opened by day

rooms.name: Reckoners' room
rooms.purpose: juniors reduce the eclipse-tables; taught to forget the names attached to the timings

rooms.name: The Shadow-Chamber
rooms.purpose: top floor; a single north aperture and a graduated dark-glass; the reading is taken alone, always alone

rooms.name: Servants' stair & lamp-room
rooms.purpose: the spiral stair; the dome's finial is lit but hooded, so it shows as the dimmest of the nine

structures.notes: First Occulter + 6 live-in reckoners. Alone of the nine rim domes, its lit finial is deliberately hooded — the House prefers to be the one watching, not the one seen.

structures.name: The Shuttered Seat
structures.purpose: The living seat of the House — and the only rim manor whose principal rooms face away from the Mirror. Nyx'Talar built to see the terraces below, not the lake: a house that watches the city more attentively than it watches the sky. Every window has an inner shutter, and the shutters are the point.

rooms.name: The Hall of Screens
rooms.purpose: reception behind carved lattices; guests are seen long before they are received

rooms.name: Suvane's chambers
rooms.purpose: the head's rooms; a listening-tube to the gate-lodge runs behind the wall

rooms.name: Family wing
rooms.purpose: chambers for the near family, each with its own lock

rooms.name: The Muffled Room
rooms.purpose: a felt-hung room where the House says aloud the things it will say nowhere else

rooms.name: Kitchen & stores
rooms.purpose: below the hall

rooms.name: Staff quarters
rooms.purpose: attic rooms; the staff are chosen for what they can be trusted not to repeat

structures.notes: Suvane + near family (5) + 11 household staff. The Seat faces the city, not the sky — the whole House's character in one architectural decision.

structures.name: The Villa Behind the Lattice
structures.purpose: Home of a senior Warden of the House, and shuttered so completely that neighbours cannot say whether anyone is home from one month to the next. Its protected sightline is real and legally registered, but the shutters over it are almost never drawn — a sightline held as an asset, not used as a view.

rooms.name: The Registered Study
rooms.purpose: the sightline is on file; the shutter over it has a dust-seal that has not been broken in years

rooms.name: Family rooms
rooms.purpose: Warden Ottress and household

structures.notes: Warden Ottress + household of 5. A villa that hoards a view it will not spend — the local definition of wealth.

structures.name: The Second Warden's Villa
structures.purpose: The household of the Second Warden — the House officer who, on paper, catalogues transits, and, off paper, arranges that certain observations are never made. The most-visited villa on the terrace after dark, though its visitors come by the back stair and are never seen to arrive.

rooms.name: The Cataloguing Room
rooms.purpose: the ostensible work; ledgers of who observed what and when

rooms.name: The Back Parlour
rooms.purpose: the real work; a room reached only from the servants' stair

rooms.name: Family rooms
rooms.purpose: Warden Coreth and household

structures.notes: Warden Coreth + household of 6. The House's discreet fixer; a rich vein of side-content — every favour has a timing, and a price paid in silence.

structures.name: The Kept Villa
structures.purpose: A villa the House maintains for the widow Halissa — not of Nyx'Talar blood, but of Nyx'Talar knowledge. She saw something, once, at an occultation, and has been comfortably, silently kept ever since. She has never been asked to leave, and understands perfectly why.

rooms.name: The Quiet Study
rooms.purpose: a sightline she was granted and does not use; she prefers the shutters

rooms.name: Rooms
rooms.purpose: Halissa, a companion, a House-appointed servant who is also a watcher

structures.notes: Halissa + household of 4 (one of whom reports to the Seat). Kept comfortable to be kept quiet — the House's method in one household.

structures.name: The Furnished Absence
structures.purpose: A villa kept fully furnished, warmed, dusted, and empty — a House property held ready for a guest who is never named in advance and never stays twice. A single caretaker lives in the back rooms and asks nothing. On the Plate it is a dwelling like any other; in truth it is a room the House keeps so that certain meetings can happen at an address that belongs to no one.

rooms.name: The Ready Rooms
rooms.purpose: kept warm and made up; a decanter always full, a fire always laid

rooms.name: Caretaker's rooms
rooms.purpose: the one soul who lives here, and forgets faces professionally

structures.notes: Caretaker Pell alone. A furnished alibi — the wedge's quiet novelty at ground level, before you even reach the Hall of Occultations below.

structures.name: The Sealwrights' Hall
structures.purpose: Wax, lead, wire and cipher: the makers of the city's seals and locks work here, and the House that owns them makes very sure the trade stays in the wedge. A seal is a promise that a thing was not opened; Nyx'Talar built its fortune on being the people you trust to certify that a thing stayed shut.

rooms.name: The Sealing Floor
rooms.purpose: matrices, melting-pots, the die-safe; each sealwright's dies are numbered and never leave

rooms.name: The Cipher Room
rooms.purpose: where letter-locks and cipher-wheels are cut for private clients

rooms.name: Master's dwelling
rooms.purpose: the master sealwright's family above the floor

rooms.name: Journeymen's loft
rooms.purpose: boarded sealwrights, oathbound

structures.notes: Master-sealwright Ordell Craze + 12 (family & oathbound journeymen). Every wax seal in Starfall's official post is struck from a die kept in this room.

structures.name: The Sealed Copyists
structures.purpose: Discreet copyists who reproduce documents they are trained not to read — contracts, testaments, sealed depositions, the occasional thing that must exist in exactly two copies and no third. They work at screened desks, each blind to the next, and are paid partly in coin and partly in the House's protection.

rooms.name: The Screened Floor
rooms.purpose: single desks in felt booths; a copyist never sees the whole of what they copy

rooms.name: The Warden's window
rooms.purpose: the overseer sees every desk and every desk knows it

rooms.name: Copyists' dormitory
rooms.purpose: boarded copyists, sworn to the House

structures.notes: Overseer plus 8 copyists. The honest twin of the Sealwrights: one House makes the thing that stays shut, the other makes the thing that quietly exists twice.

structures.name: Lesser Wardens' Row
structures.purpose: Six joined houses of the wedge's lesser wardens — the watchers without a sightline, who keep the House's real survey: not of the stars, but of the streets. Who came up the Processional and when; whose shutters opened; which barge ran late. Sightless, respectable, and never off duty.

rooms.name: Per-house: watch-room + 2 chambers
rooms.purpose: each of the 6 houses: a front room with a good view of the stair, and two chambers behind

structures.notes: 6 households, ~22 souls. Named principal: the ledger-warden Nessa Ptol, who has a memory for faces the House cannot afford to lose.

structures.name: The Blind Eye
structures.purpose: The wedge's inn, and the one place in the House of watchers where, by long custom, no one is watched. The rule is enforced by the innkeeper and honoured by everyone, because a city this observed needs exactly one room in which to be unseen. This quarter's Strain-relief haven.

rooms.name: The Common Room
rooms.purpose: hearth, deep booths, the painted-over eye above the bar that gives the place its name and its promise

rooms.name: Letting rooms (x5)
rooms.purpose: five rooms above; the register records only false names, on purpose

rooms.name: Cellar
rooms.purpose: canal-cooled store; a low door, never mentioned, that opens toward the under-galleries

structures.notes: Innkeeper Mistress Oll (one-eyed, and pointed about it) + 2 family + 2 staff. The cellar door is the wedge's over/under seam.

structures.name: The Unlabelled Market
structures.purpose: Ten shopfronts, and not one of them a painted sign — you are meant to already know which door you want. Letter-writers, a lock-fitter, a dealer in second-hand seals, a discreet apothecary, a fence who calls himself a valuer, and a tea-house where introductions are made. Live-over-the-shop trade, conducted at a murmur.

rooms.name: Per unit: shopfront + workshop + room above
rooms.purpose: 10 units, most with a family living above; the signless door is the local etiquette

structures.notes: 10 shops, ~30 souls. Named: the 'valuer' Sim Onrey, who can find the owner of anything for a fee, and the letter-writer old Fenn.

structures.name: The Shrine of the Passing Shadow
structures.purpose: An Umbrion shrine kept by Nyx'Talar custom: not merely dark, but built around a single slow aperture that lets one blade of star-lamp light cross the floor and pass, once, each night. You come to watch the light be hidden — to practise, the House would say, the one grace it truly believes in: that some things are meant to pass out of sight and be let go.

rooms.name: The Transit Cell
rooms.purpose: the moving blade of light and the long dark on either side of it; you sit and watch it occulted

rooms.name: Keeper's cell
rooms.purpose: the shrine-keeper's room

structures.notes: Keeper Threnn, who has watched the same blade of light vanish for a hundred and forty years and calls it the only honest clock in the city.

structures.name: Canal Dwellings — Shutterside
structures.purpose: Dense canalside housing named for its most-remarked feature: every window has a shutter, and on this stretch the shutters stay closed even in warm weather. Home to the wedge's boatwrights, runners, sealwrights' families and market-hands — folk who have learned that the House rewards those who see much and say little.

rooms.name: Per dwelling: 2-3 rooms
rooms.purpose: 8 dwellings, families of 3-6

structures.notes: ~38 souls. Named: the boatwoman Corra Sel, who runs the night-barge and knows which cargoes are never weighed.

structures.name: The Watcher's Rooms
structures.purpose: Two rented rooms taken by a professional watcher — a freelance who sells the House what its lesser wardens miss. The window commands the canal-mouth and the foot of the terrace stair; the rooms hold a chair, a good glass, and a wall of dated notes in a private shorthand no one else can read.

rooms.name: The Watching Room
rooms.purpose: one chair, one glass, one window that sees the whole approach

rooms.name: Sleeping room
rooms.purpose: a cot; the watcher sleeps by day and works the dark

structures.notes: The watcher Aline Voss + an apprentice she is training to disappear. A freelance eye the House uses and does not quite trust — a quest-broker with her own agenda.

structures.name: The Watch-Customs
structures.purpose: The wedge's customs post, and unlike its neighbours' it is staffed around the clock — because Nyx'Talar cares less what a cargo weighs than who is standing next to it. Everything that comes up from below is weighed here; everyone that comes up is noted. The watch lives above the scales, so the door is never unmanned.

rooms.name: The Weighing Hall
rooms.purpose: scales, tally-desks, a wardsealed strongroom, and a second ledger that records faces, not freight

rooms.name: The Watch-loft
rooms.purpose: the live-in watch; a window onto the shore that is never dark

structures.notes: Watch-officer Delm + 2 clerks, resident above the scales (unlike the day-only posts of other wedges). The House's official eye on the one door up from the under-city.

structures.name: The Silent Lock

position.depth_note: beneath the canal quarter

structures.purpose: The wedge's barge lock, greased and counter-weighted so that it runs without the crash and clang of the others — Nyx'Talar's cargoes prefer to arrive without announcing themselves. It lifts the ordinary stone and grain of the quarter, and, on certain nights, one crate more that is not on the manifest and is never weighed at the post above.

rooms.name: The Muffled Chamber
rooms.purpose: the lock basin; the gates run on felted rollers so a lift can be made at midnight and heard by no one

rooms.name: The Capstan Floor
rooms.purpose: walked by the lift-gang; the overseer here logs everything except what he is paid to forget

rooms.name: The Off-Manifest Niche
rooms.purpose: a walled recess for the crate that has no paper

structures.notes: Worked, not lived-in. Lock-master Bront (homes in the Warren). The quietest lock in Starfall, by design — the throat of the wedge's unseen economy.

structures.name: The Listening Gallery

position.depth_note: runs radially under the terraces

structures.purpose: Twin function in one tunnel: it carries the tuned Song-conduits up to the wedge's star-lamps, like every wedge's gallery — but Nyx'Talar shaped its vaults so that sound gathers and travels, and set listeners in its niches. Voices from certain rooms above, spoken near a hearth or a drain, arrive here thinned but legible. The House does not call it eavesdropping. It calls it acoustics.

rooms.name: The Long Gallery
rooms.purpose: conduit run + focusing vaults; access ladders to each terrace's lamp-stems

rooms.name: Listening niches (x4)
rooms.purpose: where the listeners sit their shifts; each niche hears a different quarter of the wedge above

structures.notes: A crew of 6 who both tend the Song-conduits and man the niches. They live at their posts and are relieved rarely; what they hear goes up in a sealed hand to the Hall of Occultations.

structures.name: The Deep-Wrights' Warren

position.depth_note: cut into the shore-mass

structures.purpose: Home and hall of the Terran stone-wrights who cut this wedge's under-galleries — and, more than in any other wedge, its hidden passages: the House pays well for tunnels that appear on no wright's plan but their own. The deep folk hold the beautiful city up and also, quietly, riddle it with ways to move unseen. Proud, glow-warm, and closer-mouthed even than the House above them.

rooms.name: The Carved Hall
rooms.purpose: a communal hall; a long stone table; the wrights eat together and speak little of the day's digging

rooms.name: Sleeping galleries
rooms.purpose: bunk-niches for ~46 wrights

rooms.name: The Unmapped Room
rooms.purpose: where the warren-master keeps the only true plan of what has been dug, in Terran stone-script

rooms.name: The Shrine of Petrocore
rooms.purpose: a Stone-Voice shrine — the wrong god for this city, kept anyway

structures.notes: Warren-master Bront + lock-master (same Bront works the Silent Lock) + ~46 Terran deep-wrights. They know every hidden way in the wedge, and sell that knowledge to no one — the one thing the House cannot buy outright.

structures.name: The Runners' Bunks

position.depth_note: beside the lock, at the gallery mouth

structures.purpose: The bunk-hall of the wedge's runners: the human and orc porters who carry sealed things through the under-galleries by hand, because a thing that never touches the official post can never be intercepted at it. They run the dark between the two cities all night, memorise routes and never write them, and are paid to have poor memories for everything else. The largest, youngest, most disposable population in the wedge.

rooms.name: Bunk rows
rooms.purpose: double-bunks for ~52; the runners sleep in shifts, so a bunk is never cold

rooms.name: The Route-room
rooms.purpose: where a runner is given a destination and a seal to match, and nothing in writing

structures.notes: ~52 runners (human & orc). The muscle and legs of the unseen economy; part of the unnamed 778. Named: the runner-elder Vosk, who has never once been caught and teaches the young ones how not to be.

structures.name: The Underquiet Canteen

position.depth_note: at the gallery crossing

structures.purpose: The wedge's under-city commons, and the one place its habitual silence lifts a little: runners, wrights, lift-gang and listeners eat the same grey good stew and, for the length of a meal, say true things. The canteen-keeper enforces the Blind Eye's rule down here too — what is said over the pot is not carried out of the room.

rooms.name: The Long Room
rooms.purpose: trestles, a great range, a wall where the dead are chalked and no name is ever a false one

rooms.name: Kitchen & store
rooms.purpose: run by the keeper

structures.notes: Canteen-keeper Ma Dell + 3 helpers. Sister-room to the Underspill and the Undertoll; the three under-canteens' keepers know each other, and between them know everything.

structures.name: The Keeper of the Seam

position.depth_note: at the foot of the watch-customs stair

structures.purpose: The seam-office where the under-city answers to the watch above — and where, uniquely in this wedge, the foreman's real job is to decide what the watch is told. He keeps two shift-books: the one that goes up, and the one that is true. He is trusted by neither map, and knows more than both.

rooms.name: The Office
rooms.purpose: a ledger-desk, a lamp, two locked shift-books that do not agree

rooms.name: Bunk
rooms.purpose: the foreman sleeps at the seam, as they all do

structures.notes: Foreman Karse. In a House of secrets the seam-keeper is the most dangerous man in the wedge, because he is the one who edits the record before it rises. A natural quest-broker — and a natural blackmail target.

structures.name: The Hall of Occultations

position.depth_note: a deep sealed vault beneath the wedge, reached only through the Umbral Tower's private stair

footprint.form: vaulted stone chamber, wards on every door

structures.purpose: The wedge's — and secretly the city's — true archive: the place where secrets are timed, sealed, and kept. Sealed depositions, testaments held against a death, confessions bought and never used, and the dated occultation-records that prove who was hidden from what and when. A message left here at a named hour is delivered at another named hour to a named hand and no other; a thing sealed here is opened only when its condition falls due. The House sells not information but its safekeeping — and the whole city, from Conclave down, quietly depends on it. It is on no plate, because a vault of everyone's secrets cannot be allowed to have an address.

rooms.name: The Timed Vault
rooms.purpose: ranked warded drawers, each dated to open; the Sealed Warden alone knows which fall due tonight

rooms.name: The Drop
rooms.purpose: a screened chamber where a client leaves or collects without ever seeing another face

rooms.name: The Keepers' cells
rooms.purpose: the record-keepers live sealed inside; they take an oath of the vault and are not seen above for years at a time

structures.notes: The Sealed Warden Ilex + 11 record-keepers who live within the vault. THE novel landmark of the wedge and a franchise-grade set-piece: whoever holds this hall holds a lever on every House in Starfall — including, one imagines, a record or two the Academy would rather did not exist.

structures.name: The Ferry-Warren

position.depth_note: at the under-mouth of the Silent Lock

structures.purpose: Where the crews of the night-barges live — the polemen and gate-hands who work the world-below cargo up through the Silent Lock in the dark. They keep the same hours as the runners and the same silence, and their children grow up knowing the black under-water better than the terraces of light above their heads, which most of them have never seen by day.

rooms.name: Bunk galleries
rooms.purpose: family bunk-niches along the loading water; whole lives lived below the waterline of the city

rooms.name: The Wet Floor
rooms.purpose: where barges are made fast and unladen out of the light

structures.notes: ~47 barge-folk (human, orc, a few Terran). A community entirely of the under-city, born to it — the sharpest edge of the two-maps theme in this wedge: people the Plate cannot omit, because it never knew to include them.

structures.name: The Wanderers' Tower

position.note: the Oravelle rim observatory — greybox tower i=2; where the five wandering lights are logged nightly and the city's dates are made

structures.purpose: The wandering lights are tracked from here and their positions turned, floor by floor, into the ephemeris the whole realm sets its calendar by. Vael'Suran keeps the stars that never move; Oravelle keeps the five that do, and has learned that a thing which moves can be sold a prediction of where it will be. The Conclave dates its decrees from readings taken in this drum, which is the quiet root of the House's fortune.

rooms.name: The Observing Drum
rooms.purpose: the equatorial mounting and the graduated circles; the five wanderers logged against the fixed stars each clear night

rooms.name: The Reckoning Floor
rooms.purpose: banks of computers reducing positions into the running ephemeris; the loudest quiet room in Starfall, all pen-scratch and abacus

rooms.name: The Ephemeris Vault
rooms.purpose: brass-bound, humidity-sealed; the master tables back two thousand years, the only copy the House will not sell

rooms.name: Head's cabinet
rooms.purpose: Magister Corandine's study, sightline to the Mirror, a wall of sealed contracts framed like art

rooms.name: Computers' dormitory
rooms.purpose: cots for the live-in reckoners, who are paid in board and the promise of a clerkship

rooms.name: Servants' stair & lamp-room
rooms.purpose: the spiral stair; the crowning star-lamp is tended from here

structures.notes: Head + First Reckoner + 6 live-in computers. One of the nine lit rim domes of the greybox.

structures.name: The Oravelle Counting-Seat
structures.purpose: The richest seat on this arc of the rim, and the only one that is also a place of business: half manor, half counting-house, its ground floor a hall of sealing-desks where the House's bonded almanacs are stamped and its guarantees underwritten. The Oravelle do not measure status in windows, as Vael'Suran do, but in ledgers — and theirs are the longest in the city. Every room smells of sealing-wax and money.

rooms.name: The Sealing Hall
rooms.purpose: public-facing; long counters, the great House seal on a chained press, clients who arrive by appointment and leave with a stamped future

rooms.name: The Strongroom
rooms.purpose: warded; the bond-reserve that backs the guarantees, and the register of who owes the House a favour

rooms.name: Corandine's chambers
rooms.purpose: the head's private rooms, best sightline in the House

rooms.name: Family wing
rooms.purpose: chambers for the near family and the two clerk-cousins being groomed to inherit the desks

rooms.name: Kitchen, stores, staff
rooms.purpose: household below and attic rooms above

structures.notes: Corandine + near family (6) + 17 household and counting-house staff. The seat doubles as the House's public office, unusual for the rim.

structures.name: Sightline Villa — the First Reckoner
structures.purpose: Home of First Reckoner Hessa Vun, the commoner-born computer who actually derives the ephemeris the House sells and Corandine signs. Her sightline is real and her figures are exact, and she is the one person in Starfall who could ruin House Oravelle with a single honest sentence about how often the guarantees are simply bets the House can afford to lose.

rooms.name: The Working Study
rooms.purpose: the protected sightline; a private reckoning-desk and a locked drawer of the errors the published tables do not admit

rooms.name: Family rooms
rooms.purpose: Hessa, her husband, two children

structures.notes: Hessa Vun + household of 6. The Halvenor-role of this wedge: the mind behind the signature. A strong side-quest lever (what the errata drawer holds).

structures.name: Sightline Villa — the Bonded Notary
structures.purpose: The villa of Notary-Magister Selvane, whose seal turns a computed date into a binding one. A prosperous, cautious household that has grown rich witnessing other people's certainty; the study is lined with the counterfoils of forty years of stamped tomorrows.

rooms.name: The Sealing Study
rooms.purpose: the notarial seal, the witness-bench, a sightline used mostly to impress clients

rooms.name: Living rooms
rooms.purpose: Selvane, a spouse, one grown child, two servants

structures.notes: Notary-Magister Selvane + household of 6.

structures.name: Sightline Villa — the Voided Magister
structures.purpose: The villa of Magister Orrin Tallowe, who once sealed a planting-date for an entire Terran province and was wrong by a season, ruining a harvest and, quietly, himself. The House honoured the guarantee — that is the whole point of the guarantee — but it took the cost out of Orrin, who now keeps a sightline he can no longer afford and computes, obsessively, the single reading he got wrong, looking for the House's error instead of his own.

rooms.name: The Reproach Study
rooms.purpose: one wall entirely given to the recomputation of a date fourteen years gone

rooms.name: Rooms
rooms.purpose: Orrin, an unpaid companion, one loyal old servant

structures.notes: Orrin Tallowe + household of 4. Side-quest seed: was the voided date his error or the House's? Hessa Vun's errata drawer may know.

structures.name: The Ephemeris Manufactory
structures.purpose: A factory of paper and patience: rooms of clerks who take the tower's raw readings and grind them into thousands of fair-copied almanacs, tide-tables and lucky-day sheets for sale across the realm. The work is divided so finely that no single clerk understands the whole calculation — a deliberate arrangement, since a clerk who understood the whole could set up in competition, or in blackmail.

rooms.name: The Calculating Floor
rooms.purpose: ranked desks; each clerk performs one step of a computation they are forbidden to see the ends of

rooms.name: The Fair-Copy Room
rooms.purpose: scribes multiplying the finished tables by hand under the manufactory's tallow reek

rooms.name: The Binding & Sealing Loft
rooms.purpose: where sheets become bonded almanacs and take the small House seal

rooms.name: Clerks' dormitory
rooms.purpose: boarded clerks, four to a room, docked for a blotted line

structures.notes: Overseer Marn Quell + ~27 boarded clerks and copyists. The engine of the House's fortune, and the least-credited labour in the wedge above ground.

structures.name: The Sealers' & Notaries' Hall
structures.purpose: The guild that makes and guards the seals — the bonded matrices without which no Oravelle guarantee is worth its wax. Engravers cut the dies, assayers weigh the wax, and a warden keeps the register of which seals are live and which have been struck void, because a stolen live seal could counterfeit the future itself.

rooms.name: The Die-Cutting Room
rooms.purpose: engravers at the bonded matrices; a guarded, jeweller-quiet trade

rooms.name: The Register
rooms.purpose: the warden's book of live and voided seals; a locked room within a locked room

rooms.name: Guild dormitory
rooms.purpose: boarded engravers and apprentices

structures.notes: Seal-warden Ippa Dross + 11 engravers/apprentices.

structures.name: Lesser Clerks' Row
structures.purpose: Seven joined narrow houses of the wedge's tenured clerks — the reckoners, sealers'-assistants and register-keepers who have risen just high enough to hold a lease and a title but never a sightline. The most anxious street in Starfall: every family here is one blotted ledger from the dormitory they climbed out of.

rooms.name: Per-house: counting-room + 2 chambers
rooms.purpose: each of the 7 houses: a private desk and two small rooms

structures.notes: 7 households, ~24 souls. Named: register-keeper Voss, who knows exactly what everyone above and below him earns and resents both.

structures.name: The Ledger & Compass
structures.purpose: The wedge's inn, and the one place in House Oravelle where nobody keeps a tally: the innkeeper runs a slate but rubs it clean at year's turn, a small local heresy in a district that binds everything else in triplicate. Clerks come here to be, for one evening, a person rather than a step in a calculation. The wedge's Strain-relief haven.

rooms.name: The Common Room
rooms.purpose: hearth, long tables, an old ship's compass over the bar that no longer points anywhere and is beloved for it

rooms.name: Letting rooms (x5)
rooms.purpose: five rooms above for travellers come to buy dates and for clerks between lodgings

rooms.name: Cellar
rooms.purpose: canal-cooled store; a grille to the Under-Terraces the innkeeper swears is only for the draught

structures.notes: Innkeeper Delph Ravin + 3 family + 2 staff. The cellar grille is this wedge's over/under seam (to OR-X05).

structures.name: The Almanac Market
structures.purpose: Eleven stalls and shopfronts where the House's product meets the street: printed almanacs, wedding-date charts, sailing-tables, cheap lucky-day sheets, and the second-hand almanac dealer who sells last year's certainties at a discount. The public face of prediction — retail fate, sold over a canal counter with the small seal that makes it feel binding.

rooms.name: Per unit: shopfront + back-room + room above
rooms.purpose: 11 units, most with a family living above

structures.notes: 11 shops, ~30 souls. Named: almanac-seller the widow Pell, and the second-hand dealer Osk, who reads the discounted sheets to the illiterate for a coin.

structures.name: The Chapel of Variables
structures.purpose: A small human-kept chapel to the Architect of Variables and the Observer of Outcomes — a faith that holds the world to be a running experiment — tolerated in this wedge alone because a House that sells prediction finds it good for morale that its human clerks worship a god of odds. The Noctari majority think it charmingly superstitious; the clerks who pray here think the same of the almanacs they copy.

rooms.name: The Chapel
rooms.purpose: two facing altars — one for the change, one for the watching; a wall of votive tokens, each a settled bet

rooms.name: Keeper's cell
rooms.purpose: the lay-keeper's room

structures.notes: Lay-keeper Ansel Roe (human) + 2 lodging pilgrims. Canon-aware: the human Path of Adaptation (Canon_Notes) given a foothold in a prediction House. A quiet counterweight to Noctari Umbrion-worship.

structures.name: The Assurance House
structures.purpose: The wedge's novel invention and its most quietly sinister room: a canalside office where, for a fee, House Oravelle will not merely predict a date but GUARANTEE it — underwriting your harvest, your voyage, your wedding against the sky being wrong. In practice the House pools the fees, pays the rare claim, and keeps the difference, so a hall of scholars has become, without ever quite noticing, a bank that sells the future as a hedge. The queue outside is the real proof of the House's power: the whole city has agreed to be afraid of dates on Oravelle's terms.

rooms.name: The Assuring Hall
rooms.purpose: petition-desks where a farmer or a captain buys certainty; the great odds-board chalked and rechalked

rooms.name: The Pool-Room
rooms.purpose: warded; the fee-reserve that pays out the losing guarantees, and the actuary's forbidden tables

rooms.name: Assurers' lodging
rooms.purpose: the resident assurers, who sleep above the money

structures.notes: Chief Assurer Wend Colu + 9 resident assurers/clerks. The wedge's novel landmark: prediction turned into a hedge-fund. Rich quest and theme material — the actuary's tables know the House loses more guarantees than it admits.

structures.name: Canal Dwellings — Inkside
structures.purpose: Dense canalside housing stained perpetually blue-black at the ground floor, home to the printers, ink-makers, paper-porters and copy-runners who feed the manufactory above. Ink comes up the canal by barge and the whole block smells of iron-gall and reed; the children are born with stained hands.

rooms.name: Per dwelling: 2-3 rooms
rooms.purpose: 9 dwellings, families of 3-6

structures.notes: ~46 souls. Named: ink-master Corrl, whose recipe the whole wedge depends on and whose lungs it is quietly ruining.

structures.name: The Oravelle Canal & its two bridges

position.note: one of the greybox's three canals, threading this wedge's canal quarter

structures.purpose: Star-water and cargo-water both: the canal drains the quarter and, through the lock below, carries in the reed, rag and ink the paper-machine runs on, and carries out the crated almanacs by barge. Two arched footbridges cross it, their parapets chained with the small brass tallies of goods that have passed — the canal itself kept as a ledger.
structures.notes: The visible throat of the invisible paper-supply chain (see OR-X01 the lock and OR-X04 the pulp-works).

structures.name: The Reckoners' Gate & Customs Post
structures.purpose: Where this wedge's processional meets the shore: a customs post that does not merely weigh what comes up from below but DATES it, stamping every barge-load with the licensed day it may be sold — a small, profitable tyranny by which the House converts the labour of the under-city into paper the moment it surfaces. The one official door here faces up, and it charges for the privilege.

rooms.name: The Dating Hall
rooms.purpose: scales, tally-desks, the licensing-stamp, a wardsealed strongroom

rooms.name: Officers' room
rooms.purpose: the customs-dater and two clerks

structures.notes: Customs-dater Ollen + 2 clerks (day post; counted at their canal homes; listed here as workplace).

structures.name: The Reed-Lock

position.depth_note: beneath the canal quarter

structures.purpose: A stone chamber-lock that lifts the barges of reed, rag, lime and ink up from the world below into the wedge's canal — the raw throat of the paper-machine. The whole glittering trade in printed certainty begins as sodden reed hauled up this shaft in the dark by gangs the almanacs will never mention. The Plate draws the canal and stops at the waterline.

rooms.name: The Lock Chamber
rooms.purpose: the flooding basin; the counter-weighted gates; a permanent stink of wet reed

rooms.name: The Capstan Floor
rooms.purpose: where the lift-gangs walk the capstans against the barge-weight

rooms.name: Tally hole
rooms.purpose: the under-clerk's niche, where the real weight is logged before the over-city halves it

structures.notes: Worked, not lived-in. Lock-master Bral. The under-clerk keeps the honest tonnage in charcoal — the Other Map's paper.

structures.name: The Conduit Gallery

position.depth_note: runs radially under the terraces

structures.purpose: The wedge's run of tuned crystal conduits, carrying the Song up to the star-lamps of the counting-terraces so that the manufactory can compute through the night. The clerks above write by a light that people down here keep singing by hand; when a lamp over a desk 'simply burns,' a conduit-wright in the dark is the reason the ledger can be balanced past dusk.

rooms.name: The Long Gallery
rooms.purpose: the conduit run; access ladders to each terrace's lamp-stems

rooms.name: Tuning niches (x4)
rooms.purpose: where the wrights kneel to true the crystal

structures.notes: Worked by conduit-wrights (mostly Terran), lodged in OR-X03. The literal machinery behind the manufactory's endless light.

structures.name: The Under-Reckoners' Hall

position.depth_note: cut into the shore-mass

structures.purpose: Home of the Terran deep-wrights and conduit-crews who cut and hold up the counting-house wedge — and, unusually, of a knot of Terran under-reckoners the House quietly employs to check the manufactory's figures below the record, because the deep-folk count in a base the elves find awkward and cannot easily cook. A proud, warm, glow-lit hall that does the House's most trusted arithmetic and receives none of its credit.

rooms.name: The Carved Hall
rooms.purpose: a communal hall; a long stone table scored with a reckoning-grid the deep-folk compute on directly

rooms.name: Sleeping galleries
rooms.purpose: bunk-niches for ~40 wrights and under-reckoners

rooms.name: The Shrine of Petrocore
rooms.purpose: a Stone-Voice shrine; the deep-folk keep the right god in the wrong city

structures.notes: Deep-warden Torv Greel + ~43 Terran deep-wrights, conduit-crew and under-reckoners. Novel wrinkle: the House's most trusted sums are done, off the books, by the people it will not seat.

structures.name: The Pulp-Works & Rag-Halls

position.depth_note: a flooded works cut beside the reed-lock

structures.purpose: The hidden factory that MAKES the paper the whole glittering House is printed on: a sweating, roaring vault of stamping-hammers, lime-vats and rag-halls where reed and cast-off cloth are beaten to pulp, drawn into sheets, and hung to dry on endless underground lines. Every bonded almanac and stamped guarantee in Starfall began as filth boiled in this dark by human and orc gangs who cannot read a word of what they make. The single most industrial space in Starfall, and the most invisible — a paper-mill directly beneath a House that sells paper.

rooms.name: The Stamping Floor
rooms.purpose: water-driven trip-hammers beating rag to pulp; a noise you feel in the teeth

rooms.name: The Vat-Hall
rooms.purpose: the lime and pulp vats; the vat-workers, whose hands go pale and then numb

rooms.name: The Drying Lofts
rooms.purpose: warm racks of drying sheets, lit by waste-heat; the one comfortable air in the under-city, and forbidden to linger in

rooms.name: Rag-hall bunks
rooms.purpose: bunk-niches for the pulp-gangs, who live inside the noise

structures.notes: ~58 human and orc pulp- and rag-workers, elder Osma of the rag-halls named. The wedge's second novel landmark: a paper-mill under a paper-House, the literal ground of the Other Map's theme. Part of the unnamed 778.

structures.name: The Reed-Bottom Canteen

position.depth_note: at the junction of the galleries

structures.purpose: The warm shared room of this under-city: a canteen at the gallery-crossing where deep-wrights, pulp-gangs, conduit-crews and lock-hands eat the same grey, good stew and, at the long table, teach each other to read from stolen almanac off-cuts — the one place in the wedge where the House's paper is used against the House's grain.

rooms.name: The Long Room
rooms.purpose: trestles, a great range, a wall where the dead are chalked and a corner where letters are learned

rooms.name: Kitchen & store
rooms.purpose: run by the canteen-keeper

structures.notes: Canteen-keeper Old Ghu + 3 helpers. The clandestine literacy corner foreshadows Part Two's SQ-P2-01 (The First Book) 300 years early. The Ledger & Compass cellar grille surfaces near here.

structures.name: The Foreman's Post

position.depth_note: at the foot of the customs stair

structures.purpose: The seam-office at the foot of the stair up to the Reckoners' Gate, where the under-city's real tonnage is reconciled against the dated, halved, licensed figure the over-city will accept. The foreman keeps both numbers and the arithmetic between them, and is the only person permitted to know how large the difference is.

rooms.name: The Office
rooms.purpose: a ledger-desk, a lamp, a locked reconciliation-book

rooms.name: Bunk
rooms.purpose: the foreman sleeps at the seam

structures.notes: Foreman Sarn — keeps the honest tonnage in charcoal and the House's in ink, and is paid precisely to know they differ. Twin to Foreman Adric (H0).

structures.name: The Dead-Letter Vault

position.depth_note: a dry catacomb off the far gallery

structures.purpose: A dry stone catacomb where House Oravelle buries its mistakes: every superseded ephemeris, voided guarantee and wrong-dated almanac, shelved and sealed rather than destroyed, because a prediction House cannot be seen to burn its errors and cannot bear to let a client find them. A silent underground library of every tomorrow the House got wrong — including, somewhere on the shelves, the voided date that ruined Magister Orrin Tallowe, and the errata that might exonerate him.

rooms.name: The Stacks of Voided Days
rooms.purpose: sealed cases of failed predictions, filed by the date they were proved wrong

rooms.name: Registrar's cell
rooms.purpose: the one keeper's room, lit by a single conduit-lamp

structures.notes: Registrar of Voided Days Miral Enn + one assistant. Novel landmark: a bureaucratic catacomb of wrong futures. Direct quest hook to OR-U03 (Orrin's exoneration) and the Assurance House's hidden loss-rate.

structures.name: The Long-Sight Tower

position.note: the Sabreth rim observatory — greybox tower i=3; officially a comet-watch, in practice the finest private information-engine in Starfall

structures.purpose: Where the House watches for comets — the long-haired stars whose coming everyone fears and no one will be caught fearing. Sabreth reads them true and then sells them dressed: the same faint smear of light becomes a warning, a blessing, or a silence, depending on who is paying. The instrument on the top floor is genuinely excellent; it has to be, because a House that sold false omens would eventually be caught, and Sabreth is never caught.

rooms.name: The Watch Floor
rooms.purpose: the sweep-telescopes and the comet-ledgers; every new smear of light logged before dawn and priced by noon

rooms.name: The Interpretation Room
rooms.purpose: windowless; where a true observation becomes a saleable omen — the House's real workshop, and the one room clients never see

rooms.name: The Client-Book Vault
rooms.purpose: silver-locked; who asked what, and what they were told — worth more than any chart in the city

rooms.name: Night-readers' loft
rooms.purpose: the live-in watchers who take the small hours; sworn to discretion, paid to keep it

rooms.name: The Signal Cupola
rooms.purpose: a shuttered lamp at the very top; a chosen colour shown at a chosen hour tells a waiting client, across the whole caldera, what the stars decided

structures.notes: 8 live-in night-readers & interpreters. The lit finial is one of the greybox's nine rim domes. The signal cupola is a genuine over-city broadcast the Plate would never think to draw.

structures.name: The Sabreth Seat
structures.purpose: Richer than a comet-House has any honest right to be, and dressed to make you notice and then decide not to ask. Gold leaf the fixed-star Houses would call vulgar; a hall built for arrivals; more doors than a house needs, several of which are for leaving unseen. Every grand thing in it is real, which is precisely how you know the money is not.

rooms.name: The Hall of Welcomes
rooms.purpose: reception staged for effect; a ceiling painted with a comet whose tail points, if you follow it, at the strongroom

rooms.name: The Magistra's chambers
rooms.purpose: Aubrelle Sabreth's rooms; a private stair down that is not on the House's own plans

rooms.name: The Quiet Parlour
rooms.purpose: where the largest clients are received away from the Omen Court's theatre — no veils, no incense, just numbers

rooms.name: Family & guest wing
rooms.purpose: family and the House's ever-present 'guests' — leverage, mostly, kept comfortable

rooms.name: Kitchen, stores, staff & guard-room
rooms.purpose: a household larger and harder than a scholar's house should need

structures.notes: Aubrelle + family (6) + 17 staff/guards. Grander than any other House Seat in the city, which everyone notices and no one mentions.

structures.name: The Long-Sight's Villa
structures.purpose: Home of Nemora Sabreth, the Long-Sight — the House's one genuine prodigy, the cousin who can actually read a comet's path a season ahead and finds the whole trade of selling it slightly nauseating. Her sightline is the best in the wedge and she uses it, most nights, to look at nothing anyone will pay for.

rooms.name: The True Study
rooms.purpose: her real work, unsold; a wall of comet-paths drawn for their own sake

rooms.name: Living rooms
rooms.purpose: Nemora, a companion, an aunt, three staff

structures.notes: Nemora Sabreth + household of 7. The talent the whole House lives off, and the one Sabreth who'd leave if she had anywhere colder to go. A ready side-quest: buy, or free, an honest prediction.

structures.name: The Veilkeeper's Villa
structures.purpose: Home of Sarnauld Vray, the Veilkeeper — not a Sabreth by blood but the man who decides which clients are seen, in what order, and at what price, and who remembers every one. He is the House's true engine and knows it; the family tolerate him the way a body tolerates its own heart, resentfully and without a choice.

rooms.name: The Appointment Room
rooms.purpose: a desk, a locked diary, and a second door for clients who must not meet in the corridor

rooms.name: Living rooms
rooms.purpose: Vray, spouse, two children, four staff — comfortable, watchful, curtained

structures.notes: Sarnauld Vray + household of 8. The commoner-born fixer who runs the wedge's real business, mirroring the commoner-First-Surveyor / Strike-Master pattern of the other Houses — but for vice, not science.

structures.name: The Comfortable House
structures.purpose: A villa owned by no one in particular and lived in by 'Lady' Ombrise, a charming retired nobody with a suspicious lack of past and an unlimited line of credit. She hosts the parties where deals are agreed without ever being spoken, and her sightline is worth more as a place to be seen than as a place to see from.

rooms.name: The Salon
rooms.purpose: where the wedge's laundered money puts on its best dress and dances

rooms.name: Rooms
rooms.purpose: Ombrise + companion + five staff, all better-paid than staff should be

structures.notes: 'Lady' Ombrise + 7. A front residence — the respectable face the dirty money wears on the terrace. Answers the Serenthil 'Quiet House' tenant, but for a very different quiet.

structures.name: The Ephemeris-House
structures.purpose: Where omens are turned into product: almanacs, fortune-sheets, dated warnings and charmed calendars, printed by the ream and sold across the elven lands. The presses run all night and the ink smells of camphor and money. Officially Sabreth reads the future; here they manufacture it, in editions, with margins.

rooms.name: The Press Floor
rooms.purpose: silver-plate presses; the almanac in a dozen grades from gilt-vellum to gutter-pulp, each telling a slightly different fate

rooms.name: The Composing Room
rooms.purpose: where the interpreters' wordings are set — a craft of exact, deniable vagueness

rooms.name: Printers' dwelling
rooms.purpose: the master printer's family and the compositors above the presses

structures.notes: Master printer Pellon Sabreth + 17 (compositors, pressmen, families). The wedge's most respectable-looking trade and its most quietly cynical.

structures.name: The Fate-Scriveners' Row
structures.purpose: Seven joined houses of the small fate-trade: chart-copyists, charm-writers, street-criers who shout the day's printed omen, and the freelance readers too cheap or too honest for the Court. They live over their work, take the House's piecework, and dream of a client of their own.

rooms.name: Per-house: workroom + 2 chambers
rooms.purpose: 7 households of the fate-trade's underclass-that-still-counts-as-above

structures.notes: 7 households, ~24 souls. Named: the crier Vess, whose morning shout the wedge sets its mood by; and old Halden, who reads true for free and is quietly hated for it.

structures.name: The Perfumers' & Veil-Makers' Hall
structures.purpose: The trade of atmosphere: the incense that makes the Omen Court smell of certainty, the veils clients hide behind, the dyed silks and dimmed lamps that turn a guess into a revelation. Sabreth understood before anyone that an omen is mostly staging, and this is where the staging is made.

rooms.name: The Still-Room
rooms.purpose: resins and oils; the House's proprietary incense, whose recipe is a guild secret worth killing for and never has been

rooms.name: The Veil-Loom
rooms.purpose: the gauze veils, graded by opacity to the exact degree of anonymity a client pays for

rooms.name: Makers' dwelling
rooms.purpose: the guild families above

structures.notes: Guild-mistress Cael Onwe + 11. A trade that exists nowhere else in the city, because no other House needs to be believed.

structures.name: The Comet's Tail
structures.purpose: A canalside inn a cut too glamorous for its street — mirrored, warm, a little disreputable, the kind of place where a scholar can lose an evening and a secret at the same time. This wedge's Strain-relief haven, though the relief here comes with the faint sense of being read. The wine is good and the walls, it's said, are good listeners.

rooms.name: The Mirror Room
rooms.purpose: hearth, silvered walls, a long bar; a resident 'reader' does palms for drinks and reports the interesting ones upstairs

rooms.name: Letting rooms (x5)
rooms.purpose: five rooms above, two with doors clients use and never the same night

rooms.name: Cellar
