rooms.purpose: a canal-cooled store; a false wall gives onto the Veiled Water-Gate — how a client leaves without ever having arrived

structures.notes: Innkeeper Dosca Rell + 5. The cellar's false wall is Sabreth's over/under seam (to SB-X07). Every wedge's inn hides a stair down; this one hides a stair down for the guilty.

structures.name: The Omen Court

footprint.form: colonnaded court, open centre, stalls under the arcade

structures.purpose: The beautiful open secret of Starfall: a colonnaded court that stands empty by day and, by the ninth bell of night, fills with veiled clients moving between curtained stalls where fate is sold at every price — a copper charm at the edge, a whispered comet-reading at the centre, and, in the shuttered back rooms, things that are not readings at all. Respectable Houses send servants; respectable people come themselves, veiled, and pretend in the morning they did not. Everyone knows it is here. No map has ever admitted it.

rooms.name: The Arcade
rooms.purpose: the public stalls: charms, printed fates, cheap readers — the honest-seeming edge that makes the rest plausible

rooms.name: The Inner Ring
rooms.purpose: curtained booths for the real trade; incense so thick the faces don't matter, which is the point

rooms.name: The Back Rooms
rooms.purpose: where a 'reading' becomes a loan, a threat, a name bought or a name buried

rooms.name: The Mistress's box
rooms.purpose: Dalveen watches the whole floor through a gauze and misses nothing

structures.notes: The wedge's 'novel and unique' landmark — a market of fates, live-in staff of 12 (readers, doormen, incense-boys, guards). A superb future set-piece: a level that is a social maze, not a physical one.

structures.name: The Charm-Market
structures.purpose: The daylight trade that feeds on the night one: charm-carvers, incense-sellers, ink-and-amulet shops, a dealer in 'comet-glass' (ordinary glass, sold with a story), a herbalist whose calming draughts the Court buys by the barrel. Live-over-the-shop, and every shopkeeper here owes the House a favour they can't quite name the size of.

rooms.name: Per unit: shopfront + workshop + room above
rooms.purpose: 10 units, most with a family above, all leasing from Sabreth

structures.notes: 10 shops, ~28 souls. Named: the charm-carver Sesk, honest and poor; the comet-glass dealer Two-Fingers Voll, dishonest and comfortable.

structures.name: Canal Dwellings — Lantern Walk
structures.purpose: The wedge's densest housing, along the canal walk the Court's clients drift down by night — home to the readers, criers, doormen, incense-boys, boat-hands and market families who make the trade run and never rise in it. Warm, crowded, sharp-eyed, and full of people who have learned that the surest coin in Starfall is a secret.

rooms.name: Per dwelling: 2-3 rooms
rooms.purpose: 10 dwellings, families of 3-6

structures.notes: ~52 souls. Named: the boat-girl Nella, who ferries veiled clients and could name half the city if she ever chose to.

structures.name: The Shrine of the Turning
structures.purpose: A shrine to Umbrion turned toward fate rather than dream: a dark room with a slow silver wheel that the keeper turns once a night, so that the future 'moves' whether or not anyone reads it. The genuinely devout come here to be reminded that the comet means nothing and comes anyway — a quiet rebuke to the whole wedge above it, kept by the House as a kind of alibi.

rooms.name: The Wheel-Cell
rooms.purpose: the silver wheel; no omens sold, no coin taken — the one honest room in the district

rooms.name: Keeper's cell
rooms.purpose: the shrine-keeper's room

structures.notes: Keeper Anselm + a novice. The House funds it precisely because it undercuts the House — proof, to any suspicious Conclave visitor, of Sabreth's piety.

structures.name: The Sabreth Customs & Processional Foot
structures.purpose: The wedge's official customs post on the shore — the one the House makes sure is scrupulous, well-lit and slow, so that anyone watching the front door concludes Sabreth has nothing to hide. Everything worth hiding comes up through the Veiled Water-Gate below; the customs officer here is honest precisely so the House can afford to be watched.

rooms.name: The Weighing Hall
rooms.purpose: scales, tally-desks, and a strongroom that has never held anything interesting

rooms.name: Officers' room
rooms.purpose: the customs officer and two clerks

structures.notes: Customs officer Bren + 2 clerks (day post; counted at their canal homes). Deliberately, performatively clean.

structures.name: The Slack-Water Lock

position.depth_note: beneath the canal quarter

structures.purpose: The wedge's public barge-lock, raising food, fuel and stone from the world below like any other — except that its lock-master keeps two logs, and the difference between them is the House's real import. What arrives on the honest log keeps the district fed; what arrives on the other keeps it rich.

rooms.name: The Lock Chamber
rooms.purpose: the flooding basin and counter-weighted gates; worked by the lift-gangs

rooms.name: The Two-Log Office
rooms.purpose: the lock-master's niche; the honest ledger in ink, the other in a code only Vray can read

structures.notes: Worked, not slept-in (crew home in SB-X04). Lock-master Ferrun Oskt keeps the double books — the point where the clean city and the dirty money change places.

structures.name: The Conduit Gallery

position.depth_note: runs radially under the terraces

structures.purpose: The tuned crystal conduits that carry the Song up to this wedge's star-lamps, tended in the dark by crews the glamour above never sees — the same unglamorous truth under every House. Here the gallery is also a message-run: a tapped code along the conduit-crystal lets the Court signal the water-gate without a soul crossing the terraces.

rooms.name: The Long Gallery
rooms.purpose: the conduit run; access ladders up to each terrace's lamp-stems

rooms.name: Tuning niches (x3)
rooms.purpose: where conduit-wrights kneel to true the crystal — and, quietly, to tap the House's signals

structures.notes: Conduit-wrights (6, mostly Terran; home in SB-X04). The machinery behind 'the lamps simply burn,' doubling as the House's private telegraph.

structures.name: The Counting-Vault

position.depth_note: deep beneath the Seat, reached by the Magistra's private stair

structures.purpose: Where the wedge's suspect wealth is made to look born-clean: coin weighed, recut, re-minted as Court fees, almanac sales and villa rents; debts bought and sold; the true client-books cross-checked against the false. A quiet, orderly, lamplit room of clerks and hard men, and the actual reason House Sabreth exists. The Plate draws a comet-House of scholars; this is the House.

rooms.name: The Counting Floor
rooms.purpose: reckoners at long tables turning dirty coin into clean ledger-lines

rooms.name: The Strongroom
rooms.purpose: warded; the House's true reserve and its true client-book — the one worth more than the tower

rooms.name: Reckoners' & guards' cells
rooms.purpose: the live-in staff, sworn and paid never to climb the stair by day

structures.notes: The Reckoner Old Kesk + 15 (counters & guards), live-in for secrecy. The wedge's second 'novel' space — a laundering vault under a scholar-House, the Under-Terraces' darkest civic function.

structures.name: The Porters' Warren

position.depth_note: cut into the shore-mass by the lock

structures.purpose: Home of the Terran haulers and conduit-crews who move what the Slack-Water Lock brings up and keep the wedge's dark plumbing running. Carved, glow-stone-warm, and pointedly incurious: the Warren's one rule is that you carry the crate and never ask what sings inside it. They are paid a little better than deep-folk elsewhere, which is how the House buys their lack of questions.

rooms.name: The Carved Hall
rooms.purpose: a communal hall; a Petrocore shrine, a long stone table, and a house rule chalked on the wall: ASK NOTHING

rooms.name: Sleeping galleries
rooms.purpose: bunk-niches for ~40 haulers and conduit-wrights

structures.notes: ~40 Terran haulers & conduit-crew. Better-paid, better-fed, more silent than most under-halls — bought discretion has a texture of its own.

structures.name: The Blindside Canteen

position.depth_note: at the crossing of the galleries

structures.purpose: The under-city's warm room for the wedge, so named because the one thing you learn to do here is not see. Haulers, reckoners' guards, water-gate crews and lock-hands eat the same grey stew and trade the same careful nothing; the canteen-keeper feeds everyone, keeps everyone's secrets, and is the most trusted person in the district precisely because she sells nothing.

rooms.name: The Long Room
rooms.purpose: trestles, a great range, and no chalked names on the wall — here even the dead are discreet

rooms.name: Kitchen & store
rooms.purpose: run by the keeper

structures.notes: Canteen-keeper Mother Ollen + 3. Sister-room to the other wedges' under-canteens; their runners meet, and Sabreth's runner is the one who listens more than she talks.

structures.name: The Foreman's Post

position.depth_note: at the foot of the customs stair

structures.purpose: The seam-office where Sabreth's under-city answers to its over-city — but the foreman here reports to the Veilkeeper, not the customs hall, and the two counts he keeps are not honest-versus-official but public-versus-real. He is the man who knows exactly how much the House is lying, which is why he never, ever writes it down twice.

rooms.name: The Office
rooms.purpose: a ledger-desk, a burn-bowl, and a signal-cord to the Counting-Vault

rooms.name: Bunk
rooms.purpose: the foreman sleeps at the seam

structures.notes: Foreman Adley — the seam-keeper who reports up the wrong stair. Twin-but-inverted to the other wedges' foremen: he protects a secret rather than reconciling a wrong.

structures.name: The Veiled Water-Gate

position.depth_note: a hidden dock where a canal-branch meets the lock-water, under the Comet's Tail

structures.purpose: How a client of the Omen Court arrives and leaves without ever having crossed a terrace or passed a customs desk: a low, lamplit, covered dock where a curtained boat slips in from the lock-water, and a veiled passenger climbs a stair that comes out behind a false wall in the Comet's Tail. The single most useful architecture in the wedge, and the one the House would burn the district to keep off any map.

rooms.name: The Covered Dock
rooms.purpose: one boat-length of black water under a stone roof; no names spoken, no lamps bright

rooms.name: The Waiting Cells
rooms.purpose: curtained alcoves where clients wait unseen by one another; live-in gate-keepers who see everyone

structures.notes: 6 live-in gate-keepers/boatmen. The wedge's third novel space and the literal machinery of the 'beautiful open secret' — everyone knows the Court is here; no one can prove they came.

structures.name: The Nightside Bunks

position.depth_note: beside the warren

structures.purpose: The bunk-hall of the human and orc labour who walk the lock capstans, pole the client-boats, and do the House's heavier and less mentionable errands. Kept apart from the Terran warren by old habit; kept quiet by the same well-paid discretion. The muscle of a House that pretends its trade is only paper and starlight.

rooms.name: Bunk rows
rooms.purpose: riveted bunks for ~30; no window, and a foreman's whistle instead of a bell

rooms.name: The Cut-Room
rooms.purpose: where the boat-gangs are told their runs; a quiet, businesslike menace

structures.notes: ~30 human & orc labourers — the House's hands. Part of the unnamed 778; the ones who move the secrets and are the least allowed to keep their own.

structures.name: The Tideglass Tower

position.note: the Ilmyra rim tower — greybox tower i=4; stands at the dead back of the city, opposite the causeway

structures.purpose: Where Starfall reads the moons and the slow tide the Song makes in all still water. Not a tower of fixed certainties like Vael'Suran's but a tower of returns: everything it measures comes back around. Its instrument is a tall glass column of star-water whose level rises and falls a finger's breadth on the Song's long cycle, and the whole House's calendar of locks and festivals is set by watching it.

rooms.name: The Tideglass Hall
rooms.purpose: the great graduated water-column and its floating marker; the reading is taken at moonrise and moonset

rooms.name: The Moon-Room
rooms.purpose: an aperture aligned to the risings of the three moons; charts of their long braided cycle line the walls

rooms.name: Head's study
rooms.purpose: Magistra Vessa's study, its window framing the moon's path over the Mirror

rooms.name: Gaugers' room
rooms.purpose: junior gaugers reduce the tide-readings and copy the lock-tables the barge-masters buy

rooms.name: The Cistern-head & stair
rooms.purpose: the spiral stair; the tideglass is fed from the deep water far below by a single hair-fine pipe that must never be let run dry

structures.notes: Head + First Gauger + 4 live-in junior gaugers. Its lit finial is one of the greybox's nine rim domes; alone of the nine it is trimmed to burn brighter at the full moons.

structures.name: The Ilmyra Seat
structures.purpose: A damp, beautiful, rhythmic house built around an open moon-court — a shallow reflecting pool at its centre that is filled and drained on the tide-calendar, so the Seat is mirror-bright some weeks and a dry tiled basin others. Ilmyra money is barge money and lock-toll money, made from moving water and what floats on it, and the House lives by rise and fall the way other Houses live by rank.

rooms.name: The Moon-Court
rooms.purpose: an open inner court with a tiled reflecting pool, filled and drained to the calendar; the House takes its readings without leaving home

rooms.name: The Ebb Hall
rooms.purpose: reception; a frieze of the three moons in their braided cycle, and a tide-mark on the wall from the year the canals overtopped

rooms.name: Vessa's chambers
rooms.purpose: the matriarch's rooms, over the moon-court

rooms.name: Family wing
rooms.purpose: four chambers for the near family

rooms.name: Kitchen, stores, staff
rooms.purpose: household below and attic rooms for staff

structures.notes: Vessa + near family (5) + 12 household staff (incl. a pool-keeper whose whole post is the moon-court's filling and draining).

structures.name: Moonrise Villa — Sael
structures.purpose: The villa of the House's Tide-Lunist, whose sightline is surveyed not to the Mirror in general but to the exact point on the far rim where the largest moon clears the wall at midsummer. He argues the three moons and the Song's tide are one motion seen two ways, and that the lock-cycle is a liturgy nobody has noticed is a liturgy.

rooms.name: The Lunar Study
rooms.purpose: the moonrise sightline; a floor inlaid with the three moons' braided path

rooms.name: Family rooms
rooms.purpose: the Lunist, a companion, two children, one student

structures.notes: Tide-Lunist Orrin Sael + household. A theory-thread toward the Academy's Song-work, as the Serenthil horologist is.

structures.name: The Lock-Warden's Villa
structures.purpose: Home of the Lock-Warden, the commoner-born officer who actually times the great Lock-Flight and every canal sluice in the wedge — the man whose hand is on the city's whole water economy, and who has never once been asked to dine at the Seat. He keeps a working tide-model in his front room and trusts it further than any Magister.

rooms.name: The Model Room
rooms.purpose: a plumbed brass-and-glass model of the Lock-Flight he runs it by; it leaks, and he loves it

rooms.name: Family rooms (x3)
rooms.purpose: the Lock-Warden, spouse, 3 children

structures.notes: Lock-Warden Dov Marrenh + household. The Halvenor/Ostreth pattern — the commoner who really runs the House's work.

structures.name: The Pool House
structures.purpose: A villa given over almost entirely to a private tidal pool that its owner, a wealthy retired barge-mistress, fills from the canal-race so she can watch her own small tide turn each night. The upper terrace considers it vulgar to spend a sightline villa on water rather than a view; she considers the upper terrace to have never once looked at water properly.

rooms.name: The Private Pool
rooms.purpose: a roofed tidal pool, dark and still, that rises and falls on a bled-off share of the canal-race

rooms.name: Living rooms
rooms.purpose: the barge-mistress + a companion + two boarders + a servant

structures.notes: Retired barge-mistress Halvenna Oon + 4. New money from the barge trade, holding a sightline villa and using it wrong on purpose.

structures.name: The Lockwrights' Hall
structures.purpose: Wet, heavy, and essential: the guild that builds and maintains every lock-gate, sluice, valve and paddle in Starfall's water — hinges the size of a man, timber that must be kept swelled, seals of tallow and star-reed. A lock-gate that fails does not simply stop; it empties a terrace into the one below, so the Lockwrights are trusted with the city's actual weight of water and paid, grudgingly, accordingly.

rooms.name: The Gate Floor
rooms.purpose: great gates laid flat for fitting; a wet-pit for testing seals under head of water

rooms.name: The Paddle Shop
rooms.purpose: sluice-paddles and their gearing, cut to the Lock-Warden's tables

rooms.name: Master's dwelling
rooms.purpose: the master lockwright's family above the works

rooms.name: Journeymen's loft
rooms.purpose: boarded gate-wrights

structures.notes: Master lockwright Bruska Fenn + family + 9 journeymen. Works hand-in-glove with the under-city Lock-Gangs (IL-X03); half the Hall is up top, half its labour is down below.

structures.name: The Gaugers' House (Tide-Tables)
structures.purpose: Where the moons' braided cycle is turned into numbers a barge-master can use: the tide-tables and lock-timings for the season ahead, computed by hand and printed on the House's own press. Every barge that ever climbed to Starfall did it by a page bought here. Quiet, inky, and quietly powerful — to mis-set a table is to strand a season's cargo.

rooms.name: The Reckoning Floor
rooms.purpose: ranked desks of gaugers reducing the tideglass readings into tables

rooms.name: The Press Room
rooms.purpose: the House press; tide-tables, almanacs, lock-schedules struck in silver ink

rooms.name: Gaugers' dormitory
rooms.purpose: boarded gaugers

structures.notes: Chief gauger Present Ollav-Ree + 9. The mathematical twin of Serenthil's clock-work: one House counts the hour, this one counts the water.

structures.name: Lesser Watermen's Row
structures.purpose: Six joined houses of the wedge's lesser watermen — the sluice-tenders, gaugers' clerks, paddle-boys and canal-sweeps who keep the water moving without ever setting a table or holding a warrant. Respectable, damp, and paid in the House's steady lock-toll coin.

rooms.name: Per-house: work-room + 2 chambers
rooms.purpose: 6 households of watermen

structures.notes: 6 households, ~24 souls. Named: the sluice-tender Merrow, who can tell the tide's height by the sound the paddles make.

structures.name: The Drowned Moon
structures.purpose: The wedge's inn, right on the barge-basin, low enough that at the top of a spring tide the canal comes in over the sill and the regulars simply lift their feet onto the bench-rails and drink on. Bargefolk, lock-gangs off shift, and the occasional stranded traveller from the world below all wash up here. This wedge's Strain-relief haven, and the softest, wettest room in Starfall.

rooms.name: The Common Room
rooms.purpose: hearth, long tables with foot-rails against the flood; a tide-mark ladder painted up the doorframe and a drowned moon (a lantern) hung under glass

rooms.name: Letting rooms (x5)
rooms.purpose: five rooms above, above the flood-line

rooms.name: Cellar (wet)
rooms.purpose: half-flooded by design; the beer floats in cages, and a hatch opens onto the lock-flight below

structures.notes: Innkeeper Coll Marsh + 2 family + 2 staff. The wet cellar hatch is Ilmyra's over/under seam (to IL-X01). Sister-haven to the Sounding-Glass (VS-K01) and the Ninth Bell (SR-K01).

structures.name: The Barge-Basin & Chandlery

footprint.form: open water basin ringed by quays and shops

structures.purpose: The head of navigation: a broad turning-basin where the barges that climb the Lock-Flight tie up, unload, and turn, ringed by a quay of ship's-chandlers — rope, pitch, star-reed caulk, victuals, timber, and the tide-tables from the Gaugers' House. The one place in the visible city where the world-below arrives in the open, on the water, in daylight; and the House takes a toll on every keel.

rooms.name: The Basin & Quays
rooms.purpose: open star-water basin, mooring-rings, the toll-house with its warded strongbox

rooms.name: Chandlers' row
rooms.purpose: twelve chandler shops and stores, most with a family living above

structures.notes: 12 chandler households + toll-clerks, ~33 souls. Named: the caulk-and-reed dealer Pesh, and the toll-clerk Ammary who has memorised every barge-master's face.

structures.name: The Shrine of the Three Moons
structures.purpose: A shrine to Umbrion under his lunar aspect — three silver bowls of star-water set to catch the three moons, tended so their levels track the sky. Bargefolk pour a thimble of water in before a climb and take one out after a safe descent, so the bowls are a running ledger of the wedge's fear and gratitude. Devotions are timed to moonrise, not to the bell, which quietly annoys House Serenthil.

rooms.name: The Moon-Bowls
rooms.purpose: three tiered silver basins open to the sky; the water is never allowed to still completely

rooms.name: Keeper's cell
rooms.purpose: the shrine-keeper's room

structures.notes: Moon-keeper Senna + a mute apprentice. A watery counterpart to Vael'Suran's Deepening (VS-K03) — the same god, tended through water and moon instead of pure dark.

structures.name: Canal Dwellings — Basinside
structures.purpose: The wedge's densest housing, stacked three storeys over the basin: bargefolk families who work the water above the flood-line and the boatwrights, netmakers, and lightermen who serve the traffic. The ground floor is given to boats in winter and to children in summer, and the whole block reads the day by the height of the water at its door.

rooms.name: Per dwelling: 2-3 rooms
rooms.purpose: 9 dwellings, families of 3-6

structures.notes: ~50 souls. Named: the boatwright Oram, and the pilot-widow Cael, who guides new barge-masters up the flight for a coin and a story.

structures.name: The Tide-Hall

footprint.form: colonnaded hall around a great breathing pool

structures.purpose: The visible heart of the wedge and its 'novel and unique' landmark: a great colonnaded hall built around a circular pool of star-water that VISIBLY rises and falls — a full slow breath, floor to knee-height and back — over the Song's long tide-cycle, driven from the same deep water and lock-race that runs the whole city. Citizens come to sit at its rim and watch the water go out and come in, which is the nearest thing the Noctari have to prayer. At the flood it mirrors the whole hall; at the ebb it shows a mosaic floor of the three moons, dry, that no one sees but twice a month.

rooms.name: The Breathing Pool
rooms.purpose: the circular tidal pool and its ring of black basalt steps; a graduated pillar at the centre marks the reach of each tide

rooms.name: The Colonnade
rooms.purpose: a sheltered walk around the pool where the House holds the moon-festivals and the barge-blessings

rooms.name: The Sluice-Chapel
rooms.purpose: where the keeper controls the fill and drain; the machinery is treated as holy and kept behind a screen

structures.notes: Tide-Hall keeper Haldis + 5 (attendants who live in the colonnade cells). The BEAUTIFUL, ceremonial upper face of the water — its laboring lower face is the Lock-Flight (IL-X01) directly below. Same water, two faces: the Ilmyra doubling, mirroring Serenthil's festival-bell / shift-bell split.

structures.name: The Water-Gate & Back Landing
structures.purpose: The city's back door, where the lesser rear-processional meets the shore and the canal meets the star-lake through a warded water-gate. This is the customs post for everything that arrives by barge rather than by the front stair — the working threshold to Vael'Suran's ceremonial one across the caldera. What comes up the Lock-Flight is weighed and tallied here before the water is allowed to carry it into the city.

rooms.name: The Water-Gate Hall
rooms.purpose: the gate machinery, the weighing-quay, a tally-desk and warded strongroom

rooms.name: Officers' room
rooms.purpose: the water-customs officer and two clerks

structures.notes: Water-customs officer Trennt + 2 clerks (day post; counted at their canal homes). The back-door twin of the Vael'Suran/Serenthil front gates — but this door faces the WATER, and the water comes from below.

structures.name: The Lock-Flight

position.depth_note: a radial staircase of chamber-locks climbing up under the terraces from the world below

structures.purpose: The laboring lower face of all this beautiful water: a staircase of six great chamber-locks that lifts loaded barges from the cloud-world far below the caldera, chamber by chamber, up into the city's canals. Every stone, sack, cask and lamp that the terraces above consume climbs this flight in the dark, walked up by gangs on the paddle-capstans. The Plate draws the Tide-Hall's breathing pool and stops; it does not draw the six locks and the gangs directly beneath it that make the pretty water move at all.

rooms.name: The Six Chambers
rooms.purpose: the stepped lock-basins and their counter-weighted gates; a barge takes half a shift to climb the flight

rooms.name: The Capstan Galleries
rooms.purpose: side galleries where the lock-gangs walk the paddle-capstans that fill and empty each chamber

rooms.name: The Tally-Cut
rooms.purpose: the under-clerk's niche at the head of the flight, where the true cargo-count is kept in charcoal

structures.notes: Worked, not lived-in (its gangs bunk in IL-X03). The under-clerk keeps the Other Map's tally here. Directly beneath the Tide-Hall (IL-K05): same water, two faces — glory above, labour below.

structures.name: The Conduit-and-Sluice Gallery

position.depth_note: radial run beside the flight

structures.purpose: The wedge's Song-conduits that feed its star-lamps, run in the same gallery as the sluice-controls that time the Lock-Flight and the Tide-Hall's breathing. When a lamp burns on the terraces or the great pool draws its slow breath, the cause is a crew kneeling in this tunnel setting paddles and truing crystal in the dark.

rooms.name: The Long Gallery
rooms.purpose: conduit and sluice-rods side by side; access ladders to each terrace and to the lock-chambers

rooms.name: Sluice-house
rooms.purpose: the master sluice that sets the Tide-Hall's rise and fall — treated by the crew as the thing that must never be got wrong

structures.notes: Conduit-and-sluice crew (6, mixed Terran & human). They, not the moon, decide when the Tide-Hall breathes — a fact the worshippers above would rather not hold in mind.

structures.name: The Lock-Gangs' Hall

position.depth_note: cut into the shore-mass beside the flight

footprint.form: carved hall + riveted bunks, glow-stone lit

structures.purpose: Home of the gangs who work the Lock-Flight: Terran gate-wrights who keep the great gates swelled and true, alongside the human and orc haulers who walk the capstans that lift the barges. Damp, warm with glow-stone, and loud with running water through the wall. The proudest boast here is a flight climbed with no cargo lost, and the oldest hands can name every barge-master who ever thanked them and every one who never did.

rooms.name: The Carved Hall
rooms.purpose: a communal hall; a long table, a Petrocore shrine, and a wall-carving of the flight kept by the gate-wrights

rooms.name: Sleeping galleries
rooms.purpose: bunk-niches for ~52 gate-wrights and haulers

rooms.name: The Wet-Room
rooms.purpose: where soaked gear is dried and the drowned are laid out — the flight takes someone most seasons

structures.notes: ~24 Terran gate-wrights + ~28 human/orc haulers. Works hand-in-glove with the up-top Lockwrights' Hall (IL-L01). Part of the unnamed 778.

structures.name: The Bargefolk Undershelter
structures.type: transient dwelling (bargefolk of the world below)

position.depth_note: a long low shelter at the foot of the flight

structures.purpose: The liminal, half-counted population of the wedge: bargefolk from the cloud-world below who bring cargo up the flight and shelter here between climbs — people who are not quite of Starfall and never will be, who keep their own tongue, their own gods, and their families aboard. The city needs everything they carry and grants them nothing but this vaulted room and a moon-tinted view of the water they arrived on. The most foreign faces in Starfall, living directly under its most beautiful pool.

rooms.name: The Long Shelter
rooms.purpose: a vaulted dormitory of bunks and hammocks; families curtain off corners; a shrine to gods the terraces have never heard named

rooms.name: The Undermoorings
rooms.purpose: a covered basin where empty barges wait their turn down the flight

structures.notes: ~64 transient bargefolk (fluctuates with the season). A distinct outsider population — neither the elite above nor the settled under-city labour, but the road-people of the water. Rich quest and worldbuilding ground; part of the uncounted the whole game is about.

structures.name: The Slackwater Canteen

position.depth_note: at the gallery crossing above the flight

structures.purpose: The warm room where the under-city of the water eats: lock-gangs, sluice-crews, and bargefolk share one long trestle over fish from the lake-shore nets and bread come up the flight. Named for the slack of the tide, the still hour between rise and fall when the locks rest and everyone comes up to be fed. The keeper reads the tide by the draught under the door and rings no bell — she just knows when slackwater comes.

rooms.name: The Long Room
rooms.purpose: trestles, a great range, a wall of chalked names and a second wall of names in a script the terraces can't read

rooms.name: Kitchen & store
rooms.purpose: run by the keeper

structures.notes: Canteen-keeper Mother Ilse + 3 helpers. Sister-room to the Underspill (VS-X05) and the Undertoll (SR-X05); the three under-canteens' keepers are the real government of the dark.

structures.name: The Lockmaster's Post

position.depth_note: at the foot of the water-gate stair

structures.purpose: The seam-office of Ilmyra's under-city, at the foot of the stair up to the Water-Gate, where the flight's cargo-count and the drowned-count are reconciled and sent up to the House. The Lockmaster is the one person who both sets foot in the Tide-Hall's colonnade and knows the name of the last hauler the flight killed.

rooms.name: The Office
rooms.purpose: a ledger-desk, a soaked shift-book, a working model of the flight in a glass tank

rooms.name: Bunk
rooms.purpose: the Lockmaster sleeps at the seam, listening to the water

structures.notes: Lockmaster Vel — the seam of the water-wedge; keeps the honest count in charcoal and the House's in ink. Twin to Foreman Adric (VS-X06) and Foreman Quill (SR-X06).

structures.name: The Tower of the Empty Ring

position.note: the Corvane rim observatory — greybox tower i=5; aimed not at stars but at the dark between them

structures.purpose: Alone among the nine, this tower measures nothing. Its great instrument is trained on the deep field — the black gaps where no light is — and its records are ledgers of absence, columns of nothing observed, growing more precise each year. The other Houses light finials to be seen; Corvane's dome is the dimmest on the rim, on purpose, because you cannot read the dark by lamplight.

rooms.name: The Hall of the Empty Ring
rooms.purpose: ground instrument hall; a great ring-armature that frames a chosen patch of void and holds it steady for a lifetime of watching

rooms.name: The Ledger of Absence
rooms.purpose: a vault of black-bound books recording what was not there; the House's true wealth and its unease

rooms.name: Head's cell
rooms.purpose: Magister Vaelith's study — one chair, one shuttered slit, no lamp

rooms.name: The Counting Dark
rooms.purpose: where junior scholars reduce the night's non-observations; they work by touch and memory more than sight

rooms.name: The Aperture Chamber
rooms.purpose: top floor; the roof opens onto a single fixed patch of deep field; the reading is a long, cold act of not-looking-away

rooms.name: Servants' stair & the unlit lamp
rooms.purpose: the spiral stair; a finial that is kept, and cleaned, and never lit

structures.notes: Head works here, sleeps at the Seat. Senior observer + 5 live-in computers. The tower's dark dome is one of the nine on the greybox rim — the one visitors always mistake, at first, for the dead House.

structures.name: The Corvane Seat
structures.purpose: An austere seat with fewer windows than any House on the rim — Corvane does not decorate itself with the view, it studies what the view leaves out. The halls are kept deliberately underlit; guests learn to move by the sound of their own feet. It is a proud, hushed, faintly dreaded house, and the other Houses accept its invitations rarely and leave early.

rooms.name: The Unlit Hall
rooms.purpose: reception in near-dark; the walls hung with framed patches of empty sky, each labelled with a date and a nothing

rooms.name: Vaelith's chambers
rooms.purpose: the head's rooms; a window bricked up by a former head and never reopened

rooms.name: Family wing
rooms.purpose: three chambers for the near family, who are few — the House does not breed freely

rooms.name: The Listening Court
rooms.purpose: an open court roofed only by the deep field; the House sits here in silence at new-moon, together, saying nothing

rooms.name: Kitchen, stores, staff
rooms.purpose: the household below and in the attics

structures.notes: Magister Vaelith + near family (3) + 12 staff. The staff are paid above the rim's rate — Corvane servants are hard to keep.

structures.name: Villa of the Long Look
structures.purpose: Home of the scholar who has watched a single hand's-breadth of empty sky for two hundred and forty years, waiting for it to change. It has not. Her sightline is protected not toward the Mirror, like her neighbours', but past it and up, at nothing — a legal oddity the House court fought for decades to defend.

rooms.name: The Watching Room
rooms.purpose: a chair bolted to the floor at the one correct angle; a chart of a patch of dark, unchanged, re-inked yearly for the discipline of it

rooms.name: Living rooms
rooms.purpose: the scholar, a companion, two grown students

structures.notes: Magistra Ysoreth of the Long Look + household of 4. A study in devotion to the unrewarding — the House's whole ethos in one villa.

structures.name: The Warded Study
structures.purpose: The villa where the House keeps the theory it does not copy into the public halls — the dangerous mathematics of drawing the void toward you rather than merely watching it. Its door carries a real ward, and the Academy's own void-scholars visit it by night and sign no register. What is worked out here is a generation ahead of anything the Conclave has approved, and a generation is exactly long enough to be too late.

rooms.name: The Sealed Room
rooms.purpose: warded; the restricted theory in black ledgers chained to the shelf

rooms.name: Warden's rooms
rooms.purpose: the keeper of the study and a single trusted student

structures.notes: Magister Oren Corvane, keeper of the restricted theory, + household of 3. This is, quietly, where the intellectual seed of the Nullstone lives — the room the Academy borrows from without admitting it.

structures.name: The Vacant Villa
structures.purpose: The villa of a scholar who, thirty years ago, walked out to his watching-chair one clear night and was simply not there in the morning — no body, no note, the chart still weighted open. The House pays a caretaker to keep it exactly as he left it, and pays her not to speak of why.

rooms.name: The Room As Left
rooms.purpose: dusted daily, the chair still angled at the dark, the chart still open to the same page

rooms.name: Caretaker's room
rooms.purpose: the one warm corner of a cold house

structures.notes: Caretaker Nel, alone. A quiet horror the wedge does not discuss; a strong side-quest seed (what the chart was open to).

structures.name: The Hall of Negative Results
structures.purpose: Where the House's ledgers of absence are fair-copied, cross-checked and bound, and where its scribes lodge. To copy a Corvane ledger is to transcribe nothing, exactly, for a lifetime — a discipline that produces a particular kind of scribe: patient, unsmiling, and very hard to lie to. The most reliable hands in the city are trained here, and the strangest.

rooms.name: The Copying Dark
rooms.purpose: sloped desks under hooded lamps that light only the page, never the room

rooms.name: The Cross-Check Room
rooms.purpose: where two scribes read absence against absence to catch the single night someone saw something

rooms.name: Scribes' dormitory
rooms.purpose: 14 cots; the quietest sleepers in Starfall

structures.notes: Master-scribe Corriden + 14 scribes and lodgers. Twin in function to Vael'Suran's Scribes' Hall, opposite in temperament.

structures.name: The Black-Mirror Workshop
structures.purpose: Makers of the instruments that drink light instead of gathering it — black speculum mirrors, void-glass, the hooded lamps and light-baffles the whole wedge runs on. A wet, patient, slightly feared trade; the family that keeps it has learned to grind a mirror so dark it shows you the room behind your own head.

rooms.name: The Figuring Shed
rooms.purpose: pitch laps and the black-glass melt; a speculum is polished for months to hold a perfect nothing

rooms.name: The Proving Dark
rooms.purpose: a lightless room where a finished mirror is proved against the absence of any star

rooms.name: Family dwelling
rooms.purpose: the Vess family above the shed

structures.notes: Master mirror-wright Dela Vess + household + journeymen (10). The black-glass melt vents to an Under-Terrace flue.

structures.name: Lesser Scholars' Row
structures.purpose: Six joined houses of the wedge's lesser scholars — the reducers and copyists who serve the ledgers of absence without a watching-chair of their own. Sightless, sunless, and paid in the House's steady, cold coin. They keep, between them, a shared candle they light only for births and deaths.

rooms.name: Per-house: work-room + 2 chambers
rooms.purpose: 6 households

structures.notes: 6 households, ~20 souls. Named: the copyist Wren, who has begun, against every rule, to hope the dark she records will one day answer.

structures.name: The Last Lamp
structures.purpose: The wedge's inn, named for the single lamp the keeper swears he will never let go out — the joke and the comfort of a quarter that spends its days staring into the dark. Dimmer and quieter than any other inn in the city, but warmer for it; the place Corvane scholars come to be, for one evening, in a lit room full of noise.

rooms.name: The Common Room
rooms.purpose: hearth, low tables, the one lamp kept burning above the bar like a small defiance

rooms.name: Letting rooms (x5)
rooms.purpose: five rooms above

rooms.name: Cellar
rooms.purpose: canal-cooled store; a hatch to the Under-Terraces the keeper pretends not to know about

structures.notes: Innkeeper Halb Oren + 3 family + 2 staff. The cellar hatch is Corvane's over/under seam (to CV-X05).

structures.name: The Mourning Market
structures.purpose: The wedge's market leans, by long habit, into the House's temperament: sellers of black-glass and hooded lamps, of mourning-silks and grave-silver, of the still, dark things the rest of the city buys only when someone has died and then comes here to buy. Quietly, it is the richest market in Starfall — grief keeps steadier hours than fashion.

rooms.name: Per unit: shopfront + workshop + room above
rooms.purpose: 10 units, most with a family living above

structures.notes: 10 shops, ~28 souls. Named: the silversmith Made, who casts grave-tokens, and the lamp-hooder Sulen.

structures.name: The Deep Shrine of Umbrion
structures.purpose: Not a small shrine like the Vael'Suran Deepening but THE shrine — the great dark heart of Umbrion-worship in Starfall, tended by the House that understands the god best. You descend a black stair into a cold sphere and are asked to sit until the difference between your eyes open and closed stops mattering. The devout come out changed; a few do not come out at all until they are ready, and the shrine feeds them and waits.

rooms.name: The Descent
rooms.purpose: a black stair down; the last light is left at the top

rooms.name: The Sphere
rooms.purpose: a round dark cell where the void is offered as presence; a bowl of still star-water at the centre, found by memory

rooms.name: Keepers' cells
rooms.purpose: the shrine-keeper and two acolytes

structures.notes: Keeper Onn and two acolytes. The theological centre of the wedge's whole disposition — and of Elorin Voidweaver's own faith, though she is not from here.

structures.name: Canal Dwellings — Nightside
structures.purpose: The wedge's densest housing, on the shaded canal-bank that never takes the reflected lake-light — the artisans, lamp-hooders, mirror-wrights' families and canal-hands who keep the dark quarter running. A close, quiet, watchful block; neighbours here know each other's silences.

rooms.name: Per dwelling: 2-3 rooms
rooms.purpose: 9 dwellings, families of 3-6

structures.notes: ~44 souls, including the customs officer's household (counted here, works at the shore post CV-S01). Named: the widow Oll, who reads the ledger of absence for pleasure.

structures.name: The Watcher's House
structures.purpose: A narrow canal-side house belonging to an amateur — a retired lamp-hooder who taught himself the House's discipline and now keeps, from his own roof, a private ledger of a patch of dark no scholar bothers with. The House tolerates him; one or two of its magisters quietly check his numbers.

rooms.name: Ground room
rooms.purpose: the family's living space

rooms.name: The roof-watch
rooms.purpose: a home-made ring-armature and a stool; his life's second work

structures.notes: Old Pell + household of 4. Proof the House's obsession is contagious; a warm side-character.

structures.name: The Corvane Canal & its bridge

position.note: the wedge's stretch of the third greybox canal

structures.purpose: Star-water — black, still, and here so untroubled by lamplight that the Corvane canal is the one stretch where you can lean over the parapet and see the deep field doubled in the water at your feet. One plain stone bridge crosses it. People come from other wedges to look, and leave quickly.
structures.notes: The canal drains to the Nightbarge Lock below (CV-X01). Its unnatural stillness is a small local legend.

structures.name: The Still Shore & Customs Post
structures.purpose: The Corvane stretch of the black basalt strand is the quietest shore in Starfall, and the one people come to when they need to look a long time into the Mirror without being spoken to. The House keeps a customs post here for the goods that come up from below — and, unofficially, a bench, because someone should be near when a person stands too long at the water's edge.

rooms.name: The Weighing Hall
rooms.purpose: scales, tally-desks, a wardsealed strongroom

rooms.name: Officers' room
rooms.purpose: the customs officer and a clerk; a lantern kept for the shore, not the desk

structures.notes: Day post; the officer's household is counted at CV-K04. The unofficial watch over the water's edge is a quiet, humane note in a grim wedge.

structures.name: The Nightbarge Lock

position.depth_note: beneath the canal quarter

structures.purpose: The chamber-lock that lifts cargo barges from the world below into the Corvane canal. The wedge's stone, black-glass sand, ledger-paper and grave-silver all rise through here on chain-gangs. The lock-crews say the water in this lock is stiller than any other — that it does not want to be disturbed — and they work it fast and speak little.

rooms.name: The Lock Chamber
rooms.purpose: the flooding basin and the counter-weighted gates

rooms.name: The Capstan Floor
rooms.purpose: where the lift-gangs walk the capstans

rooms.name: Tally hole
rooms.purpose: the under-clerk's niche; the real ledger, in charcoal

structures.notes: Worked, not lived-in. Lock-master Grael keeps the honest tally the Plate does not.

structures.name: The Conduit Gallery

position.depth_note: runs radially under the terraces

structures.purpose: The tuned crystal conduits that carry the Song up to the wedge's few, dim star-lamps run through here, tended in the dark by crews who barely need lamps of their own. In the Corvane gallery the conduit-wrights report a thing they will not put in writing: that here, nearer the House's watching, the Song runs a shade fainter, as if something a long way off were beginning, very slightly, to listen the other way.

rooms.name: The Long Gallery
rooms.purpose: the conduit run; access ladders to each terrace's lamp-stems

rooms.name: Tuning niches (x4)
rooms.purpose: where conduit-wrights kneel to true the crystal

structures.notes: Worked by conduit-wrights (home at the Warren). The faint-Song detail is quiet foreshadowing of the Silence — a thing measured and not believed.

structures.name: The Deep-Wrights' Warren

position.depth_note: cut into the shore-mass

structures.purpose: Home and hall of the Terran stone-wrights who cut and hold up the Corvane under-terraces — and who like this posting least of all the wedges, because the deep folk feel the House's dark in the rock and say the stone here 'keeps its own counsel.' They cut fast, shore hard, and keep their glow-stone burning a little brighter than they need to.

rooms.name: The Carved Hall
rooms.purpose: a communal hall, warm with glow-stone; the deep folk crowd the light here more than in other wedges

rooms.name: Sleeping galleries
rooms.purpose: bunk-niches for the wrights and the conduit crews

rooms.name: The Shrine of Petrocore
rooms.purpose: a Stone-Voice shrine; here, unusually, it is never left unlit

structures.notes: Warren-elder Bruk + ~43 deep-wrights + a 6-strong conduit crew. The one place in the wedge that insists on light.

structures.name: The Silent Bunks

position.depth_note: beside the lock

structures.purpose: The bunk-hall of the orc and human lift-gangs who walk the Nightbarge capstans. It is called the Silent Bunks because sound carries strangely this deep under the Corvane watching, and the crews have simply given up on noise; they sign to each other, and sleep hard, and count the days to a transfer that rarely comes.

rooms.name: Bunk rows
rooms.purpose: riveted double-bunks; no window, and here no one jokes about wanting one

rooms.name: The Collar-room
rooms.purpose: where shift-tallies are logged — the same bureaucratic horror as every wedge, quieter

structures.notes: ~46 orc and human labourers. Named: the elder Vosk, who has taught the whole hall a hand-language. Part of the unnamed 778.

structures.name: The Underhush Canteen

position.depth_note: at the gallery crossing

structures.purpose: The warm room of the Corvane under-city, and the loudest place in the whole dark wedge on purpose — the canteen-keeper bangs her pots, keeps three lamps, and will not have silence at her tables, because she has watched what the quiet does to people down here and decided to fight it with soup and noise.

rooms.name: The Long Room
rooms.purpose: trestles, a great range, three lamps kept deliberately bright, a wall of chalked names

rooms.name: Kitchen & store
rooms.purpose: run by the keeper

structures.notes: Canteen-keeper Mama Dren + 5 helpers. Knows the other wedges' canteen-keepers by their runners; the Last Lamp's cellar hatch surfaces near here.

structures.name: The Foreman's Post

position.depth_note: at the foot of the customs stair

structures.purpose: The seam-office of the Corvane under-city, where the shift-count is reconciled and sent up to the House. The foreman here is the only one of the wedge's overseers who has ever sat a night in the Void Chamber, and the crews trust him more for it and fear him a little.

rooms.name: The Office
rooms.purpose: a ledger-desk, a lamp, a locked shift-book

rooms.name: Bunk
rooms.purpose: the foreman sleeps at the seam

structures.notes: Foreman Ist — keeps the honest count in charcoal and the House's in ink. Twin to the foremen of every wedge.

structures.name: The Void Chamber

position.depth_note: the deepest room in the wedge, cut directly beneath the tower's sightline

footprint.form: a hollow sphere within a cube of shore-mass

structures.purpose: The House's greatest and least-spoken-of work: a perfect hollow sphere cut deep under the tower's own sightline, lined so that no light and almost no sound survive it. Initiates sit inside, one at a time, for as long as they can bear — hours, days — until, the House says, they stop needing light to think, and begin to hear the shape of the dark the way the tower above only measures it. It is where Corvane theory stops being mathematics and becomes something closer to prayer, or preparation.

rooms.name: The Antechamber
rooms.purpose: where the last lamp is surrendered and the initiate waits to be led in by touch

rooms.name: The Sphere
rooms.purpose: the anechoic void itself; no light, no echo, no floor you can feel the edge of; a single seat at the centre

rooms.name: Attendants' cells
rooms.purpose: the keeper and initiates who live at the chamber's mouth, tending those inside

structures.notes: The wedge's novel landmark and a future hero set-piece. This is the room that taught the student Elorin Voidweaver to look into the dark without flinching — she sat the Sphere young, and it made her, and it is a straight line from this seat to the Nullstone. The under-city here is unusually quiet, as if the Sphere's silence leaks into the surrounding rock.

structures.name: The Barge-Hands' Bunks

position.depth_note: along the barge gallery

structures.purpose: A second labour hall for the barge-hands and haulers who move cargo along the under-gallery from the lock to the terrace hoists — mostly human and orc, worked in long shifts, housed deep. They are the muscle that turns the pretty stillness of the Corvane canal into food on rim tables, and no one on the rim could name a single one of them.

rooms.name: Bunk rows
rooms.purpose: riveted bunks for the haul-gangs

rooms.name: The Gear-store
rooms.purpose: harness, hooks, hand-carts; a shift-board by the door

structures.notes: ~42 human and orc haulers. Part of the unnamed 778. Named: the hauler Renk, who is teaching himself the deep-wrights' letters.

structures.name: The Struck Tower

position.note: the dead House's rim tower — greybox tower i=6; dome dark, sigil scraped from the ring, name unsaid

structures.purpose: The unlit tower, its dome struck through with a single black shard, its sigil scraped down to bare stone by a hand that never explained itself. The great door is sealed — not by the city, but from the inside, which no one likes to mention. Eight domes go on burning around the gap it leaves and no one has ever proposed relighting the ninth. Some absences are load-bearing.

rooms.name: The sealed door
rooms.purpose: barred from within; the bar has never been found from without, and no one has tried hard

rooms.name: The scraped ring
rooms.purpose: the stone panel where the House sigil was; you can still feel the ghost of it with a fingertip

rooms.name: The dark drum
rooms.purpose: unknown; the interior is unseen in living memory. Children dare each other to knock and run

structures.notes: The mystery anchor of the wedge. WHY the House died is unresolved — sealed from inside, scraped, unnamed. Do not answer it. Its extinguished finial is the greybox's one dead rim dome.

structures.name: The Hollow Seat
structures.type: abandoned manor, now a squatted commons
structures.purpose: The dead House's great seat, left open when the House ended and never reclaimed — so the wedge took it. Where a magister once received sightline-suits, the community now holds its loose, argued, unofficial council under the same cold coffered ceiling, and anyone may speak. It is the nearest thing the wedge has to a government, and it governs by not quite deciding.

rooms.name: The Open Hall
rooms.purpose: the old reception; now a commons with a hearth built crookedly into a fireplace meant only for show

rooms.name: The Reeve's corner
rooms.purpose: where the Unwarden keeps her ledger of favours owed both ways; the only tally in the wedge kept in the open

rooms.name: Squatters' chambers
rooms.purpose: the family wing, partitioned with hung cloth into a dozen homes

rooms.name: The cold-court
rooms.purpose: the roofless observing court; someone has planted vegetables in it, which no true House would ever have allowed

structures.notes: Head of the wedge is an INFORMAL elder, not a magister. The over-city grandeur repurposed for the under-city's people — the wedge's whole thesis in one building.

structures.name: The Roofless Row
structures.purpose: Sightline villas that no one maintains, because a protected sightline is worth nothing when there is no House court to enforce it. Two have lost their roofs and stand open to the sky, which the squatters below them have decided to call a skylight. Rank once measured in windows; here the windows are free, and so is the rank.

rooms.name: Per villa: what's left
rooms.purpose: 5 shells; the two roofless ones tarped over in the rains, prized in the dry season for the view

structures.notes: The upper terrace inverted: the elite band become the cheapest rooms in the city, and the sightline — the whole point of the district — is worthless the moment no one is keeping the ledger.

structures.name: The Last Villa
structures.purpose: The one villa still kept as it was — swept, shuttered, its sightline clear — by the last servant of the dead House, who stayed when everyone else was told to go and was never told why. He is very old even for a Noctari, and he remembers the House's name, and he has kept the single promise he ever kept in his life, which was to never say it.

rooms.name: The Kept Study
rooms.purpose: dusted daily; the sightline clear to the Mirror, aimed at nothing anyone can name

rooms.name: The Sealed Cabinet
rooms.purpose: the House papers, he says; he has not opened it in three hundred years and will not

rooms.name: Rooms
rooms.purpose: the old servant and two who look after him now that he cannot

structures.notes: The mystery's living keeper. Drops the atmosphere of a secret without the secret. He knows and will not say; the wedge lets him be.

structures.name: The Cloth Terrace
structures.purpose: Three grand villas long since subdivided with hung cloth and salvaged board into perhaps twenty small homes, their old sightlines shared out room by room like slices of a great pale cake. Washing crosses between the columns. It is, quietly, one of the pleasanter places to live in Starfall, which is precisely the kind of thing that does not get onto a Plate.

rooms.name: Per home: a partition & a window-share
rooms.purpose: ~20 small homes; sightlines held in common, unmeasured and unenforced

structures.notes: Freedom rendered as architecture: the sightline, once a possession, becomes a commons.

structures.name: The Menders' Yard
structures.purpose: There is no chartered guild in a wedge with no House to charter one, so the fixers chartered themselves. Anything broken in the whole city that isn't worth a real guild's price comes here — cracked lenses re-ground rough, dead clocks made to lie convincingly, salvage from the other eight wedges given a second life. Skilled, unlicensed, and cheaper than anyone admits to using.

rooms.name: The Yard
rooms.purpose: open working court; a mountain of other people's discards, sorted with obsessive care

rooms.name: The Fixing Sheds
rooms.purpose: benches for glass, metal, clockwork, cloth — one mender to a trade, all self-taught

rooms.name: Menders' dwelling
rooms.purpose: the yard's families above and behind the sheds

structures.notes: The wedge's real economy — the city depends on it and does not name it. The other Houses send work here through intermediaries who pretend they didn't.

structures.name: The Free School
structures.purpose: A school with no charter, no fee, and no god — where anyone who knows a thing teaches it to anyone who wants it, an hour at a time, letters and numbers and the reading of stars to people the Academy would never enrol. It is the most subversive building in Starfall and looks like a draughty room with a slate wall, because that is what it is.

rooms.name: The Slate Room
rooms.purpose: one wall painted black and written on daily; benches salvaged from the Menders' Yard

rooms.name: Teacher's rooms
rooms.purpose: the teacher and a few boarded pupils with nowhere else

structures.notes: The humane heart of the wedge. Teaches literacy to the unlicensed and the under-city — the exact thing the beautiful city is built on NOT doing. A natural early-Elorin beat (she 'first sees' what the institution refuses to see).

structures.name: The Unnumbered Row
structures.purpose: A long terrace of small houses that appear on no rent-roll, because the roll died with the House and no one ever wrote another. The people here are the fled, the discreetly poor, the between-things — those who came to the dead House's wedge precisely because it is the one place in the city where you are not counted, taxed, tallied, or watched.

rooms.name: Per house: 2-3 rooms
rooms.purpose: ~9 households; nobody asks the next door's name unless offered

structures.notes: The district of the un-measured. To live here is to be off the Plate on purpose.

structures.name: The Blind Lamp
structures.purpose: The wedge's taphouse, named for the dead star-lamp over its door that has never once been lit in living memory — the Song does not come cleanly to a wedge whose House stopped paying to route it. So the Blind Lamp burns cheap tallow instead, which is illegal, which is the point. Rougher than the Sounding-Glass or the Ninth Bell, and warmer than either.

rooms.name: The Tallow Room
rooms.purpose: real flame, real smoke, real shadows; the one room in Starfall lit like the world below

rooms.name: Kitchen & cellar
rooms.purpose: the cellar stair goes straight down to the Open Stair — here there is no grille, no seam, no pretending

rooms.name: Letting rooms (x4)
rooms.purpose: four rooms above, let by the night to whoever, no name asked

structures.notes: This wedge's Strain-relief haven. The unlit lamp is a quiet, precise symbol: the light the rest of the city takes for granted was never free — it was a service the dead House stopped buying.

structures.name: The Unmarket
structures.purpose: A market that keeps no hours because there is no bell to keep them by and no House to charge a stall-fee. It runs on barter as much as coin, sells the salvage of the Menders' Yard and the produce of the cold-courts, and asks no questions about the provenance of anything. Serenthil sells time to the death; the Unmarket gives it away.

rooms.name: The Sprawl
rooms.purpose: barrows, cloth-shaded pitches, a barter-post where debts are chalked and rubbed out by trust

structures.notes: The economic mirror of the Hour-Market across the city: no hours, no fees, no measure. The un-timed market of the un-timed House.

structures.name: The Empty Niche
structures.purpose: A shrine built around an absence: a stone niche with no idol in it, no name over it, and one worn place on the floor where people kneel anyway. Some come for the dead House. Some come for their own erased and unspoken things. The keeper does not ask which, because the keeper's own name was struck from a ledger long ago too, and never restored.

rooms.name: The Niche
rooms.purpose: an empty carved recess; offerings left are small, wordless, and never idols

rooms.name: Keeper's cell
rooms.purpose: the nameless keeper's room

structures.notes: Novel: a shrine TO erasure itself, in a city of gods of light and shadow. The theological answer to the whole wedge — you can worship an absence, and people do.

structures.name: Canal Dwellings — the Mingle
structures.purpose: The densest housing in the wedge, and the only place above ground in all Starfall where Noctari, human, Terran and orc keep house side by side as a matter of course rather than a scandal — because the House that would have forbidden it is dead, and no one has troubled to invent the rule again. The over-city calls it the Mingle, and does not visit.

rooms.name: Per dwelling: 2-4 rooms
rooms.purpose: ~12 dwellings stacked four deep, families of every race and several of no single one

structures.notes: The wedge's central humane fact: the segregation the rest of the city enforces simply lapsed here. The Under-Terraces' mixed halls, but above ground and by choice.

structures.name: The Common Wash
structures.purpose: A wash-house on the canal, steam-warm, where the wedge does its laundry and, incidentally, most of its living — births are announced here, disputes settled, the sick minded. It was a House bath-house once. The community keeps the boiler going by collective agreement and no small effort, and treats it as the nearest thing they have to a temple that works.

rooms.name: The Steam Hall
rooms.purpose: stone tubs, a scavenged boiler, benches worn smooth by gossip

rooms.name: The Minding Room
rooms.purpose: a warm back room where the sick and the newborn are kept; the wash-women take turns

structures.notes: Humane detail: the mutual-aid of a place with no institutions doing the institutions' job, warmer than any of them.

structures.name: The Untended Gate
structures.purpose: Where the dead House's processional foot meets the shore stands a customs post with no customs officer — the House that appointed one is gone, and the Conclave never bothered to replace the post over a wedge worth nothing to tax. So the community keeps a volunteer at the door, not to weigh goods but to warn the wedge who is coming down the stair. The one gate in Starfall that watches the over-city, and not the under.

rooms.name: The Empty Weighing Hall
rooms.purpose: scales long since sold; the strongroom stands open and is used to store the wash-house coal

rooms.name: The Watcher's stool
rooms.purpose: one chair by the door, kept warm in shifts by whoever the wedge can spare

structures.notes: The customs post inverted: it exists to watch the rich descend, not to tax the poor ascending. Structurally twins Vael'Suran's and Serenthil's official gates, and refutes them.

structures.name: The Open Stair

position.depth_note: runs from the canal quarter straight down into the under-terraces, unbarred

structures.purpose: Everywhere else in Starfall the two cities meet at a locked seam — a grille, a customs door, a foreman's post. Here the stair between the terraces and the under-terraces simply stands open, and always has, because the House that kept the door shut is dead and no one rehung it. People go up and down it carrying laundry and gossip and bread. It is the single most quietly radical object in the city: a door that isn't there.

rooms.name: The Stair
rooms.purpose: broad worn steps, no gate, lit at the turns by tallow because the conduits here are failing

structures.notes: The wedge's thesis made into architecture: the two-map divide physically broken. The 'Other Map' and the Plate share a staircase here, and neither minds.

structures.name: The Slack Lock

position.depth_note: beneath the canal quarter

structures.purpose: The wedge's barge lock still works, because the city below still needs a way up whether the House above it lives or dies — but it runs slack and half-idle, worked by volunteers off the Mingle when a barge comes, not by a chained gang on a bell. It lifts less than any lock in the city and is, by every account of the people who work it, the only pleasant one to crew.

rooms.name: The Lock Chamber
rooms.purpose: the basin and gates; worked when needed, quiet when not

rooms.name: The Capstan Floor
rooms.purpose: no chain-gang; the capstans walked by whoever the wedge sends, for a share of the cargo

structures.notes: Worked, not lived-in; crewed from the Undercroft Bunks (DH-X04). The labour that is compulsion elsewhere is cooperative here.

structures.name: The Failing Gallery

position.depth_note: radial run under the terraces

structures.purpose: The Song-conduits that should light the wedge's star-lamps, kept barely alive by a crew too small for the work since the House stopped funding it. The crystal goes untuned, the light fails terrace by terrace, and that is exactly why the wedge burns tallow above — the failing gallery is the reason the Blind Lamp is blind. They keep the last few conduits singing out of stubbornness and to sell a little light to the Menders.

rooms.name: The Dimming Run
rooms.purpose: conduits going dark one by one; the crew tunes what they can reach and mourns the rest

rooms.name: Crew niche
rooms.purpose: where the conduit-crew sleep beside their failing charge

structures.notes: Concrete cause of the wedge's darkness: light in Starfall was always a service that had to be paid for, and this House stopped paying. Decay you can see the reason for.

structures.name: The Undercroft Bunks

position.depth_note: cut beneath the mid terraces

structures.purpose: A bunk-hall like the other wedges' — except that here no one is confined to it. With the Open Stair unbarred and the Mingle open above, the under-dwellers who work the lock and the gallery live below by choice, habit, or the plain warmth of glow-stone, and go up whenever they please. It is the same architecture of segregation as the other wedges, emptied of its cruelty and left standing as merely a home.

rooms.name: The Carved Hall
rooms.purpose: a communal hall; the same long table as every under-hall, but the door out is never locked

rooms.name: Sleeping galleries
rooms.purpose: bunk-niches, many of them empty now that people may live above if they like

structures.notes: The same structure the other wedges use to keep labour out of sight — here rendered harmless by the simple fact that the door is open. Houses the lock and gallery crews.

structures.name: The Open Table

position.depth_note: at the foot of the Open Stair

structures.purpose: The under-canteen of the wedge, set where the Open Stair lands — so that, uniquely in Starfall, the people from above and the people from below eat at one table without a wall or a rule between them. The same grey good stew as every under-canteen; the difference is who is allowed to sit.

rooms.name: The Long Room
rooms.purpose: trestles under the stairhead; a wall of chalked names shared between over and under, which no other wedge's wall is

rooms.name: Kitchen
rooms.purpose: run by the keeper on donated stores

structures.notes: Sister-room to the Underspill (VS-X05) and the Undertoll (SR-X05) — but here the over-city sits down too. The one integrated table in the city.

structures.name: The Empty Post

position.depth_note: at the seam where a foreman would sit

structures.purpose: Every other wedge has a foreman at the seam, keeping one honest ledger and one dishonest one and knowing they differ. This wedge's post stands empty — the House that would appoint the overseer is dead — and the astonishing, quietly damning fact the over-city cannot afford to notice is that the work still gets done. One volunteer keeps a single open tally on the desk that no one above demands and no one below resents.

rooms.name: The Ledger Desk
rooms.purpose: one book, kept in the open, in one hand, honest because no one is made to lie to it

structures.notes: The wedge's sharpest political point: remove the overseer and the labour organizes itself and works anyway. Twins the Foreman's Posts (VS-X06, SR-X06) and refutes their necessity.

structures.name: The Drowned Terrace

position.depth_note: a whole service level that flooded when the pumps stopped

structures.purpose: A service terrace that drowned when the dead House's pumps fell silent and no one paid to restart them — a still black flood standing waist-deep among the pillars, roofed by the living wedge above. The community did not drain it. They learned to use it: they fish the star-water for the pale blind things that breed in it, the children swim in the warm dark, and the flood doubles the tallow-light into a low uncanny second city that is not on even the Other Map.

rooms.name: The Flood
rooms.purpose: waist-deep still water among pillars; punted, fished, swum; the drowned doorways lead nowhere anyone returns from

rooms.name: The Fishers' ledge
rooms.purpose: a dry shelf where the fisher-folk of the flood keep their nets and their homes

structures.notes: Novel & eerie & tied to the House's death (the pumps stopped when the House did). A place beneath the 'Other Map' itself — a third city no map contains. Strong future set-piece; leaves an unanswered edge (the drowned doorways).

structures.name: The Horizon Tower

position.note: the Duskmere rim observatory — greybox tower i=7; also the city's landward beacon

structures.purpose: Alone among the nine, this tower half-turns its back on the Mirror to watch the rim of the world instead — every rising and every setting, the exact degree at which a star first clears the cloud-sea and the exact degree at which it drowns. Its lamp is not only a finial but a beacon, the highest light in Starfall and the first thing a traveller climbing the outer stair sees for two days.

rooms.name: The Rising Hall
rooms.purpose: ground instrument floor; a low horizon-quadrant ringed to the walls, aimed outward not down

rooms.name: The Ephemeris of Departures
rooms.purpose: the register of first-and-last lights; travellers pay to have an auspicious hour named for setting out

rooms.name: Head's Study
rooms.purpose: Magister Corvenn's study; the only one in the House that faces outward, over the stair

rooms.name: The Beacon Room
rooms.purpose: where the great landward lamp is trimmed and shuttered; a code of shutterings tells the stair-foot what weather waits above

rooms.name: The Setting Chamber
rooms.purpose: top floor; the outward aperture; the reading of last-light is taken standing in the wind off the cloud-sea

rooms.name: Watch-stair & lamp-loft
rooms.purpose: the spiral stair; the beacon is tended in shifts through the night

structures.notes: First Watcher + 6 live-in watchers/beacon-keepers. The beacon doubles as the greybox rim finial; it also faces outward, the one lamp that looks away from the city.

structures.name: The Duskmere Seat

footprint.faces: outward (toward the rim gate and the stair)

structures.purpose: The only House seat arranged around a view of the way out rather than the Mirror — a house built for leaving, hung with the maps of roads no other House keeps and the trophies of journeys down. Half its rooms are always shut, their people away; the family measures its status not in windows but in how far its members have gone and come back.

rooms.name: The Hall of Roads
rooms.purpose: reception; a floor inlaid with the outer roads, worn palest where the family walks its own routes in thought

rooms.name: Corvenn's chambers
rooms.purpose: the head's rooms, facing the beacon and the stair-head

rooms.name: The Shut Wing
rooms.purpose: chambers of the family who are travelling; kept aired and ready, sometimes for decades

rooms.name: The Returns Court
rooms.purpose: a court with a single lit lamp burning for whoever is on the road — put out only when all are home, which is almost never

rooms.name: Kitchen & stores
rooms.purpose: below the hall; provisioned for departures as much as meals

rooms.name: Staff quarters
rooms.purpose: attic rooms for the household

structures.notes: Corvenn + resident family (5) + 10 staff. The Returns lamp is the House's soul: a light kept for the absent.

structures.name: The Stair-Head Gatehouse

position.note: crowns the outer switchback stair where it meets the rim — the plate's zigzag line off the edge starts here

structures.purpose: The one land gate of Starfall: a fortified house straddling the top of the long outer switchback stair, the only walked road down to the world far below the cloud-sea. Everything and everyone that does not come up a barge-lock comes through here — counted, tolled, and named in the gate-book. Its double portcullis is warded shut at the ninth bell, and after that the city is, quite literally, unreachable by foot.

rooms.name: The Passage
rooms.purpose: the warded gate-tunnel; two portcullises with a killing-dark between, a relic of a fear no living Noctari remembers the cause of

rooms.name: The Gate-Book Hall
rooms.purpose: where every arrival is named and every departure marked; the most complete list of who is in the city that exists — and it lists no one from below

rooms.name: The Toll Room
rooms.purpose: gate-customs on foot-traffic and pack-loads; the strongroom under it

rooms.name: Guard barracks
rooms.purpose: the resident gate-guard company; the only standing armed body in a city that pretends it needs none

rooms.name: The Beacon-mirror loft
rooms.purpose: answers the Horizon Tower's shutter-code down the stair to the way-stations

structures.notes: Gate-serjeant Ollun-Rekk + a resident guard company of 11. The gate-book is a quiet theme-piece: the city's official census of souls, which by design cannot see the Under-Terraces or the world below.

structures.name: Sightline Villa — the Warden's House
structures.purpose: Home of the Warden of the Stair, the commoner-born officer who actually holds the gate and the descent — a heavier authority than any House head, because the Warden decides who comes into the city at all. Keeps a sightline to the Mirror out of rank and never once looks at it; the window that matters faces the stair.

rooms.name: The Duty Study
rooms.purpose: the gate-rosters, the toll-ledgers, a spyglass trained down the switchbacks

rooms.name: Family rooms
rooms.purpose: the Warden, a spouse, two children, a ward taken off the stair years ago

structures.notes: Warden Hesk Ollun + household of 5. Real power in the wedge; the House defers to the Warden and resents it.

structures.name: Sightline Villa — the Caravan-Master's House
structures.purpose: A rim villa bought — scandalously, with trade money — by a retired human caravan-master who spent sixty years hauling up the stair and now owns a view the old blood thinks he has no right to. He keeps the door open and the wine good, and the House cannot afford to snub him, because he still owns half the mule-lines.

rooms.name: The Map Room
rooms.purpose: walls of trade-roads; the sightline used, unusually, to actually look at the lake

rooms.name: Living rooms
rooms.purpose: Tovek, his wife, a grandchild, a manservant

structures.notes: Caravan-master Tovek Sarn (human) + household. New money on the rim — an affront and a fact. Side-quest seed: buying respectability.

structures.name: Sightline Villa — the Empty House
structures.purpose: A Duskmere villa whose whole family is a decade into a survey of the drowned coasts and is not expected back this generation. A caretaker keeps the lamp, dusts the instruments, and answers the door to no one — the most enviable sightline in the wedge, held by an empty house and a woman who is not allowed to sit at its window.

rooms.name: The Shrouded Study
rooms.purpose: instruments under cloth; the sightline unused for eleven years

rooms.name: Caretaker's rooms
rooms.purpose: the caretaker and her three lodgers, who are not supposed to be there

structures.notes: Caretaker Nell + 3 quiet lodgers she takes rent from and does not report. A wedge of departures leaves houses like this everywhere.

structures.name: The Wayfarers' Hall
structures.purpose: The guild of guides, road-cartographers and stair-pilots — the people who know the switchbacks in fog, the safe camps, the season the lower road floods. They draw the maps no Plate would deign to include (the outward roads, the world below) and lodge the guild's own in the floors above. The one hall in Starfall where the city is treated as a place you leave.

rooms.name: The Road-Room
rooms.purpose: long tables of outward maps; a relief-model of the whole switchback stair in carved slate

rooms.name: The Pilots' Register
rooms.purpose: who is licensed to guide the descent; a stair-pilot's word is worth a House seal down below

rooms.name: Guild dormitory
rooms.purpose: lodging for pilots between runs; cots that smell of the outside

structures.notes: Guild-warden Ilsa Wend + 12 lodged pilots/cartographers. The Road-Room's outward maps are the over-city cousin of the Under-Terraces' 'Other Map' — knowledge the Plate refuses.

structures.name: The Gatewrights' Court
structures.purpose: Where the gate-mechanisms, the portcullis counterweights, the mule-harness and the stair's iron are made and mended — the heavy, greasy trade that keeps the one door working. A family firm that has held the gate-contract for four generations and guards its winch-designs like a House guards a sightline.

rooms.name: The Iron Shed
rooms.purpose: forge, winch-benches, the great counterweight-jigs

rooms.name: The Harness Room
rooms.purpose: mule-tack and stair-litters for the loads too heavy to carry

rooms.name: Family dwelling
rooms.purpose: the Rekk family above the forge

rooms.name: The Court
rooms.purpose: open assembly yard for gate-iron

structures.notes: Master gatewright Dorn Rekk + household + journeymen. Kin to the gate-serjeant; the Rekks are the gate, above and below.

structures.name: Doorkeepers' Row
structures.purpose: Six joined houses of the wedge's doorkeepers — gate-clerks, toll-tallymen, stair-lamplighters and the runners who carry the gate-book's news up to the House. Respectable, sightless service to the threshold; they know everyone's comings and goings and are paid to forget them.

rooms.name: Per-house: work-room + 2 chambers
rooms.purpose: 6 households

structures.notes: 6 households, ~22 souls. Named: toll-tallyman Vess, who has memorised every face that came up the stair in forty years and never once written a name he was paid to lose.

structures.name: The Last Lamp
structures.purpose: The wedge's inn, and by old custom the last warm light a traveller passes going down and the first coming up — its sign a lamp that is never let go out. Half its trade is farewells and half is homecomings, and the innkeeper has learned to tell, from the door, which a stranger needs. This quarter's Strain-relief haven.

rooms.name: The Common Room
rooms.purpose: hearth, long tables, the never-dark lamp over the door; a wall of tokens left by travellers who meant to come back

rooms.name: Letting rooms (x5)
rooms.purpose: five rooms above, more often taken for one hard-slept night than a stay

rooms.name: Cellar
rooms.purpose: a stair-cool store; a low door that lets onto the Undergate, which the innkeeper swears is bricked up

structures.notes: Innkeeper Wenna Sarr + 2 family + 2 staff. The cellar door is this wedge's over/under seam — to the Undergate (DK-X07).

structures.name: The Caravanserai of the First Night
