position.note: the largest single footprint in the wedge — a courtyarded stopping-house

structures.purpose: A vast galleried courtyard where the outside world sleeps its first night in Starfall: muleteers, pilgrims, traders, envoys, and the merely lost, stacked in tiers of let-rooms around a central yard loud with beasts and languages. The most cosmopolitan single building in a city that prides itself on knowing exactly who everyone is — and the one place that, for a night, does not. A churning, half-transient population no census ever fixes.

rooms.name: The Great Court
rooms.purpose: open yard; a well, a fire-pit, mule-lines, and every dusk a different crowd

rooms.name: The Tier Galleries
rooms.purpose: three storeys of let-rooms opening onto the court; the cheapest are highest and coldest

rooms.name: The Long Stable
rooms.purpose: beasts of the road; the smell of the outside, which the rim finds unspeakable

rooms.name: The Keeper's House
rooms.purpose: Old Mireth and her people, who never sleep the same night twice

structures.notes: Caravanserai-keeper Old Mireth + ~14 permanent staff + ~30 long-stay transients counted this season (the number is never the same twice). The city's true melting-pot; a natural quest and information hub.

structures.name: The Arrival Market
structures.purpose: The market of the freshly-arrived and the about-to-leave: money-changers who take any coin, outfitters, a letter-writer for those who cannot, a physician for stair-broken legs, a dealer in second-hand everything left behind by people who did not make it back for it. Prices tuned to exactly what a tired stranger will pay.

rooms.name: Per unit: shopfront + room above
rooms.purpose: 9 units, most with a family above

structures.notes: 9 shops, ~24 souls. Named: the changer Oshka (who fences what the Undergate brings up) and the letter-writer old Pell (who knows every secret in the wedge and sells none).

structures.name: Canal Dwellings — Gateside
structures.purpose: Dense canalside housing for the wedge's settled working folk — the porters, gate-clerks, stable-hands, changers' families and off-shift customs-men who work the threshold and, unlike the trade that passes through, actually stay. The block that anchors a wedge otherwise made of people leaving.

rooms.name: Per dwelling: 2-3 rooms
rooms.purpose: 8 dwellings, families of 3-6

structures.notes: ~40 souls incl. the customs officer's household (counted here, day-posted to the gate-foot). Named: portress Grella, who has carried loads up the stair since she was nine and will not speak of what she has seen come down it.

structures.name: The Threshold Shrine
structures.purpose: A shrine to Umbrion in his aspect of the threshold — the god of dusk being the god of the moment between, of doorways, of the step you have half-taken. Travellers touch its cold sill going down and coming up; the keeper marks a tally-stone for every soul who prays to leave and does not return, and the wall of them is long.

rooms.name: The Between-Cell
rooms.purpose: a doorless doorway of black stone; you pray standing in it, neither in nor out

rooms.name: Keeper's cell
rooms.purpose: the shrine-keeper's room, walled in tally-stones of the un-returned

structures.notes: Keeper Onwe, who came up the stair once, meaning to go back, and never has. A quiet counterpart to House Vael'Suran's Deepening.

structures.name: The Gate-Foot Customs & Processional Foot
structures.purpose: Where this wedge's processional meets the shore: the second customs post of Duskmere, twinned with the gatehouse far above — the gatehouse tolls what comes overland from the world, this post tolls what the barge-lock lifts from directly below. Between the two, in theory, nothing enters Starfall uncounted. In practice, there is the Undergate.

rooms.name: The Weighing Hall
rooms.purpose: scales, tally-desks, a warded strongroom

rooms.name: Officers' room
rooms.purpose: the customs officer and clerks

structures.notes: Customs officer Brae + 2 clerks (day post; housed at DK-K04). 'In theory nothing enters uncounted' is the wedge's central irony.

structures.name: The Duskmere Lock

position.depth_note: beneath the canal quarter

structures.purpose: The chamber-lock that raises cargo barges from the world directly below the caldera up into the wedge's canal — the fast route, for goods too heavy or too discreet for the long stair. The gate above counts mules; the lock below lifts the tonnage; and the difference between what each records is where a great deal of the wedge's real wealth lives.

rooms.name: The Lock Chamber
rooms.purpose: the flooding basin and counter-weighted gates

rooms.name: The Capstan Floor
rooms.purpose: walked by the lift-gangs

rooms.name: Tally hole
rooms.purpose: the under-clerk's niche and his charcoal ledger

structures.notes: Worked, not lived-in. Lock-master Braff. The gap between the gate-book above and the lock-tally below is the wedge's open secret.

structures.name: The Conduit Gallery

position.depth_note: runs radially under the terraces

structures.purpose: The tuned crystal conduits that carry the Song up to this wedge's star-lamps — including the great landward beacon, which drinks more Song than any lamp in the city and so keeps a whole crew climbing in the dark to feed a light that faces away from them. When the beacon burns for a traveller, it burns on their backs.

rooms.name: The Long Gallery
rooms.purpose: the conduit run; a heavy branch climbs to the beacon-stem

rooms.name: Tuning niches (x4)
rooms.purpose: where conduit-wrights true the crystal

structures.notes: Worked by a conduit crew of 6 (housed at DK-X04). The beacon's hunger is a small cruelty the wedge does not think about.

structures.name: The Stair-Gangs' Hall

position.depth_note: cut beneath the caravanserai

structures.purpose: The bunk-hall of the muscle of the threshold: the stair-porters who carry loads no mule can up the switchbacks, and the barge lift-gangs who walk the lock capstans. Human and orc, road-hard and lock-hard, they are the two halves of how weight gets into Starfall — and neither half is on the gate-book, because the gate-book counts arrivals, and they never leave.

rooms.name: The Porters' Gallery
rooms.purpose: bunks for the stair-gangs; a rack of carry-frames worn to the shape of specific backs

rooms.name: The Lift-Gang Gallery
rooms.purpose: bunks for the capstan-walkers; a wall of notches, one per season survived

rooms.name: The Wash
rooms.purpose: the one place the road-dust and the lock-damp come off

structures.notes: ~28 human/orc stair-porters + ~22 lift-gang. Named: the stair-elder Karsk, who has climbed the equivalent of off the world and back many times over. Part of the unnamed 778.

structures.name: The Stairwrights' Hall

position.depth_note: cut into the outer shore-mass, nearest the stair's roots

structures.purpose: Home and hall of the Terran stairwrights — the deep-folk who cut, shore and endlessly repair the outer switchback stair and the gate's roots, the most dangerous stone-work in Starfall because it hangs over the cloud-sea on the outside of the world. Carved, glow-warm, and grimly proud: every course of the stair a traveller trusts was set by a hand in this hall, and lost fingers are counted here as a kind of rank.

rooms.name: The Carved Hall
rooms.purpose: communal hall; a long stone table and the roll of the stair-dead, cut into the wall

rooms.name: Sleeping galleries
rooms.purpose: bunk-niches for the wrights, the lock-master and the conduit crew who bunk with them

rooms.name: The Shrine of Petrocore
rooms.purpose: a Stone-Voice shrine facing outward, toward the exposed cut — the wrong god, the right prayer

structures.notes: ~42 Terran stairwrights + lock-master Braff + the 6-strong conduit crew who bunk here. Kin-connected to House Vael'Suran's deep-wrights; the two Terran halls trade apprentices and grief.

structures.name: The Waygate Canteen

position.depth_note: at the gallery crossing under the caravanserai

structures.purpose: The under-city's warm room for the wedge, and the strangest table in Starfall: stair-porters, lift-gangs, stairwrights, conduit-crews and, now and then, an outsider come up the Undergate who has nowhere else to be, all eating the same grey good stew. The canteen-keeper feeds anyone who comes down the right passage and asks no gate-book question at all.

rooms.name: The Long Room
rooms.purpose: trestles, a great range, a wall chalked with the dead of the stair and the lock

rooms.name: Kitchen & store
rooms.purpose: run by the keeper

structures.notes: Canteen-keeper Bem + 3 helpers. Sister-room to the Underspill and the Undertoll; the three under-canteens run a quiet grapevine the length of the city.

structures.name: The Foreman's Post

position.depth_note: at the foot of the gate-foot stair

structures.purpose: The seam-office where the under-city of the threshold answers to the over-city — where the lock-tally, the porter-shifts and the awkward matter of the Undergate are all reconciled into whatever number the House is willing to hear. The foreman keeps three ledgers: one for the House, one that is true, and one he burns.

rooms.name: The Office
rooms.purpose: a ledger-desk, a lamp, a strongbox with a false bottom

rooms.name: Bunk
rooms.purpose: the foreman sleeps at the seam

structures.notes: Foreman Idris — the one who decides what the Undergate is allowed to be. Trusted by neither map; feared by both. Prime quest-broker.

structures.name: The Undergate

position.depth_note: where the outer stair's lowest flights breach the under-city, off the plate

footprint.form: a breached gallery, half-walled, lamp-lit in rust

structures.purpose: The city's other door: a place low on the outer stair where a broken flight lets into the under-galleries, and those who cannot pay the gatehouse toll — or cannot afford to be written in the gate-book — come up into Starfall through the dark instead. Not a secret, exactly; a thing the foreman manages, the changers fence for, and the Plate could not draw if it tried, because officially it is a rockfall. The truest threshold in a wedge of thresholds.

rooms.name: The Breach
rooms.purpose: the broken gate; a plank bridge over the drop, and a rust lamp that means 'open tonight'

rooms.name: The Waiting Dark
rooms.purpose: where the un-booked wait to be let up; some for a night, some for years; a squat-camp of the truly uncounted

structures.notes: Gate-shadow Kobb + ~7 long-term squatters of the Waiting Dark. The single sharpest image of the two-maps theme in the wedge: a door the city insists is a wall.

structures.name: The Meridian Tower

position.note: the Serenthil rim tower — greybox tower i=8; the city's public timepiece, not a private observatory

structures.purpose: Where Starfall's time is made and rung. Not a House hiding its instrument but a House whose instrument the whole city can hear — the nine bells that mark the hours, the ceremonies, and (a fact the rim prefers not to dwell on) the labour-shifts below. Vael'Suran keeps the eye; Serenthil keeps the ear.

rooms.name: The Bell-Chamber
rooms.purpose: the nine verdigris bells in their frame; the ninth is the great one, rung only at the solstice count

rooms.name: The Clockwork Hall
rooms.purpose: the master escapement driven by star-water from the cistern below; a floor of turning brass

rooms.name: The Meridian Slit
rooms.purpose: a north-south roof-slit; noon is the instant a fixed star crosses it — time proved against the sky

rooms.name: Strike-Master's watch-room
rooms.purpose: someone watches the clock every hour of every night; the post is never empty

rooms.name: Ringers' loft & rope-race
rooms.purpose: the ropes drop from here — some to the belfry, some straight down into the dark to the shift-bells

structures.notes: Head + Strike-Master + 4 live-in ringers/watch-keepers. Its lit finial is one of the greybox's nine rim domes.

structures.name: The Serenthil Seat
structures.purpose: Plainer than Vael'Suran's Seat and closer to the street — Serenthil money is civic money, made from keeping everyone's time, and the House wears its usefulness where the fixed-star grandees wear their view. Every room is on time; not one clock in it agrees to be wrong.

rooms.name: The Striking Hall
rooms.purpose: reception; a wall of the House's retired clocks, each stopped at the hour of a death

rooms.name: Head's chambers
rooms.purpose: Magister Toll Serenthil's rooms

rooms.name: Family & apprentice rooms
rooms.purpose: family + two horology apprentices boarded in

rooms.name: Kitchen, stores, staff
rooms.purpose: household below and attic

structures.notes: Toll + family (5) + 2 boarded apprentices + 11 staff. Less grand, more lived-in than VS-M01.

structures.name: The Strike-Master's Villa
structures.purpose: Home of the Strike-Master, the commoner-born officer who actually decides when the bells ring — a heavier hand on the city's day than most House heads. His sightline matters less to him than his hearing-line: he can tell a mistuned bell from three terraces off.

rooms.name: The Listening Room
rooms.purpose: shuttered, bare, acoustically true; he checks the bells' pitch from here

rooms.name: Family rooms (x3)
rooms.purpose: the Strike-Master, spouse, 3 children

structures.notes: Strike-Master Venn Ostreth + household.

structures.name: The Horologist's Villa
structures.purpose: The villa of the House's chief horologist — the theorist of time itself, who argues that the Song has a beat and that a perfect clock would simply count it. Half the Academy thinks him a crank; the other half quietly borrows his figures.

rooms.name: The Escapement Study
rooms.purpose: a study full of half-built regulators, each trying to find the Song's beat

rooms.name: Living rooms
rooms.purpose: the horologist + a companion + one apprentice

structures.notes: Chief horologist Marn Ilve + household. Provides a theory-thread toward the Academy's Song-work.

structures.name: Sightline Villa — the Quiet House
structures.purpose: A Serenthil villa let, unusually, to a tenant from outside the House — an aged Noctari astronomer who wanted only quiet and a view, and pays for both. The House takes the coin and pretends the arrangement is temporary; it has been temporary for ninety years.

rooms.name: The Study
rooms.purpose: an outsider's sightline, rented

rooms.name: Rooms
rooms.purpose: the tenant + a single servant

structures.notes: Tenant-astronomer Ollisan + 4 (companion, servant, 2 boarders). A wedge with rented rooms reads differently from Vael'Suran's closed bloodline.

structures.name: The Bell-Foundry
structures.purpose: Loud, hot, and the opposite of everything the rim pretends to be: the wedge's bells and clock-brass are cast and tuned here. A bell is tuned by shaving metal from its inside until its note is true — a craft of subtraction, done by ear, over weeks. The most important trade in Serenthil and the least gentrified.

rooms.name: The Casting Floor
rooms.purpose: the bell-pit, the furnace, the crane; a floor no scholar visits twice

rooms.name: The Tuning Bay
rooms.purpose: where a cast bell is shaved to its true note against a monochord

rooms.name: Founders' dwelling
rooms.purpose: the master founder's family above the heat

rooms.name: Journeymen's loft
rooms.purpose: boarded workers

structures.notes: Master founder Hessa Drun + family + 8 journeymen. The vent-flue drops to the under-forge (SR-X04).

structures.name: The Horologists' Hall
structures.purpose: The clockmakers: escapement-fitters, gear-cutters, dial-engravers, and the water-clock wrights who keep the city's public clepsydrae running. Fine, patient, indoor work — the bench-craft that turns the founder's raw brass into time.

rooms.name: The Bench Floor
rooms.purpose: ranked benches under north light; a wall of running regulators for comparison

rooms.name: The Wheel-Cutting Room
rooms.purpose: the dividing engine that cuts gear-teeth — the Hall's guarded secret

rooms.name: Apprentices' dormitory
rooms.purpose: boarded apprentices

structures.notes: Guild-warden Pel Corriden + 8 (fitters & apprentices).

structures.name: Lesser Timekeepers' Row
structures.purpose: Six joined houses of the wedge's lesser timekeepers — the hour-callers, dial-readers, water-tenders and rope-boys who serve the Tower without ever entering the bell-chamber. Respectable, sightless, and paid in the House's steady, unglamorous coin.

rooms.name: Per-house: work-room + 2 chambers
rooms.purpose: 6 households

structures.notes: 6 households, ~22 souls. Named: hour-caller old Renn, whose voice the whole wedge wakes to.

structures.name: The Ninth Bell
structures.purpose: The wedge's inn, named for the great solstice bell you can feel in your chest from here — and the one place the day's timekeeping stops mattering. Rope-boys, off-shift founders, and the occasional deaf old ringer drink under a cracked bell hung over the bar. This wedge's Strain-relief haven.

rooms.name: The Common Room
rooms.purpose: hearth, long tables, the cracked bell; a clock deliberately kept five minutes wrong, as a joke that is also a mercy

rooms.name: Letting rooms (x5)
rooms.purpose: five rooms above

rooms.name: Cellar
rooms.purpose: a canal-cooled store; a grille here opens onto the shift-bell undercroft — you hear the dark ringing through it

structures.notes: Innkeeper Wenna Kob + 2 family + 2 staff. The cellar grille is Serenthil's over/under seam (to SR-X01).

structures.name: The Clepsydra-Works
structures.purpose: The public water-clocks of the whole city are built and regulated here, tapping the canal's star-water — the works that turns flowing water into counted time. A calm, dripping, faintly hypnotic place; its overflow feeds back to the canal, and its intake comes up from the Great Cistern below.

rooms.name: The Flow Hall
rooms.purpose: tiered basins, float-gauges, the master clepsydra whose drip sets the Tower's water-drive

rooms.name: The Regulator Room
rooms.purpose: where flow is trimmed to a true hour

rooms.name: Wrights' dwelling
rooms.purpose: the water-wrights above

structures.notes: Water-warden Iss Vellun + 11 (wrights & families). Mechanically ties the canal, the cistern and the Tower into one water-driven clock.

structures.name: Sera's Lodging
structures.purpose: Two small rented rooms where Sera lodges — a Solari structural enchantress, a sun-elf alone in the night-city, on the Nullstone team and trusted by no faction on it. She chose the timekeepers' wedge on purpose: their bells are the one thing in Starfall that keep to a schedule she recognises, and she keeps a single forbidden sun-lamp she lights only when the shutters are closed.

rooms.name: Work-room
rooms.purpose: structural models in silver wire; a Solari sun-disc turned to the wall

rooms.name: Sleeping room
rooms.purpose: a cot, a shuttered window, the sun-lamp

structures.notes: Sera (CH-008, PO-006) — 'the outsider's outsider.' Canonical Nullstone-team anchor in this wedge, deliberately mirroring Vara's garret in the Vael'Suran wedge.

structures.name: Canal Dwellings — Watergate
structures.purpose: Dense canalside housing by the watergate, home to the rope-boys, water-tenders, dial-runners and canal-hands who keep the wedge's time-machinery fed and moving. The block wakes to old Renn's hour-call and sleeps to the ninth-of-night bell.

rooms.name: Per dwelling: 2-3 rooms
rooms.purpose: 8 dwellings, families of 3-6

structures.notes: ~40 souls. Named: the widow Ferrun, whose late husband fell from the belfry, and who counts every bell since.

structures.name: The Hour-Market
structures.purpose: A market that opens and closes to the bell — nine stalls and shops selling by strict tolled hours (a Serenthil custom, and a small tyranny): a baker, a dial-shop, a candle-and-oil merchant, a rope-walk, a cook-stall, a scrivener, a herbalist. Live-over-the-shop trade timed to the death by the very House that sells them the clocks.

rooms.name: Per unit: shopfront + room above
rooms.purpose: 9 units, most with a family above

structures.notes: 9 shops, ~22 souls. Named: the baker Doln, who bribes a rope-boy to ring his opening a half-minute early.

structures.name: The Bell-Gate & Processional Foot
structures.purpose: Where the Grand Processional meets the shore on Serenthil's side: a gate with its own small bell that opens and closes the processional to ceremony, and a customs post twinned with Vael'Suran's across the way. The two Houses' gate-bells answer each other across the stair — the city's front door, in stereo.

rooms.name: The Gate Hall
rooms.purpose: the gate-bell rope, a tally-desk, a warded night-strongroom

rooms.name: Gatekeepers' room
rooms.purpose: the gate-warden and a clerk

structures.notes: Gate-warden Ospren + clerk (day post; counted at their canal homes).

structures.name: The Shift-Bell Undercroft

position.depth_note: directly under the Tower's rope-race

structures.purpose: The dark twin of the bell-chamber. The same ropes that ring the festival's ninth bell drop through the whole city to here, where under-ringers pull the SHIFT-bells that govern the labour below — the cistern-gangs, the bell-wrights, the lift-crews. To the rim, the bell is glory; to the dark, the identical bell is a whip you can hear but not see. Serenthil rings both and calls it one service.

rooms.name: The Under-Belfry
rooms.purpose: the shift-bells and the drop-ropes; a board chalked with the shift-count

rooms.name: Under-ringers' bunk
rooms.purpose: the ringers live at their ropes; they have not seen a festival in years

structures.notes: Under-ringer crew (8). The Sounding-metaphor made literal: one bell, two meanings, and only the dark hears both. The Ninth Bell inn's cellar grille opens near here.

structures.name: The Clock-Water Gallery

position.depth_note: radial run beneath the terraces

structures.purpose: Twin runs in one gallery: the tuned Song-conduits that feed this wedge's star-lamps (as under Vael'Suran) AND the star-water race that carries the Great Cistern's water up to the clepsydra-works and the Tower's clock-drive. When a lamp burns or a clock ticks on the terraces above, its cause is in this tunnel, tended in the dark.

rooms.name: The Long Gallery
rooms.purpose: conduit + water-race side by side; access ladders to each terrace

rooms.name: Sluice niches (x3)
rooms.purpose: where water-wrights set the race's flow

structures.notes: Conduit-and-race crew (6, mixed Terran & human). The literal plumbing of both light and time.

structures.name: The Great Cistern

position.depth_note: a vaulted reservoir deep under the shore-mass

structures.purpose: Starfall's hidden heart of star-water: a vast pillared vault of black, still, faintly-starred water that drives every clock, feeds every canal-lock, and cools the whole under-city — a subterranean night sky underneath the lake that is a night sky. The single most impressive space in Starfall, and it is on no map, because the people who need it are not on the map either. Reached by boat across its own black surface.

rooms.name: The Vault
rooms.purpose: forty stone pillars standing in still water; a rowed jetty; the water doubles the lamplight into a false depth

rooms.name: The Pump-Floor
rooms.purpose: the great treadwheel pumps that lift water to the race — walked by the cistern-gangs

rooms.name: Keepers' rooms
rooms.purpose: the cistern-keepers, who live beside the water and learn to read its level like a face

structures.notes: Cistern-keepers + pump-crew (12). The wedge's 'novel and unique' landmark — a cathedral of dark water no citizen above has ever seen. Strong future hero-set-piece.

structures.name: The Bell-Wrights' & Cistern-Gangs' Hall

position.depth_note: cut beside the cistern

structures.purpose: The largest under-dwelling of the wedge: Terran bell-wrights (who tune the shift-bells and cast the clock-brass at an under-forge the foundry's flue feeds) alongside the human and orc cistern-gangs who walk the pumps. A rare mixed hall — the Song does not reach here, so the races that the city above keeps carefully apart share one warm, loud, glow-lit room.

rooms.name: The Under-Forge
rooms.purpose: a small casting floor fed by the Bell-Foundry's flue; shift-bells are born and tuned here

rooms.name: The Long Hall
rooms.purpose: shared eating-and-living hall; a Petrocore shrine and a scratched orc tally-board share a wall

rooms.name: Sleeping galleries
rooms.purpose: bunk-niches for ~46 wrights and gang-hands

structures.notes: ~30 Terran bell-wrights + ~16 human/orc cistern-gang. The mixed hall varies the texture from Vael'Suran's segregated Terran/orc halls, and is a natural place for a cross-race scene.

structures.name: The Undertoll Canteen

position.depth_note: at the gallery crossing

structures.purpose: The under-city's warm room for this wedge, named for the toll-bell that calls its meal-shifts. Under-ringers, cistern-gangs, bell-wrights and conduit-crews eat here between shifts; the canteen-keeper rings her own small bell for meals and, once a year, quietly rings it nine times for the dead.

rooms.name: The Long Room
rooms.purpose: trestles, a great range, a wall of chalked names

rooms.name: Kitchen & store
rooms.purpose: run by the keeper

structures.notes: Canteen-keeper Old Sable + 3 helpers. Sister-room to Vael'Suran's Underspill; the two under-canteens know each other's runners.

structures.name: The Foreman's Post

position.depth_note: at the foot of the bell-gate stair

structures.purpose: The seam-office of Serenthil's under-city, at the foot of the stair up to the Bell-Gate — where the shift-count is reconciled against the toll and sent up to the House. The foreman keeps time for people the timekeepers never count.

rooms.name: The Office
rooms.purpose: a ledger-desk, a shift-book, a small answering bell wired to the undercroft

rooms.name: Bunk
rooms.purpose: the foreman sleeps at the seam

structures.notes: Foreman Quill — keeps the honest count in charcoal and the House's count in ink, and knows they differ.

npcs.name: Archmagister Sennel Vaross
npcs.role: head of the Academy of Astral Harmony
npcs.note: Rules an instrument the nine Houses answer to and none of them own; keeps the peace between them by keeping the sky common. Older than any House head.

npcs.name: First Astronomer Deire + observers (12)
npcs.role: keep the night watches under the great dome

npcs.name: Senior Lector Vessine
npcs.role: runs the Theory Wings; the Academy's memory
npcs.note: Has read everything and forgotten nothing; disapproves of void-work and cannot stop reading it.

npcs.name: Resident theorists (5)
npcs.role: fellows of the Wings
npcs.note: Coil (CH-009), Vara (CH-010), Sera (CH-008), Durak (CH-011) work here daily but are housed in the city — not counted on the island.

npcs.name: Corel
npcs.role: containment archmagister; Elorin's exhausted superior
npcs.note: Decency worn thin by duty. Keeps an office and often sleeps at the rig rather than cross the causeway. Signs off on the safeguard he is too tired to fully check.

npcs.name: Night-wards of Containment (3)
npcs.role: keep the rig-pit through the night watches

npcs.name: Elorin Voidweaver
npcs.role: the Architect; resident fellow; designer of the Nullstone
npcs.note: PROTAGONIST of Part One. Lodges here through her Academy years; Umbrion-aligned, House Corvane-trained, the one person who can build a piece of the void into the heart of the Song. Her spare over-open rooms are the most consequential on the island.

npcs.name: Resident fellows (11)
npcs.role: senior scholars boarded on the island
npcs.note: Coil (CH-009) lodges among them when not at the Wings.

npcs.name: Refectory-master Ondle + staff (9)
npcs.role: feeds the whole island at one set of tables
npcs.note: Runs the one room on the island where the city's separations quietly don't apply.

npcs.name: The students (84)
npcs.role: the Academy's students — the Houses' sharpest, a few from below and beyond
npcs.note: The NA-02 crowd. Most will never own a sightline; all of them think they will. Named among them: the canal-quarter prodigy Ithe, and the House heir Varrun who resents her.

npcs.name: Proctors (4)
npcs.role: keep order in the dorms

npcs.name: Gate-porter Sull + night-porters (2)
npcs.role: keeps the causeway gate and the island register
npcs.note: Knows exactly who is on the island at any hour — a fact that will matter.

npcs.name: The Ward-Keepers (6) — ward-master Gollen
npcs.role: guard the prototype and the drafting dais
npcs.note: Almost bored in Part One; their successors the Void Wardens (CH-017) will guard the finished Stone, unbored, for three hundred years.

npcs.name: Magister Ysolde Vael'Suran
npcs.role: Head of House Vael'Suran; Keeper of the Master Survey
npcs.note: Ancient, exact, proud; signs the survey her First Surveyor actually runs. The city's sightlines are her family's word made law.

npcs.name: First Reader Pan-Ostrel
npcs.role: senior observer, the Gnomon Chamber
npcs.note: Takes the cold midnight readings; they and the gnomon are the only two things in the House never wrong.

npcs.name: the junior computers (4)
npcs.role: live-in calculating clerks
npcs.note: Reduce the night's numbers by hand; dream in tables.

npcs.name: Ilvenor Vael'Suran
npcs.role: Ysolde's heir, bored and dangerous with it
npcs.note: Slums at the Sounding-Glass; will inherit sightlines he has never once looked along.

npcs.name: the near family (3)
npcs.role: House family

npcs.name: the Seat household staff (13)
npcs.role: cook, chart-porters, lamp-tender, gate-keeper, maids
npcs.note: Includes two humans who may not dine in the rooms they clean.

npcs.name: Sub-Magister Aeliston Vael'Suran
npcs.role: cousin of the House; keeper of the running correction of the caldera's own sky
npcs.note: Lives alone with his door open; the Open House lectern is his life's chart. The eccentric the House indulges.

npcs.name: First Surveyor Halvenor Daskei
npcs.role: commoner-born scholar who actually runs the survey
npcs.note: The mind behind Ysolde's signature; keeps a private roof platform because the House will not give him a tower key.

npcs.name: Renne Daskei & 4 (family)
npcs.role: Halvenor's household

npcs.name: Magistra Ivrenne (née Vael'Suran, m. Corvane)
npcs.role: void-adjacent scholar; the House's disowned-and-funded research
npcs.note: Household of 5. A living link to House Corvane (H5).

npcs.name: Astronomer Sarrent
npcs.role: widowed scholar losing a sightline suit
npcs.note: Household of 3. Side-quest seed: the encroached sightline.

npcs.name: Master-scribe Ovinn
npcs.role: warden of the Scribes' Hall

npcs.name: Talindir
npcs.role: apprentice scribe, the fastest and finest hand in the hall
npcs.note: The Cold Open's chronicler, 550 years younger. Copies the fixed-star charts; observation is already 'the only thing he does well enough for it to constitute protection.'

npcs.name: Master optician Delu Marn + household (9)
npcs.role: lens-grinders

npcs.name: Lesser Scholars' Row (22)
npcs.role: reducers, correctors, lecture-assistants; sightless
npcs.note: Named principal: reducer Kessa Von. A social border made of geometry — no protected view.

npcs.name: Bruin Hale + house (5)
npcs.role: innkeeper of the Sounding-Glass
npcs.note: Knows about the cellar hatch to the under-city and says nothing.

npcs.name: The Instrument Market (34)
npcs.role: brass-founders, tube-makers, engravers, a paper merchant
npcs.note: Named: brass-founder Ossa Kellen; the elder engraver Pim.

npcs.name: Serae the shrine-keeper
npcs.role: keeper of the Deepening (Umbrion shrine)
npcs.note: Blind; chosen because the dark costs her nothing.

npcs.name: Vara
npcs.role: structural theorist on the Nullstone team; the wedge's best mind, worst room
npcs.note: 'Twice as good, half as credited.' A human housed in a canal garret while lesser Noctari keep rim villas; walks the whole city to the island every day.

npcs.name: Lockside dwellings (38)
npcs.role: artisans, boatwrights, lamplighters, canal-workers
npcs.note: Named: lamplighter Corrun, who knows a stair down that isn't drawn.

npcs.name: Customs officer Trell + 2 clerks
npcs.role: weighs everything that comes up from below
npcs.note: Guards the one official door between the two cities; it only faces up.

npcs.name: Lock-master Dregg
npcs.role: runs Cael's Lock
npcs.note: The under-clerk beneath him keeps the real ledger — the Other Map's tally.

npcs.name: Conduit-wrights (crew of 6)
npcs.role: keep the Song singing up to the star-lamps
npcs.note: The literal hands behind 'the lamps simply burn.'

npcs.name: Durak Ironthought
npcs.role: geomancer; Nullstone-team consultant; lodges among the deep-wrights
npcs.note: 'You are trying to redirect water; we would build a basin.' He lives with the people who actually build — the whole reason he sees what the elves miss.

npcs.name: The Deep-Wrights (43)
npcs.role: cut and hold up the Under-Terraces
npcs.note: Proud, glow-stone-warm, prouder than the rim. Keep a shrine to Petrocore in a city of the wrong god.

npcs.name: The Lift-Gang (30) — elder Ghesh
npcs.role: walk the lock capstans; carry what the barges bring
npcs.note: Where Elorin first SEES the labour (Narrative Outline Ch2). Ghesh counts the shifts. Part of the unnamed 778.

npcs.name: Mother Vesh + 3
npcs.role: canteen-keeper of the Underspill
npcs.note: Feeds every race in the under-city the same good grey stew; chalks the dead on the wall.

npcs.name: Foreman Adric
npcs.role: the seam between the two cities; answers to the over-city, works the under
npcs.note: Over-city clothes, under-city hands; trusted by neither map. Natural quest-broker.

npcs.name: Magister Suvane Nyx'Talar
npcs.role: Head of House Nyx'Talar; Warden-in-Chief of the Occultation
npcs.note: Soft-voiced, never hurried, and the best-informed person in Starfall who is not on the Conclave. Governs by knowing; her manor faces the city, not the sky.

npcs.name: First Occulter Dess
npcs.role: senior observer; times the eclipses and transits
npcs.note: Takes every reading alone. Knows the exact second of every concealment in the sky and has been taught never to wonder about the ones on the ground.

npcs.name: the live-in reckoners (6)
npcs.role: reduce the eclipse-tables
npcs.note: Taught to forget the names attached to the timings; they mostly manage it.

npcs.name: the Nyx'Talar near family (5)
npcs.role: House family
npcs.note: Each chamber with its own lock; a family that keeps secrets even from itself.

npcs.name: the Shuttered Seat staff (11)
npcs.role: cook, gate-lodge keeper, chart-porters, maids
npcs.note: Chosen for what they can be trusted not to repeat; paid a little extra for it.

npcs.name: Warden Ottress + household (5)
npcs.role: senior Warden; holds a registered sightline he never opens
npcs.note: Wealth here is a view you own and refuse to spend.

npcs.name: Warden Coreth + household (6)
npcs.role: Second Warden; catalogues transits by day, arranges silences by night
npcs.note: The House's discreet fixer. Her back parlour is the busiest unlit room on the terrace; every favour has a timing and a price paid in quiet.

npcs.name: the widow Halissa + household (4)
npcs.role: kept tenant; saw something once at an occultation
npcs.note: Comfortably kept to be kept silent; one of her four servants reports to the Seat, and she knows which.

npcs.name: Caretaker Pell
npcs.role: keeps the Furnished Absence warm and empty
npcs.note: Lives alone in the back rooms of a villa built to belong to no one; forgets faces as a profession.

npcs.name: Master-sealwright Ordell Craze + hall (13)
npcs.role: makes the city's official seals, locks and ciphers
npcs.note: His dies certify that a thing stayed shut; the House's fortune is built on being believed.

npcs.name: the Sealed Copyists (9)
npcs.role: reproduce documents they are trained not to read
npcs.note: Work blind in felt booths. Named overseer: the warden Prisca, who reads everything and remembers on command.

npcs.name: Lesser Wardens' Row (22) — Nessa Ptol
npcs.role: sightless street-watchers; keep the House's survey of the city
npcs.note: Nessa Ptol has a memory for faces the House cannot afford to lose. Sightless, respectable, never off duty.

npcs.name: Mistress Oll + house (5)
npcs.role: innkeeper of the Blind Eye
npcs.note: One-eyed and pointed about it; enforces the one rule that makes her inn matter — here, no one is watched.

npcs.name: the Unlabelled Market (30) — the 'valuer' Sim Onrey
npcs.role: letter-writers, a lock-fitter, a seal-dealer, a fence, a tea-house
npcs.note: No painted signs; you are meant to know which door. Sim Onrey can find the owner of anything, for a fee.

npcs.name: Keeper Threnn
npcs.role: keeper of the Shrine of the Passing Shadow
npcs.note: Has watched the same blade of light be occulted for 140 years; calls it the only honest clock in the city.

npcs.name: Shutterside dwellings (38) — Corra Sel
npcs.role: boatwrights, runners' families, sealwrights' kin, market-hands
npcs.note: Corra Sel runs the night-barge and knows which cargoes are never weighed.

npcs.name: the watcher Aline Voss + apprentice
npcs.role: freelance watcher; sells the House what its wardens miss
npcs.note: Keeps her notes in a shorthand no one else can read; a quest-broker with an agenda of her own, and training an apprentice to disappear.

npcs.name: Watch-officer Delm + 2 clerks
npcs.role: runs the round-the-clock Watch-Customs
npcs.note: Cares less what a cargo weighs than who stands beside it; keeps a second ledger of faces.

npcs.name: Lock-master Bront
npcs.role: runs the Silent Lock; warren-master of the deep-wrights
npcs.note: Keeps the only true plan of what has been dug, in stone-script, and sells that knowledge to no one — the one thing the House cannot buy.

npcs.name: the Listeners (6)
npcs.role: tend the Song-conduits and man the listening niches
npcs.note: Live at their posts; what they hear rises in a sealed hand to the Hall of Occultations. The House calls it acoustics.

npcs.name: the warren-elders (with Bront)
npcs.role: keepers of the Unmapped Room
npcs.note: The elder council of the warren; counted here as one record beside Bront.

npcs.name: the Deep-Wrights (46)
npcs.role: cut the under-galleries and the hidden ways
npcs.note: Riddle the wedge with passages that appear on no plan but their own. Closer-mouthed than the House above them.

npcs.name: the Runners (52) — the runner-elder Vosk
npcs.role: carry sealed things by hand through the dark
npcs.note: Memorise routes, write nothing, keep poor memories for pay. Vosk has never been caught and teaches the young how not to be. Part of the unnamed 778.

npcs.name: Ma Dell + 3
npcs.role: canteen-keeper of the Underquiet
npcs.note: Enforces the Blind Eye's rule below ground; between her, Mother Vesh and Old Sable the three under-canteens miss nothing.

npcs.name: Foreman Karse
npcs.role: keeper of the seam; edits the record before it rises to the watch
npcs.note: Two shift-books that do not agree. The most dangerous man in the wedge, and the most blackmailable.

npcs.name: the Sealed Warden Ilex
npcs.role: keeper of the Hall of Occultations; times, seals and releases the city's secrets
npcs.note: Has not been seen above ground in thirty years. Knows which drawers fall due tonight; holds a quiet lever on every House in Starfall — very possibly on the Academy too.

npcs.name: the record-keepers (11)
npcs.role: live sealed within the vault, keeping the timed drawers
npcs.note: Take the oath of the vault and are not seen above for years at a time; a whole life spent keeping other people's.

npcs.name: the Ferry-Warren (47)
npcs.role: night-barge crews of the Silent Lock
npcs.note: Born to the under-water; their children know the black loading-channels better than any terrace of light. The Plate never knew to omit them.

npcs.name: Magister Corandine Oravelle
npcs.role: Head of House Oravelle; Keeper of the Ephemeris; underwriter of the realm's dates
npcs.note: Gracious, papered, and entirely certain that selling certainty is a public service. Signs an ephemeris her First Reckoner computes and guarantees she privately knows the odds on.

npcs.name: First Reckoner Hessa Vun
npcs.role: commoner-born chief computer; derives the ephemeris the House sells
npcs.note: The mind behind Corandine's seal; keeps a locked drawer of the errors the published tables omit. Could unmake the House with one honest sentence.

npcs.name: the live-in computers (6)
npcs.role: junior calculating clerks reducing the wanderers' positions
npcs.note: Paid in board and the promise of a clerkship; dream in columns.

npcs.name: the Oravelle near family (6)
npcs.role: House family + 2 clerk-cousins in line for the desks

npcs.name: the Counting-Seat staff (17)
npcs.role: sealing-clerks, cook, porters, strongroom-warden, maids
npcs.note: The seat is half household, half office; the human clerks pray at the Chapel of Variables.

npcs.name: Hessa Vun's household (5)
npcs.role: the First Reckoner's husband and two children + a lodging aunt
npcs.note: Listed with NPC-OR-002 who heads it.

npcs.name: Notary-Magister Selvane + household (6)
npcs.role: bonded notary; his seal makes a computed date binding
npcs.note: Grown rich witnessing other people's certainty.

npcs.name: Magister Orrin Tallowe + household (4)
npcs.role: disgraced date-sealer; recomputes the reading that ruined him
npcs.note: Voided a whole province's planting-date by a season; the House honoured the guarantee and billed him for it. Side-quest: was it his error or the House's? See OR-X07.

npcs.name: Overseer Marn Quell + clerks (28)
npcs.role: runs the Ephemeris Manufactory; keeps the computation divided so no clerk sees the whole
npcs.note: The engine of the House's fortune; docks a clerk for a blotted line.

npcs.name: Seal-warden Ippa Dross + guild (12)
npcs.role: warden of the bonded seals; keeps the register of live and voided matrices
npcs.note: Guards the dies that could counterfeit the future.

npcs.name: Lesser Clerks' Row (24) — register-keeper Voss
npcs.role: tenured reckoners, sealers'-assistants, register-keepers; sightless
npcs.note: Voss knows what everyone above and below earns and resents both. The most anxious street in the city.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Delph Ravin + house (6)
npcs.role: keeps The Ledger & Compass; rubs his slate clean each year
npcs.note: Runs the one untallied room in a district of triplicate. Knows about the cellar grille.

npcs.name: The Almanac Market (30) — the widow Pell & the dealer Osk
npcs.role: almanac-sellers, chart-makers, a second-hand date dealer
npcs.note: Osk reads discounted lucky-day sheets aloud to the illiterate for a coin — retail fate.

npcs.name: Lay-keeper Ansel Roe + 2
npcs.role: keeper of the Chapel of Variables (Path of Adaptation)
npcs.note: Tends a god of odds in a House that sells them; thinks the almanacs the superstition, not his faith.

npcs.name: Chief Assurer Wend Colu + assurers (10)
npcs.role: runs the Assurance House; underwrites dates as a hedge
npcs.note: Keeps the actuary's forbidden tables — which show the House loses more guarantees than it lets the rim believe. Sleeps above the money.

npcs.name: Inkside dwellings (46) — ink-master Corrl
npcs.role: printers, ink-makers, paper-porters, copy-runners
npcs.note: Corrl's iron-gall recipe the wedge depends on and his lungs pay for. The block's children are born with stained hands.

npcs.name: Customs-dater Ollen + 2 clerks
npcs.role: dates and licenses everything that comes up from below
npcs.note: Day post. Converts under-city labour into dated, sellable paper at the waterline.

npcs.name: Lock-master Bral
npcs.role: runs the Reed-Lock; lifts the paper-machine's raw reed from below
npcs.note: The under-clerk beneath him keeps the honest tonnage in charcoal.

npcs.name: Conduit-wrights (crew of 6)
npcs.role: keep the Song singing up to the manufactory's lamps
npcs.note: The reason the ledger can be balanced past dusk.

npcs.name: Deep-warden Torv Greel
npcs.role: warden of the Under-Reckoners' Hall; leads the deep-wrights
npcs.note: The House's most trusted sums pass through his people, off the books, because the deep-folk count in a base the elves cannot easily cook.

npcs.name: The Under-Reckoners & Deep-Wrights (43)
npcs.role: cut and hold the wedge; check the manufactory's figures below the record
npcs.note: Do the House's most trusted arithmetic and receive none of its seat. Keep a Petrocore shrine in the wrong city.

npcs.name: The Pulp- & Rag-Gangs (58) — elder Osma
npcs.role: beat reed and rag to pulp; make the paper the House is printed on
npcs.note: Cannot read a word of what they make. Live inside the stamping-noise. Part of the unnamed 778; Osma keeps the rag-halls' own count.

npcs.name: Canteen-keeper Old Ghu + 3
npcs.role: keeps the Reed-Bottom Canteen; hosts the secret letters-corner
npcs.note: Teaches the under-city to read from stolen almanac off-cuts — the House's paper turned against its grain. Knows Mother Vesh (H0) and Old Sable (H8) by their runners.

npcs.name: Foreman Sarn
npcs.role: the seam of Oravelle's under-city; reconciles real tonnage to the dated figure
npcs.note: Paid precisely to know how large the difference is. Twin to Foreman Adric (H0) and Foreman Quill (H8).

npcs.name: Registrar of Voided Days Miral Enn + 1
npcs.role: sole keeper of the Dead-Letter Vault of failed predictions
npcs.note: Lives underground among every tomorrow the House got wrong. Holds, somewhere, the errata that could exonerate Orrin Tallowe (OR-U03) and the true loss-rate of the Assurance House (OR-K04).

npcs.name: Magistra Aubrelle Sabreth
npcs.role: Head of House Sabreth; Reader of the Long-Haired Stars
npcs.note: Gracious, exact, and entirely without illusions about what her House sells. Reads a comet true and prices the lie precisely. The most powerful person in Starfall no respectable person will admit to knowing.

npcs.name: the Sabreth family (6)
npcs.role: House family + resident 'guests' (leverage)
npcs.note: Some of the 'family' are hostages of a soft and comfortable kind.

npcs.name: the Seat household & guard (17)
npcs.role: cook, dressers, doormen, guards, a discreet physician
npcs.note: Larger and harder than a scholar's household; the orc guards are the only orcs in the city who sleep above ground.

npcs.name: the Night-Readers & interpreters (8)
npcs.role: live-in comet-watchers who log the sky and price the omen
npcs.note: Sworn to discretion; the good ones are half-astronomer, half-actor.

npcs.name: Nemora Sabreth, the Long-Sight
npcs.role: the House's true prodigy; reads comet-paths a season ahead
npcs.note: Household of 7. The genuine talent the whole trade rests on, sickened by the selling of it. Side-quest anchor: an honest prediction, freely given, at a cost to her.

npcs.name: Sarnauld Vray, the Veilkeeper
npcs.role: commoner-born fixer; decides who is seen, when, and for what
npcs.note: Household of 8. The House's true engine; remembers every client and every price. Mirrors the other Houses' commoner-officers — but for vice.

npcs.name: 'Lady' Ombrise + household (7)
npcs.role: charming front-resident; hostess of the deals no one speaks aloud
npcs.note: A past that does not survive inspection and credit that never runs out. The laundered money's public face.

npcs.name: Master printer Pellon Sabreth + house (18)
npcs.role: runs the Ephemeris-House; manufactures fate by the edition
npcs.note: Compositors, pressmen, families. The wedge's most respectable trade and its most cynical.

npcs.name: The Fate-Scriveners' Row (24) — the crier Vess, old Halden
npcs.role: chart-copyists, charm-writers, criers, cheap freelance readers
npcs.note: The fate-trade's small fry. Halden reads true for free and is quietly hated for it.

npcs.name: Guild-mistress Cael Onwe + hall (12)
npcs.role: perfumers & veil-makers; makers of the Court's atmosphere
npcs.note: Keeps the incense recipe — a guild secret worth killing for that never has been, because the House needs it more than any one life.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Dosca Rell + house (6)
npcs.role: keeps the Comet's Tail
npcs.note: Knows about the false cellar wall and rents the two client-doors upstairs; the walls, she says, are good listeners.

npcs.name: Dalveen, Mistress of the Omen Court
npcs.role: runs the night-market of fates; sees the whole floor, misses nothing
npcs.note: Dalveen + 11 live-in Court staff (readers, doormen, incense-boys, guards). The ringmaster of the beautiful open secret.

npcs.name: The Charm-Market (28) — Sesk, Two-Fingers Voll
npcs.role: charm-carvers, incense-sellers, comet-glass dealers, a herbalist
npcs.note: All leasing from the House, all owing a favour of unnamed size.

npcs.name: Lantern Walk dwellings (52) — the boat-girl Nella
npcs.role: readers, criers, doormen, incense-boys, boat-hands, market families
npcs.note: Nella ferries veiled clients and could name half the city; she won't, which is the only reason she's alive to ferry them.

npcs.name: Shrine-keeper Anselm + novice
npcs.role: keeps the Shrine of the Turning; sells nothing
npcs.note: Preaches that the comet means nothing and comes anyway — the one honest voice in the wedge, funded by the House as its alibi.

npcs.name: Customs officer Bren + 2 clerks
npcs.role: runs the performatively-clean Sabreth customs post
npcs.note: Genuinely honest, and kept honest on purpose — the House's proof of nothing to hide, while everything comes up the water-gate.

npcs.name: The Conduit-wrights (6)
npcs.role: keep the Song singing to the star-lamps; tap the House's signal-code
npcs.note: The hands behind 'the lamps simply burn,' doubling as Sabreth's private telegraph.

npcs.name: The Reckoner, Old Kesk + counters & guards (16)
npcs.role: master of the Counting-Vault; turns dirty coin into clean ledger-lines
npcs.note: Live-in for secrecy. Keeps the House's true reserve and truer client-book. A Terran trusted with the elves' filthiest arithmetic — and never allowed up the stair by day.

npcs.name: The Porters' Warren (40) — hall-elder Brud
npcs.role: haulers & conduit-crew; carry what the lock brings and ask nothing
npcs.note: Better-paid than deep-folk elsewhere; the House buys their silence with comfort. Their one rule, chalked on the hall wall: ASK NOTHING.

npcs.name: Lock-master Ferrun Oskt
npcs.role: runs the Slack-Water Lock; keeps the two logs
npcs.note: The point where the clean city and the dirty money change places. The honest log in ink; the other in Vray's code.

npcs.name: Canteen-keeper Mother Ollen + 3
npcs.role: keeps the Blindside Canteen
npcs.note: Feeds everyone, keeps everyone's secrets, sells nothing — the most trusted person in the district. Her runner listens more than she talks.

npcs.name: Foreman Adley
npcs.role: seam-keeper who reports up the wrong stair, to the Veilkeeper
npcs.note: Knows exactly how much the House is lying, which is why he never writes it down twice. Twin-but-inverted to the other wedges' honest foremen.

npcs.name: The Veiled Water-Gate crew (6)
npcs.role: boatmen & gate-keepers who bring clients in unseen
npcs.note: See every veiled face in Starfall and will die before matching one to a name — because the House has made very sure they understand the alternative.

npcs.name: The Nightside Bunks (30) — boat-gang leader Ghurr
npcs.role: capstan-labour, client-boat polers, the House's heavier errands
npcs.note: The House's hands; move the secrets, least allowed to keep their own. Part of the unnamed 778, and the ones the Rebellion will one day remember.

npcs.name: Magistra Vessa Ilmyra
npcs.role: Head of House Ilmyra; Keeper of the Tides of the Song
npcs.note: Slow, tidal, patient; measures her House's fortunes in cycles no other House has the temperament to wait out. Signs the city's lock-calendar and moon-festivals into law.

npcs.name: First Gauger Pallun Ree
npcs.role: senior observer of the tideglass and the moons
npcs.note: Reads the water-column at moonrise and moonset; has not slept a whole night through in two centuries and considers this normal.

npcs.name: the junior gaugers (4)
npcs.role: live-in gauging clerks
npcs.note: Reduce the tide-readings and copy the lock-tables; dream in rising and falling numbers.

npcs.name: the Ilmyra family (5)
npcs.role: House family

npcs.name: the Seat household staff (12)
npcs.role: cook, pool-keeper, porters, maids
npcs.note: Includes the pool-keeper whose whole post is filling and draining the moon-court to the calendar.

npcs.name: Tide-Lunist Orrin Sael
npcs.role: moon-and-tide theorist; argues the moons and the Song's tide are one motion
npcs.note: Household of 6. A theory-thread toward the Academy's Song-work — the lock-cycle as unnoticed liturgy.

npcs.name: Lock-Warden Dov Marrenh
npcs.role: commoner-born officer who times the Lock-Flight and every canal sluice
npcs.note: Household of 6. The hand on the city's whole water economy; never asked to dine at the Seat. Runs it by a leaking brass model he trusts over any Magister.

npcs.name: Retired barge-mistress Halvenna Oon
npcs.role: wealthy new-money tenant of a sightline villa given over to a private tidal pool
npcs.note: Household of 5. Made a fortune on the barges and spends her villa's sightline on watching her own small tide turn — a deliberate affront to the upper terrace's values.

npcs.name: Master lockwright Bruska Fenn + household (15)
npcs.role: runs the Lockwrights' Hall; builds and maintains every lock-gate in the city
npcs.note: Trusted with the city's actual weight of water; a failed gate empties one terrace into the next.

npcs.name: Chief gauger Present Ollav-Ree + house (10)
npcs.role: computes the tide-tables and lock-timings; runs the House press
npcs.note: Every barge that ever climbed to Starfall did it by a page struck here. 'Present' is a Noctari name, a gauger's joke about always being on time.

npcs.name: Lesser Watermen's Row (24) — sluice-tender Merrow
npcs.role: sluice-tenders, gaugers' clerks, paddle-boys, canal-sweeps
npcs.note: Sightless service class; Merrow tells the tide's height by the sound the paddles make.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Coll Marsh + house (5)
npcs.role: keeps The Drowned Moon
npcs.note: Serves on through the spring floods with everyone's feet on the bench-rails; knows the wet cellar hatch down to the flight.

npcs.name: The Barge-Basin & Chandlery (33) — dealer Pesh, toll-clerk Ammary
npcs.role: ship's-chandlers, victuallers, toll-clerks
npcs.note: The one place the world-below arrives in the open on the water; Ammary has memorised every barge-master's face.

npcs.name: Moon-keeper Senna + apprentice
npcs.role: keeps the Shrine of the Three Moons
npcs.note: Tends three silver bowls of star-water to track the moons; the bowls are a running ledger of the bargefolk's fear and gratitude.

npcs.name: Basinside dwellings (50) — boatwright Oram, pilot-widow Cael
npcs.role: bargefolk families, boatwrights, netmakers, lightermen
npcs.note: Read the day by the height of the water at the door. Cael guides new barge-masters up the flight for a coin and a story.

npcs.name: Tide-Hall keeper Haldis + attendants (6)
npcs.role: keeps the Tide-Hall; controls the breathing pool's fill and drain
npcs.note: Treats the sluice-machinery as holy and keeps it behind a screen — devout about a thing the crew in IL-X02 works with bare hands.

npcs.name: Water-customs officer Trennt + 2 clerks
npcs.role: weighs and tallies everything that comes up the flight by water
npcs.note: Day post; the back-door twin of the Vael'Suran and Serenthil front gates — but his door faces the water, and the water comes from below.

npcs.name: The Lock-Flight under-clerk & signal-crew (worked by IL-X03)
npcs.role: keep the true cargo-count and signal the chambers; bunk in the Lock-Gangs' Hall
npcs.note: Counted among the Lock-Gangs (IL-X03). The under-clerk keeps the Other Map's tally at the head of the flight.

npcs.name: The Conduit-and-Sluice Crew (6)
npcs.role: keep the Song-conduits and set the sluices that time the Tide-Hall and the flight
npcs.note: They, not the moon, decide when the great pool breathes.

npcs.name: The Gate-Wrights (24) — old gate-wright Dross
npcs.role: keep the Lock-Flight's great gates swelled, sealed and true
npcs.note: Keep a Petrocore shrine and a carving of the whole flight; boast of climbs made with no cargo lost.

npcs.name: The Lock-Haulers (28)
npcs.role: walk the paddle-capstans that lift the barges chamber by chamber
npcs.note: The muscle of the flight; the wet-room takes one of them most seasons. Part of the unnamed 778.

npcs.name: The Bargefolk of the flight (~64)
npcs.role: road-people of the water; bring cargo up the flight and shelter between climbs
npcs.note: A distinct outsider population with their own tongue and gods, families kept aboard; needed for everything they carry, granted nothing but the undershelter. The most foreign faces in Starfall, living under its most beautiful pool.

npcs.name: Canteen-keeper Mother Ilse + 3
npcs.role: keeps the Slackwater Canteen
npcs.note: Reads the tide by the draught under the door; rings no bell. Knows Mother Vesh (VS-X05) and Old Sable (SR-X05) by their runners — the three under-canteen keepers are the real government of the dark.

npcs.name: Lockmaster Vel
npcs.role: the seam of Ilmyra's under-city; reconciles the flight's cargo-count and drowned-count
npcs.note: The one soul who both walks the Tide-Hall's colonnade and knows the last hauler the flight killed. Keeps the honest count in charcoal and the House's in ink. Twin to Foreman Adric (VS-X06) and Foreman Quill (SR-X06).

npcs.name: Magister Vaelith Corvane
npcs.role: Head of House Corvane; Keeper of the Ledger of Absence
npcs.note: The oldest and least-visited House head on the rim; speaks rarely and is never wrong about what is not there. The Conclave fears her opinions and asks for them anyway.

npcs.name: First Watcher Oel-Vane
npcs.role: senior observer of the deep field, the Aperture Chamber
npcs.note: Has not seen the sun's side of the caldera in a century; navigates the tower blind and prefers it.

npcs.name: the void-computers (5)
npcs.role: live-in clerks who record the night's absences
npcs.note: Reduce columns of nothing; the steadiest, strangest young scholars in the House.

npcs.name: the Corvane near family (3)
npcs.role: House family
npcs.note: Few, quiet; the House does not breed freely.

npcs.name: the Seat household staff (12)
npcs.role: cook, porters, lamp-tender, maids
npcs.note: Paid above the rim's rate; Corvane servants are hard to keep and know it.

npcs.name: Magistra Ysoreth of the Long Look
npcs.role: scholar of a single unchanging patch of deep field
npcs.note: 240 years watching one hand's-breadth of dark for a change that has not come; the House's whole ethos in one obsessive, courteous person.

npcs.name: Ysoreth's household (4)
npcs.role: companion and two grown students

npcs.name: Magister Oren Corvane
npcs.role: keeper of the Warded Study; guardian of the restricted void-theory
npcs.note: Household of 4. Signs no register when the Academy's void-scholars visit by night. The intellectual seed of the Nullstone lives on his shelves, chained.

npcs.name: Caretaker Nel
npcs.role: keeps the Vacant Villa exactly as its vanished scholar left it
npcs.note: Paid to keep the room, and paid more not to say why. Knows what the open chart is pointed at.

npcs.name: Master-scribe Corriden
npcs.role: warden of the Hall of Negative Results
npcs.note: Trains the most reliable and least deceivable scribes in the city.

npcs.name: the ledger-scribes (14)
npcs.role: copy and cross-check the ledgers of absence; lodge in the hall
npcs.note: The quietest sleepers in Starfall.

npcs.name: Master mirror-wright Dela Vess + household (10)
npcs.role: grinds black speculum mirrors and void-glass
npcs.note: Can figure a mirror so dark it shows the room behind your head. Feared a little, courted much.

npcs.name: Lesser Scholars' Row (20) — the copyist Wren
npcs.role: reducers and copyists; sightless service class
npcs.note: Wren has begun, against every rule, to hope the dark she records will answer. A side-character with a small, dangerous faith.

npcs.name: Halb Oren + house (6)
npcs.role: innkeeper of the Last Lamp
npcs.note: Swears he will never let the one lamp go out. Knows about the cellar hatch and says nothing.

npcs.name: The Mourning Market (28)
npcs.role: sellers of black-glass, hooded lamps, mourning-silk, grave-silver
npcs.note: Named: silversmith Made (grave-tokens), lamp-hooder Sulen. Quietly the richest market in Starfall.

npcs.name: Keeper Onn + two acolytes
npcs.role: keeper of the Deep Shrine of Umbrion
npcs.note: Tends the god the whole wedge understands best; feeds the ones who cannot yet come out of the dark.

npcs.name: Nightside dwellings (44) — the widow Oll
npcs.role: artisans, lamp-hooders, mirror-wrights' families, canal-hands
npcs.note: Includes the customs officer's household. Oll reads the ledger of absence for pleasure. Neighbours who know each other's silences.

npcs.name: Old Pell + household (4)
npcs.role: retired lamp-hooder; self-taught amateur watcher of the deep field
npcs.note: Keeps a private ledger of a patch no scholar bothers with; two magisters quietly check his numbers. Proof the obsession is contagious.

npcs.name: Customs officer Sael + clerk
npcs.role: weighs the goods that come up from below; keeps an unofficial watch over the water's edge
npcs.note: Household counted at CV-K04. Keeps a lantern for the shore, not the desk — someone should be near when a person stands too long at the Mirror.

npcs.name: Lock-master Grael
npcs.role: runs the Nightbarge Lock
npcs.note: Works the stillest water in the city fast and speaks little. Counted within the Warren.

npcs.name: Conduit-wrights (crew of 6)
npcs.role: keep the Song singing up to the wedge's dim star-lamps
npcs.note: Report, off the record, that the Song here runs a shade fainter each year. Measured, not believed.

npcs.name: Warren-elder Bruk
npcs.role: elder of the Deep-Wrights' Warren
npcs.note: Says the Corvane stone 'keeps its own counsel'; keeps the glow-stone brighter than any other wedge's.

npcs.name: The Deep-Wrights (43)
npcs.role: cut and hold up the Corvane under-terraces
npcs.note: Like this posting least of all the wedges; crowd the light. Keep a Petrocore shrine that is never left unlit.

npcs.name: The Silent Bunks (46) — the elder Vosk
npcs.role: walk the Nightbarge capstans; carry what the barges bring
npcs.note: Vosk has taught the whole hall a hand-language, because sound carries wrong this deep. Part of the unnamed 778.

npcs.name: Mama Dren + 5
npcs.role: canteen-keeper of the Underhush
npcs.note: Fights the wedge's silence with soup and noise on purpose; keeps three bright lamps. Knows the other under-canteens by their runners.

npcs.name: Foreman Ist
npcs.role: the seam of Corvane's under-city; reconciles the shift-count to the House
npcs.note: The only overseer who has sat a night in the Void Chamber; the crews trust and fear him for it. Keeps the honest count in charcoal, the House's in ink.

npcs.name: The Void Chamber initiates & keeper (12)
npcs.role: sit the Sphere and tend those inside it
npcs.note: Keeper Sael-Dun and eleven initiates who live at the chamber's mouth. The room that made Elorin Voidweaver; a straight line from this seat to the Nullstone.

npcs.name: The Barge-Hands (42) — the hauler Renk
npcs.role: move cargo along the under-gallery from lock to hoist
npcs.note: The muscle behind the pretty still canal; unnamed by the rim. Renk is teaching himself the deep-wrights' letters. Part of the unnamed 778.

npcs.name: Anneth Correa, the Unwarden
npcs.role: informal elder of the dead House's wedge; keeps the one open ledger of favours
npcs.note: Not a magister and refuses to be called one. Came here fled from something she does not discuss and stayed to hold the loose place together. Governs by listening and by not quite deciding. The head of a wedge that has no head.

npcs.name: the Hollow Seat commons (27)
npcs.role: squatter-families housed in the abandoned manor; the wedge's loose council
npcs.note: Every race under one dead House's roof, partitioned by hung cloth. Grow vegetables in the observing court.

npcs.name: the Roofless Row squatters (14)
npcs.role: occupants of the ruined sightline villas
npcs.note: Live free under the best views in the city, and under tarps when it rains. Named: the tinker Osk, who chose a roofless room for the stars.

npcs.name: Sennox the Last
npcs.role: the dead House's final servant; keeper of its name and its silence
npcs.note: Very old even for a Noctari. Kept the House's last villa exactly as it was for three centuries; remembers the name and has promised, once, to never say it — the only promise he ever kept. Knows why the House died. Will not tell. Do not resolve it.

npcs.name: the Cloth Terrace (16) — the weaver Illa Mott
npcs.role: families in the subdivided villas; sightlines held in common
npcs.note: Illa hangs the washing between the old columns and calls the shared view 'everyone's window.'

npcs.name: Cord Vellamy, the Head Mender + yard (16)
npcs.role: self-appointed head of the Menders' Yard; fixes what the guilds won't
npcs.note: Chartered themselves when no House would. The city's cheapest repairs and its worst-kept secret; the other Houses send work through cut-outs.

npcs.name: Teacher Meret + pupils (10)
npcs.role: runs the Free School; teaches letters, numbers and the stars to anyone
npcs.note: A human who was refused the Academy and teaches its knowledge for free below it. Boards the pupils with nowhere else. The most subversive person in Starfall and the gentlest.

npcs.name: the Unnumbered Row (32)
npcs.role: the fled, the discreetly poor, the between-things; on no rent-roll
npcs.note: Came to the dead wedge to be un-measured. Nobody asks the next door's name unless it is offered. Some are hiding; most are simply tired of being counted.

npcs.name: Bram Nolt + house (5)
npcs.role: keeps the Blind Lamp taphouse
npcs.note: Burns illegal tallow because the Song won't come here; lets rooms by the night, no name asked. Warmer than any legal inn.

npcs.name: the Unmarket traders (30) — the barter-clerk Sable-of-no-House
npcs.role: barrow-traders and barterers; keep no hours and pay no stall-fee
npcs.note: Debts chalked and rubbed out on trust. The un-timed market of the un-timed House.

npcs.name: the Nameless Keeper + a companion
npcs.role: tends the Empty Niche; a shrine to the unnamed and the erased
npcs.note: Was themselves struck from a ledger long ago and never restored, and so keeps the shrine to erasure. Asks no one why they kneel.

npcs.name: the Mingle (52)
npcs.race: Noctari, human, Terran, orc, and several of no single race
npcs.role: the mixed-race warren of the canal quarter
npcs.note: The only above-ground place in Starfall where every race keeps house side by side as a matter of course. The rule against it lapsed with the House and no one rebuilt it. Includes the city's few openly mixed-race children.

npcs.name: the wash-women of the Common Wash (8) — Gerta Voss
npcs.role: keep the wash-house and, incidentally, mind the wedge's sick and newborn
npcs.note: Keep the salvaged boiler alive by collective effort; do the work no institution here exists to do. Gerta has delivered half the Mingle's children.

npcs.name: the Gate-Watchers (2) — old Pell
npcs.role: volunteer watch at the untended customs post
npcs.note: Watch not for goods coming up but for the rich coming down the stair; warn the wedge who is descending. The one gate in Starfall aimed at the over-city.

npcs.name: the Failing-Gallery crew (6) — the tuner Orin Deep
npcs.role: keep the last few Song-conduits singing as the rest go dark
npcs.note: Sleep beside their failing charge; sell a little of the last light to the Menders. The reason the Blind Lamp is blind is that this crew is losing.

npcs.name: the Undercroft dwellers (40) — the lock-caller Mudge
npcs.role: crew the Slack Lock and live below by choice, not confinement
npcs.note: Work the lock cooperatively for a share of cargo; come and go up the Open Stair as they please. Segregation's architecture, emptied of its cruelty.

npcs.name: the Open Table keeper Bess + 3
npcs.role: keeps the under-canteen at the foot of the Open Stair
npcs.note: Feeds over and under at one table — the only integrated board in the city. Knows Mother Vesh (VS-X05) and Old Sable (SR-X05) by their runners, and pities their walled rooms.

npcs.name: the volunteer tally-keeper, young Wrenn
npcs.role: keeps the one open ledger at the abandoned foreman's post, unpaid and undemanded
npcs.note: Keeps an honest count no one above requires — proof, sitting in the dark, that the labour organizes itself and works without an overseer. Would be a foreman's clerk in any other wedge; here, just a person who counts to be useful.

npcs.name: the fisher-folk of the Drowned Terrace (8) — the punt-woman Calla
npcs.role: fish and live on the flooded under-level the pumps stopped draining
npcs.note: Netting the pale blind things that breed in the star-water; punting children over the drowned doorways. Live beneath even the Other Map. Calla will not say where the deepest drowned doors lead, and has stopped going to find out.

npcs.name: Magister Corvenn Duskmere
npcs.role: Head of House Duskmere; Warden of the Horizon
npcs.note: Watches the settings; keeps the outward-facing seat and the Returns lamp. Prouder of who his House has sent out into the world than of any sightline — the one head who thinks the city is a place you leave.

npcs.name: First Watcher Ysolt Vane
npcs.role: senior observer of first-and-last light
npcs.note: Names the auspicious hours travellers pay to set out on; privately believes no hour is auspicious and every departure a small death.

npcs.name: the watchers & beacon-keepers (6)
npcs.role: live-in observers and beacon-tenders
npcs.note: Keep the landward lamp and the shutter-code through every watch of the night.

npcs.name: the resident Duskmere family (5)
npcs.role: House family currently at home
npcs.note: The half of the family not on the road; they keep the Returns lamp for the other half.

npcs.name: the Seat household staff (10)
npcs.role: cook, map-keeper, lamp-tender, porters, maids

npcs.name: Warden Hesk Ollun + household (6)
npcs.role: Warden of the Stair; commoner-born officer who holds the gate and the descent
npcs.note: Decides who enters Starfall at all — a heavier hand than any House head, and resented for it. Household of 6 incl. a ward taken off the stair as a child.

npcs.name: Gate-serjeant Ollun-Rekk + guard company (12)
npcs.role: commands the resident gate-guard; keeps the gate-book
npcs.note: Kin to both the Warden and the gatewrights; the Rekks are the gate. The only standing armed body in a city that pretends it needs none.

npcs.name: Caravan-master Tovek Sarn + household (5)
npcs.role: retired trade-master; new money on the rim
npcs.note: Sixty years up and down the stair; bought a sightline the old blood says he has no right to, and still owns half the mule-lines. An affront and a fact.

npcs.name: Caretaker Nell + lodgers (4)
npcs.role: keeps the Empty House for a family a decade away
npcs.note: Dusts an unused sightline she is not permitted to sit at; quietly rents its spare rooms to three she does not report.

npcs.name: Guild-warden Ilsa Wend + pilots (13)
npcs.role: warden of the Wayfarers' Hall; road-cartographer
npcs.note: Draws the outward maps the Plate refuses; her stair-pilots' word is worth a House seal in the world below.

npcs.name: Master gatewright Dorn Rekk + household (9)
npcs.role: holds the gate-contract; makes and mends the gate-iron
npcs.note: Guards his winch-designs like a House guards a sightline. Kin to the gate-serjeant.

npcs.name: Doorkeepers' Row (22) — tallyman Vess
npcs.role: gate-clerks, toll-tallymen, stair-lamplighters, gate-runners
npcs.note: Vess has memorised every face up the stair in forty years and never written a name he was paid to lose. Sightless service to the threshold.

npcs.name: Innkeeper Wenna Sarr + house (5)
npcs.role: keeps The Last Lamp
npcs.note: Can tell from the door whether a stranger needs a farewell or a homecoming. Swears the cellar door to the Undergate is bricked up.

npcs.name: Caravanserai-keeper Old Mireth + house (44)
npcs.role: keeps the Caravanserai of the First Night
npcs.note: ~14 permanent staff + ~30 long-stay transients this season (never the same number twice). Runs the most cosmopolitan roof in a city that prides itself on knowing everyone; a quest and rumour hub.

npcs.name: The Arrival Market (24) — the changer Oshka, the letter-writer Pell
npcs.role: money-changers, outfitters, a physician, a letter-writer, second-hand dealers
npcs.note: Oshka fences what the Undergate brings up; Pell knows every secret in the wedge and sells none. Prices tuned to a tired stranger.

npcs.name: Gateside dwellings (37) — portress Grella
npcs.role: porters, stable-hands, gate-clerks' and changers' families
npcs.note: The settled folk of a wedge made of leavers. Grella has carried loads up the stair since she was nine and will not speak of what she has seen come down it.

npcs.name: Keeper Onwe
npcs.role: keeper of the Threshold Shrine
npcs.note: Came up the stair once meaning to go back and never has; marks a tally-stone for every soul who prays to leave and does not return.

npcs.name: Customs officer Brae + 2 clerks
npcs.role: runs the gate-foot customs; tolls what the lock lifts from below
npcs.note: Day post (household counted at DK-K04). Between her post and the gatehouse, in theory nothing enters uncounted — the wedge's central irony.

npcs.name: Lock-master Braff
npcs.role: runs the Duskmere Lock
npcs.note: The under-clerk beneath him keeps the charcoal tally; the gap between it and the gate-book above is where the wedge's real wealth hides.

npcs.name: Conduit crew (6)
npcs.role: keep the Song singing up to the star-lamps and the beacon
npcs.note: Climb in the dark to feed the landward beacon, the hungriest lamp in the city — a light that faces away from them.

npcs.name: The Stair-Gangs (50) — stair-elder Karsk
npcs.role: stair-porters and barge lift-gangs; the muscle of the threshold
npcs.note: ~28 porters + ~22 lift-gang. Karsk has climbed the equivalent of off the world and back many times over. On no gate-book, because the book counts arrivals and they never leave. Part of the unnamed 778.

npcs.name: The Stairwrights (42) — under-mother Tesk
npcs.role: cut, shore and repair the outer stair and the gate's roots
npcs.note: The most dangerous stone-work in Starfall, hanging over the cloud-sea on the outside of the world; lost fingers counted as rank. Kin to House Vael'Suran's deep-wrights.

npcs.name: Canteen-keeper Bem + 3
npcs.role: keeps the Waygate Canteen

npcs.name: Foreman Idris
npcs.role: the seam of Duskmere's under-city; manages the Undergate
npcs.note: Keeps three ledgers — one for the House, one that is true, one he burns. Decides what the Undergate is allowed to be; trusted by neither map. Prime quest-broker.

npcs.name: Magister Toll Serenthil
npcs.role: Head of House Serenthil; Keeper of the Meridian
npcs.note: Civic, dry, and quietly aware that his House's dignity rests on being useful rather than revered. Signs the city's time into law.

npcs.name: Strike-Master Venn Ostreth

npcs.name: the Tower ringers & watch (4)
npcs.role: live-in bell-ringers and clock-watchers

npcs.name: the Serenthil family (5)
npcs.role: House family + 2 boarded horology apprentices

npcs.name: the Seat household staff (11)
npcs.role: cook, clock-keeper, porters, maids

npcs.name: Venn Ostreth's household (5)
npcs.role: the Strike-Master's spouse & 3 children

npcs.name: Chief Horologist Marn Ilve

npcs.name: Master founder Hessa Drun + household (14)

npcs.name: Guild-warden Pel Corriden + hall (9)
npcs.role: clockmakers' guild; keeps the dividing engine's secret

npcs.name: Lesser Timekeepers' Row (22) — hour-caller Renn
npcs.role: hour-callers, dial-readers, water-tenders, rope-boys

npcs.name: Innkeeper Wenna Kob + house (5)
npcs.role: keeps The Ninth Bell

npcs.name: Water-warden Iss Vellun + works (12)

npcs.note: The human node between canal, cistern and Tower — all one water-driven clock.

npcs.name: Sera
npcs.role: structural enchantress on the Nullstone team; a sun-elf alone in the night-city
npcs.note: 'The outsider's outsider.' Lodges in the timekeepers' wedge because the bells keep a schedule she recognises; a forbidden sun-lamp lit only behind shutters. Mirrors Vara's garret across the Processional.

npcs.name: Watergate dwellings (40) — the widow Ferrun
npcs.role: rope-boys, water-tenders, dial-runners, canal-hands
npcs.note: Ferrun counts every bell since her husband fell from the belfry.

npcs.name: The Hour-Market (22) — the baker Doln
npcs.role: baker, dial-shop, chandler, rope-walk, cook-stall, scrivener, herbalist

npcs.name: The Conduit-and-Race Crew (6)

npcs.name: The Cistern-Gangs (16)
npcs.role: walk the pumps; haul; the muscle of the water-system

design_notes.tallies_are_computed: Population per wedge and per district is summed from each structure's resident_count by the generators — never hand-maintained here, so it cannot drift.
design_notes.over_under_balance: In a finished wedge the Under-Terraces should hold roughly as many souls as the visible quarter above — and appear on no official map. That imbalance in plain sight is the theme.
design_notes.distinct_wedges: Wedges must not read as clones. Vael'Suran = the eye, pride, protected sightlines, a closed bloodline. Serenthil = the ear, the hour, civic utility, rented rooms, a mixed under-city. Each further House should get its own social texture from its celestial domain.

institutions.note: The Academy of Astral Harmony — the institution at dead centre, on the island in the Mirror (district D-ACADEMY, r 0-75, reached by the one railless causeway). Not a House wedge: the nine Houses send their best here and it answers to none of them. This is where Elorin Voidweaver works and lodges through her Academy years, where the Nullstone team assembles, and where the safeguard is designed. Structures follow docs/Zone_Atlas.md Z-03/04/05 and the greybox island in godot/threed/StarfallCity3D.gd (_build_island). Sera, Vara and Durak WORK here but are housed in the city (SR-K03, VS-K04, VS-X03) — listed there, not here.
